That should provide some perspective for all their preseason games, right, Milhouse?. “Say […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent (17) passes the ball against the Cleveland Browns during the first half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On the FOX 32 pregame show, host Cassie Carlson brought up a good point: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson has recycled the same preseason game plan that he’s used going back to when he first started calling plays for the Lions. That should provide some perspective for all their preseason games, right, Milhouse?. “Say the line!” We’re talking about practice! The Bears beat the Cleveland Browns 34 to 10 after falling behind 10-0 in the first half. Chicago scored 34 unanswered and then stopped the Browns in the red zone to seal the game. Tyson Bagent had some nice moments for the Bears in the first half, throwing to Kaden Davis (4 receptions, 88 yards) and Maurice Alexander (3 receptions for 42 yards and a TD), but he also threw a pick and had a couple of floaters. All in all, it was a fine performance by a fine QB2, going 13-for-22 (59.1%), 169 passing yards, 1 touchdown, 1 interception, and a 79.5 passer rating. Reserve running back Salvon Ahmed showed some nice vision and speed on a 49-yard TD catch off a Case Keenum screen. Keenum put up a perfect 158.3 passer rating on his 10 passing attempts. Regarding the left tackle competition, neither Kiran Amegadjie nor Jedrick Wills Jr. stood out, so Braxton Jones, who should be back next week, was today’s winner. Jamree Kromah, who is trying to make his first 53-man roster as a backup defensive end, had a sack, forced fumble, and fumble recovery trifecta on Browns starting QB Deshaun Watson. Overall, he had 6 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, and 2 sacks. James Lynch got reps at both defensive tackle and end, showing some versatility. Rookie sixth-round pick Jordan van den Berg played a lot at defensive tackle, but didn’t make a big impact with just 1 tackle and a QB hit. However, I thought he played well, although on the initial watch I’d like to see him keep his head up and stay on his feet more often. Fellow rookie DT Jayden Loving had a nice sequence in the second half where he got doubled but got his hand up to knock the pass down on one play; then on the next play he got a good push up the middle to pressure Shedeur Sanders, who threw a pick to Beanie Bishop Jr. Bishop got a second interception later in the game. Mongo Peanut: Devin Bush. I think his speed is going to be a massive part of the Bears’ improvement, and not enough people are talking about it. I’m really excited to see that speed on display. title: ESPN projects Bengals players’ Hall of Fame chances
summary: The Bengals have not had much luck getting players into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the past, with only two members of the team in it. They still have a couple of players with potential to make it in and have gotten close in the past with Willie Anderson and Ken Anderson. Now, […]
full_text: The Bengals have not had much luck getting players into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the past, with only two members of the team in it. They still have a couple of players with potential to make it in and have gotten close in the past with Willie Anderson and Ken Anderson. Now, the question becomes what they can do to increase the chances of their current players. In a new article, ESPN discussed the potential Hall of Fame players on each team , and they only mention one Bengal on the right path. Keep it up: WR Ja’Marr Chase Chase has been every bit as good as Justin Jefferson, his former teammate at LSU. But as Chase entered the NFL 12 months after Jefferson, his résumé is one year shorter. The 2021 No. 5 pick has started his career with five straight Pro Bowls and an Offensive Rookie of the Year award, and he has been a first-team All-Pro each of the past two seasons. He’s still only 26, and it would be no surprise if Chase had already clinched his spot in Canton before turning 30. Work to do: QB Joe Burrow, WR Tee Higgins, DT Dexter Lawrence II Burrow also has a Hall of Fame case based on his level of play, but injuries are the concern here. He has now missed significant portions of three different seasons (2020, 2023 and 2025), a significant amount for a player who has been in the league for only six years. The Bengals also haven’t made the playoffs since 2022, and while that shouldn’t impact Burrow given that he has already made it to a Super Bowl, more playoff success wouldn’t hurt. While the Bengals are currently projected to have only one Hall of Famer at their current pace, if they can add more team success with a Super Bowl win or two, that should raise the profile of everyone on the team. The work to do seems a bit pessimistic, as Burrow and Lawrence have looked like some of the best players at their positions when healthy. A solid year could easily have both back on the Hall of Fame trajectory, and the Bengals could be looking at doubling their Hall of Fame members.

title: 9 takeaways from Browns vs Bears, including on Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders
summary: The Cleveland Browns and Chicago Bears faced off in their first preseason game of the 2026 season, with the home team sitting many key players while the visitors were trying to evaluate some key players. full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 27: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns signals to teammates during the first half of a preseason game against the Chicago Bears at FirstEnergy Stadium on August 27, 2022 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns and Chicago Bears faced off in their first preseason game of the 2026 season, with the home team sitting many key players while the visitors were trying to evaluate some key players. The final score was far from the most important thing for the Browns, but DBNers spent the game chatting through all the details of the game and noticing a lot of key things . Final score: 34-10 Bears with the victory . A few key takeaways from Cleveland’s first preseason game under HC Todd Monken: Deshaun Watson crisp, then not; far from perfect The game against the Bears gave Watson a chance to clearly establish himself as the QB leader heading into the Buffalo Bills’ joint practices. To start the game, it looked like that was very possible as Watson looked comfortable in the pocket, made some good throws across the middle, and his only incompletion was a drop by TE Harold Fannin Jr. Then as things sped up, Watson looked more uncomfortable, and the offense stopped producing. The QB was not the only problem (see below), but the veteran left the door wide-open for Shedeur Sanders to run through next week. On 4th down, Watson failed to get the ball out quickly, leading to a fumble and turnover (line seemed to be quick setting, expecting a quick throw): Jamree Kromah forces and recovers the fumble! CLEvsCHI on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4N2OKC5Yut — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 A breakdown of the data: Deshaun Watson in the first half vs. the Bears: 18 dropbacks 11/15 (73.3% completion rate) 129 passing yards (4 rushing yards) 98.2 passer rating Sacked once (one lost fumble) 2.75s avg. time to throw 4.4 air yards per attempt pic.twitter.com/GTeKCGzUCa — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 15, 2026 OLine struggles, especially in run blocking It was not surprising to see the new Cleveland OLine looking better than last year; almost anything would be, but it wasn’t pretty as a whole. Rookie Spencer Fano , who has had a very good training camp, was left in much longer than the rest of the starters and didn’t look great overall. Rushing up the middle was almost non-existent, and the second string looked outmatched by the second and third stringers from Chicago. The run game, as a whole, just did not look good. Pass protection was okay at times, but the line lacks power for sure. Rookie WRs, especially KC Concepcion, look good Monken looks like he plans to make Concepcion his Zay Flowers , with the ball in his hands in as many ways and times as possible. Concepcion caught three passes, including a pop pass, and took an end-around for a touchdown. His speed is a real threat and Monken’s use of rub routes will open up things for his quickness as well. Denzel Boston had just one reception, but his size-and-speed combo fits perfectly along with Concepcion. Chris Edmunds struggles; Michael Coats Jr. does not A lot of questions in the Browns defensive backfield, including whether they will keep four or five safeties and the cornerback depth chart after Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell , and Myles Harden . The more experienced Edmunds did not help his cause in the safety room, but UDFA cornerback Coats did. Not only did Coats have an interception, but he had a nice pass breakup as well: Michael Coats Jr. with a well-executed PBU. Recovers to the outside shoulder, stays patient, and rips through the catch-point. pic.twitter.com/uWMwdnktqQ — Browns Film Breakdown (@BrownsFilmBDN) August 15, 2026 Coats did leave the game with an ankle injury in the second half, something to watch. Todd Monken aggressive on 4th down For fans who were hoping that Kevin Stefanski’s penchant for going for it on 4th down had left with him will likely be disappointed. As it is almost universally around the league, Monken seems likely to go for it regularly. Preseason isn’t always indicative with 4th down attempts, but Monken didn’t “take the points” or “punt it away and play defense.” Where is the pass rush? Given the Browns bringing in a number of old pass rushers , it seems the team is not happy with their depth at the defensive end position. Except for a few snaps against former Cleveland OT Jedrick Wills , the Browns pass rush was mostly toothless in the game. Probably not a big deal, with vanilla plans, but something to watch with DE Myles Garrett traded away. Special teams no longer ugly A big return from Concepcion was great, but overall not having terrible plays on special teams, which normally includes a bunch of flags, was nice. Defense got gashed, concerning for now As a whole, the defense wasn’t terrible, but there were quite a few gash plays where defenders were out of position or overpursuing. Given the Garrett departure and replacing Jim Schwartz with Mike Rutenberg, Cleveland fans have a right to be concerned that the unit that carried the squad for a couple of years is going to take a step back. Far from certain, but for now a concern. Shedeur Sanders with the good and bad Playing against a lot of backups, Sanders needed to not look bad, and he didn’t to start the second half; then, similar to Watson but against more backups, things got worse. A couple of good throws on his first drive, including slightly drifting in the pocket to make this throw: deep shot through pressure 😮‍💨 #CLEvsCHI on News 5 and NFL Network pic.twitter.com/QzfpBciGE0 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 15, 2026 While incomplete, the ball placement to Gage Larvadain on the sideline was nice in the Cover-2 hole near the end of the third quarter. Overall, everything felt slow with Sanders, including time in the huddle. Sanders’ overthrow, by about five yards, led to an interception. Looks like a terrible throw, but always a chance that the receiver ( Malachi Corley ) ran the wrong depth, or a different depth than Sanders expected. The dots seem to indicate that it was an overthrow: Yep, it was schemed up well. Just overthrew it. https://t.co/JP99uESSQH pic.twitter.com/D4spM9wkFu — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 15, 2026 Dillon Gabriel took over after the interception. What were your takeaways from the Browns preseason game versus the Bears? Join the conversation! full_text: Young fans gather around Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson as they try for autographs after Browns training camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus of the Cleveland Browns in Berea, Ohio on June 9, 2026. on July, 31, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Cleveland Browns fans will get their first taste of Todd Monken as the team’s head coach today when his team battles the Chicago Bears in their first preseason game. The most important thing people will be paying attention to this preseason is how the quarterback competition plays out. Deshaun Watson will get the start this week, with Shedeur Sanders entering in the third quarter. That scenario will be flipped next week against the Buffalo Bills. Watson is expected to play the entire first half today, as Monken wants to give equal looks at both quarterbacks in competition, with the hopes of getting them a two-minute drive as well. Both quarterbacks have been connecting on the long ball better in practice lately, with KC Concepcion , Denzel Boston , and Isaiah Bond all shining in particular. We’re not sure exactly how long the other starters will play, but Monken had indicated that the first-unit (other than quarterback) would see about one series. Since both quarterbacks have been getting experience with the first- and second-team offenses in practice, chemistry and rhythm issues should be less of a factor. This season, we’re going to be having one game thread for the entire game, so this will be your home to discuss the game for all four quarters! VS. title: Browns offense might require patience this year, and that is okay
summary: People often express patience when it comes to certain things, but struggle when they have to experience it. It’s not uncommon to have to wait for certain things, whether it’s a new job or waiting to buy something that you have wanted to buy. Having patience is an underrated skill. It might take a while […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken takes notes during team OTAs at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus of the Cleveland Browns in Berea, Ohio on June 2, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co People often express patience when it comes to certain things, but struggle when they have to experience it. It’s not uncommon to have to wait for certain things, whether it’s a new job or waiting to buy something that you have wanted to buy. Having patience is an underrated skill. It might take a while to get the object you want, but it will be worth the wait once the opportunity is right. The Cleveland Browns are entering Year 2 of a rebuild. Rebuilds take time, but eventually it pays off when/if everything falls into place. From the offensive side, the Browns are rebuilding on that side of the ball, including a new offensive scheme, system, and voice. Young, exciting pieces , but with uncertainty at the quarterback position. Offensively, Cleveland has been a below-average unit for the past two seasons but most of the fanbase believes the offense will be better under new head coach Todd Monken. The new head coach, who has facilitated top-tier offenses during his tenure with the Baltimore Ravens and during his time for the Georgia Bulldogs football team , has a good understanding of how to build a top offense. For those expecting instant results from this offense immediately, don’t. As a whole, the entire fanbase has been frustrated with the Browns offense for the past two seasons but at least the offense this year has talent which is something the unit hasn’t had recently. Despite the influx of talent, learning a new offense takes time. It’s not uncommon for a new offense to have inconsistent days. It takes time for a unit to gel collectively because it’s a ton of moving parts. The quarterback competition will be decided eventually, the offensive line will gain chemistry with more reps, and the skill position groups will get better with every rep. The offense will look rough to start the season, but the unit will improve gradually over time as everyone will get acclimated to the scheme. It might seem like a hard ask for this fanbase to endure, but it’s necessary that patience is necessary for this season’s offense. How patient do you think you can be with the Browns offense this year? When do you expect everything to “click” under Monken? Join the conversation! title: Browns 2026 predictions: Rushing yards for Quinshon Judkins
summary: Quinshon Judkins is entering his second season with the Cleveland Browns and has an opportunity to have a really big season. After showing plenty of promise during his rookie season, he now has an opportunity to take another step forward with a year of experience under his belt. Considering the talent around him on the […]
full_text: Quinshon Judkins is entering his second season with the Cleveland Browns and has an opportunity to have a really big season. After showing plenty of promise during his rookie season , he now has an opportunity to take another step forward with a year of experience under his belt. Considering the talent around him on the Browns’ offense, along with the uncertainty at quarterback and the offensive line, what are realistic expectations for Judkins’ production this season? As a rookie, he totaled 827 rushing yards and seven touchdowns while adding 26 receptions for 171 receiving yards. There is no reason that his production shouldn’t be even greater in 2026. There are some recent additions to the offensive line, including Spencer Fano , Austin Barber , Tytus Howard , Zion Johnson , and Elgton Jenkins . This group already has more depth and young talent than the 2025 group, which should open up opportunities for Judkins. It would be reasonable to expect Judkins to surpass 1,000 rushing yards this season. If the offensive line can open up some running lanes for him, this level of production will be very possible. The passing game will most likely continue to struggle whether Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders is at quarterback, so Cleveland will need to rely on Judkins often to get things going. title: If Shedeur Sanders loses Browns QB competition, a trade could be possible
summary: With the 2026 preseason beginning on Saturday for the Cleveland Browns, the team is still trying to figure out their current quarterback situation. Shedeur Sanders, who is in his second year with the Browns, is trying to take the starting job from veteran Deshaun Watson. However, Sanders is running into some form of adversity whilst […]
full_text: Shedeur Sanders hands off to Raheim Sanders at the Browns OTA in Berea on May 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co With the 2026 preseason beginning on Saturday for the Cleveland Browns, the team is still trying to figure out their current quarterback situation. Shedeur Sanders, who is in his second year with the Browns, is trying to take the starting job from veteran Deshaun Watson. However, Sanders is running into some form of adversity whilst trying to earn the starting job, which may be one reason Watson is starting against the Chicago Bears in Week 1 of the preseason. Inconsistencies or lack of progress in crucial areas have changed the tides of the quarterback situation, and people are wondering if Cleveland could possibly trade Sanders if he doesn’t win the starting job. It’s not certain that the Browns would choose to explore this path, but it’s a situation that cannot be ruled out. It’s the NFL, and roster decisions like these are fluid. Most likely it would be SS for a defender on the bubble with another team where they have a lot of depth. A CB or DE particularly as of now — Jared Mueller (@JaredKMueller) August 14, 2026 As the current quarterback situation has gone on, Sanders has made strides, but he is still struggling in the things that are key when it comes to playing the quarterback position. The team has viewed Sanders as a “developmental quarterback” given some of the limitations coming out of the Colorado offense. Sanders has talent, but he is behind in the key aspects of playing the position, mostly in presnap and progressions. Considering his draft position, the team is not committed to Sanders by any means, but they are giving him an opportunity to prove he is the guy of the future. Considering how last season went for Sanders, he is already facing an uphill battle to start. Sanders could build his trade value if he plays well in the preseason. If he plays well, but not well enough to beat out Watson, the Browns will likely keep him and play him this season if Watson were to get hurt or get benched. Then again, if he doesn’t get the starting spot out of training camp but shows some flashes, Cleveland might just turn the page, getting something in return while preparing for the next would-be future of the franchise in the 2027 NFL draft.

CAAAAAMDEN BROOOOOOWN pic.twitter.com/44xjaS9O6n — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) August 16, 2026 The first score was obviously very impressive from an overall standpoint, but the second was particularly wow-worthy based on how he hauled in Joe Milton’s pass. title: Cowboys vs. Seahawks preseason recap: Dallas impressive in win to start season
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are 1-0 in the preseason for the first time in a long time. It was 2017 when Dallas last started a preseason undefeated, but it took a hard-fought game against the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday night to get there. Things began a bit rough, but ultimately the Cowboys offense and defense each […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Sam Howell (16) leads the team onto the field before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys are 1-0 in the preseason for the first time in a long time. It was 2017 when Dallas last started a preseason undefeated, but it took a hard-fought game against the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday night to get there. Things began a bit rough, but ultimately the Cowboys offense and defense each settled to put some things on tape that we are all going to enjoy even more after a night’s sleep. Camden Brown was easily the game’s MVP as he scored both touchdowns for the boys in blue (and silver). Jaydon Blue, James Houston, Michael Trigg, and others all had their moments as well. Below you will find our recap of the game as it happened. It is officially football season! First Quarter The Dallas Cowboys won the toss for their preseason opener… hopefully a sign of things to come. It was decided that they were defer so Christian Parker’s new-look defense was on the field to start. Unfortunately things did not exactly go well. Drew Lock marched the Seahawks down the field for a game-opening touchdown. It didn’t help that the Cowboys committed two costly penalties to help move things along, and it specifically didn’t help for Caelen Carson that he was the guilty party for both of them (pass interference and facemask). SEAHAWKS TOUCHDOWN (Drew Lock to Montorie Foster, 5 yards): COWBOYS 0, SEAHAWKS 7 Sam Howell got the start at quarterback, but nobody looked good on the first possession. Jaydon Blue kind of did, but it wasn’t enough to stop a three and out and punt. Thankfully the Cowboys then forced a three and out of their own. Christian Parker, ladies and gentlemen! The quarter ended with the Dallas offense moving the ball thanks to Jonathan Mingo (seriously) and Jaydon Blue. . @Jaydonblue23 moves the chains ⛓️ 📺: #DALvsSEA on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx89QL pic.twitter.com/fO8EkPeVVi — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 16, 2026 let's go @ogmingo1k 📺: #DALvsSEA on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/VAWEmzGTJ1 — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 16, 2026 Second Quarter Blue and Mingo kept up their contributions when the break was over, but it was not enough to carry things all the way into the endzone. A third down miscommunication between Sam Howell and Anthony Smith led to the Cowboys calling in Mr. Reliable for a three-pointer. COWBOYS FIELD GOAL (Brandon Aubrey, 29 yards): COWBOYS 3, SEAHAWKS 7 Jalen Milroe was in for Seattle at this point and as they started moving… Caelen Carson was called for another penalty. This time it was holding. Having three to your name before the second quarter is halfway over is never a good thing. Seattle got into field goal range before it was all said and done, but Jason Myers pushed it right. The Cowboys took over with about two minutes to go before the half. The Cowboys got themselves into striking distance… and boy did they strike. Sam Howell found Camden Brown for the first Dallas Cowboys touchdown of the year! CAMDEN BROWN!!!! pic.twitter.com/ayWtwHc2Y2 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) August 16, 2026 COWBOYS TOUCHDOWN (Sam Howell to Camden Brown, 39 yards): COWBOYS 10, SEAHAWKS 7 For an early moment it appeared as if Seattle was going to find a way to squeak some points out before the break… but then James Houston took over. THAT’S JAMES HOUSTON pic.twitter.com/L6Nf6uXxLq — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) August 16, 2026 Dallas went to the locker room with the lead. Third Quarter The second half marked the pass over from Sam Howell to Joe Milton, and things began rather well. Camden Brown, Michael Trigg, and Anthony Smith helped out from a pass-catching standpoint, but Milton also got on the move and showed out as an athlete. All told he looked really put-together. His passes were a thing of beauty. Dallas got down to a 3rd and 1 up against the goal line, and Brian Schottenheimer even called timeout right before it to make sure things worked out the right way. The Cowboys ran a quarterback sneak to move those chains. Right after they did… Camden Brown struck again. CAAAAAMDEN BROOOOOOWN pic.twitter.com/44xjaS9O6n — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) August 16, 2026 Seriously. How impressive is this? COWBOYS TOUCHDOWN (Joe Milton to Camden Brown, 2 yards): COWBOYS 17, SEAHAWKS 7 The defense was able to stand tall for their first second half opportunity, and they gave the ball back to Milton and Co. for another shot. Nothing happened and Dallas punted away and then saw a huge return to make things worse. Seattle got down near the goal line (ish) and was staring at a fourth and short that they decided to take into the fourth quarter. Fourth Quarter The Seahawks were unable to convert and the Cowboys took over. You always like to see that. With a 10-point lead at their back the Cowboys weren’t exactly aggressive, and after gaining just 19 yards they booted the ball back to the home team. The Seahawks were unable to do much yet again, and they punted the ball away… this was when disaster struck. Traeshon Holden tried to field it near the Cowboys’ endzone and unfortunately muffed the punt. Seattle recovered and thanks to penalty began on the Cowboys’ 5-yard line. The defense stood tall, though! Seriously! Isaiah Land got to Jalen Milroe when Seattle went for it on fourth down (it’s the preseason) and ultimately the Seahawks lost 10 yards on the possession. The Cowboys were able to grind things out to the end of the game, something that Brian Schottenheimer surely enjoyed. With that the Cowboys won their preseason opener for the first time since 2017 by a final score of 17-7. Onward!

title: Cowboys at Seahawks: 5 things to watch
summary: The long, grueling wait is officially over. It has been 223 days since the Dallas Cowboys last lined up and played a football game, but that streak ends today. The time has finally arrived as the team travels to the beautiful Pacific Northwest to square off against the Super Bowl Champion, Seattle Seahawks, for their […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys looks to pass against the New York Giants during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The long, grueling wait is officially over. It has been 223 days since the Dallas Cowboys last lined up and played a football game, but that streak ends today. The time has finally arrived as the team travels to the beautiful Pacific Northwest to square off against the Super Bowl Champion, Seattle Seahawks, for their first preseason game of the season. Training camp practices and inter-squad scrimmages are great for getting the blood flowing, but nothing compares to the thrill of actual live-action hitting people who are wearing a completely different jersey, even if the game doesn’t count in the standings. Coaches are evaluating talent, bubble players are fighting for a job, and fans finally get a good view of some structured football. There is a lot to draw our attention, but here are five things to keep an eye on when the lights come on Saturday night. 1. Revel vs. someone else’s WR Cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. has spent the majority of training camp locked in intense battles against elite receivers named CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. It’s been exhilarating, but we’re all incredibly eager to see how he fares when he is matched up against a wideout we can comfortably root against. Revel Jr. has progressed beautifully throughout camp, drawing plenty of praise for his improved technique and route anticipation. The coaching staff is excited to see how those practice developments translate into a live game setting against real opponents. Tonight’s game will serve as a nice first test for the year-two version of this young corner. 2. Who runs the ball well? While Javonte Williams firmly holds down the starting running back role, the backup spots behind him are up for grabs. Jaydon Blue comes into this matchup carrying big expectations from the coaching staff and should have an excellent opportunity to establish himself early. For him, it’s about keeping his mental game sharp and picking up blitzes. Right on his heels is Phil Mafah, a physical runner eager to showcase what he can do as well. It would also be wise not to forget about Malik Davis. If the backup offensive line can open up some lanes and give Davis room to operate in open space, he might surprise some people. This backup running back job remains wide open, and Saturday night is the perfect stage for someone to seize the momentum. 3. The backup QBs The Cowboys’ quarterback group features a fascinating duel with the backup job currently undecided between Joe Milton III and Sam Howell. These battles are often determined by how well the backup can handle themselves when the unexpected is coming right at them. Making smart, quick decisions and delivering accurate balls are paramount. Those factors are crucial and will carry a lot of influence on the tough decisions the coaches have to make in a few weeks. With final roster cuts looming next month, every good decision and well-thrown ball will carry immense weight in determining who’s seated behind Dak Prescott in the quarterback room. 4. Pressure from the edge Dallas enters the preseason with plenty of unanswered questions about their pass rush depth, opening the door for Saturday night to serve as auditions for players looking to climb the depth chart and earn more reps. The team has some highly intriguing options to test out. Rookie Malachi Lawrence will be a point of keen interest for fans as everyone waits to see how his raw burst translates against NFL offensive tackles. Meanwhile, veterans Sam Williams and James Houston will be playing with plenty of urgency, looking to prove they deserve their spot in the defensive rotation. 5. The new darkhorse Every single year, a brand-new preseason darling emerges from the bottom of the depth chart, making flashy plays that catch the entire fanbase completely by surprise. Expect more of the same this weekend, which begs the question of who will step up to claim this honor. Linebacker Justin Barron is already gaining serious steam after putting together a highly impressive showing during the recent scrimmage against the Los Angeles Rams. In the secondary, safety Julius Wood has consistently found himself around the ball and making plays throughout the week. If you are looking for an offensive spark, Camden Brown enters the weekend as a prime undrafted free agent wide receiving sleeper to watch, while everyone is still waiting on another UDFA, tight end Michael Trigg, to show out with some big plays. Who is your darkhorse selection who will turn heads tonight?

For the players, however, it is a chance to show the coaches what they’ve got, part of a three-week stretch that could make or break their path to the 53-man roster. Today we’ll examine the Dallas Cowboys’ preseason opener against the defending Super Bowl champion, the Seattle Seahawks, with three predictions. Defenders will be hungry Fans have heard how intense the practices have been so far, with physicality standing out. The defense, along with new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, have led that charge. Players like Shavon Revel, who is having a strong camp, and Justin Barron, who is still not yet penciled into a roster spot even after securing three interceptions in the joint practice against the Rams, should be bringing the energy they’ve built up in Oxnard. Among their play-calls, Dallas likely won’t reveal anything of note, but having the players in the right places would be a huge step for this defense compared to a year ago. TRENDING: Caleb Downs has had CeeDee Lamb IN A BOX throughout training camp. Downs has reportedly been “blanketing” several of the Cowboys top receiving threats during team periods. The Cowboys rookie safety is showing early flashes of ALL-PRO potential 📦😳 pic.twitter.com/ioqgDdTh96 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 14, 2026 Shavon Revel with the pick here off Dak – Revel has had a really strong camp. Tons to like about his game, and the way he's taking strides. pic.twitter.com/4xiCbdAnT5 — Mike Leslie (@MikeLeslieWFAA) August 14, 2026 The offense will try to highlight potential RB2 and WR5 The offense has a ton of continuity from last season, so the top levels are essentially etched in stone at this point. Yet, the Cowboys’ search for a running back to spell Javonte Williams seems to be ongoing. Earlier in the week, there was positional movement there with the Cowboys bringing in Jashaun Corbin, and although Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah have had some moments in camp, the rumbling is that Dallas still wants to see more from the backs behind Williams, even if Blue might be a lock for the 53-man roster. The receiver situation is a bit different; basically, slots 1-4 are taken, and by all accounts, the Cowboys are only going to carry five wide receivers into the 2026 season, meaning one spot is up for grabs. title: Take your drama to yo mama: The NFC East’s offseason soap opera isn’t in Dallas
summary: The 2026 Cowboys have largely avoided the drama that has felt more like a feature than a bug in years past. Getting ahead of the Quinnen Williams extension and handling the George Pickens deal without a public spectacle put them ahead of the curve on the contract front. Reputed interest in Brandon Sorsby for the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 9: Jaxson Dart #6 and Cam Skattebo #44 of the New York Giants pose for a photo after winning the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at MetLife Stadium on October 9, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Cowboys have largely avoided the drama that has felt more like a feature than a bug in years past. Getting ahead of the Quinnen Williams extension and handling the George Pickens deal without a public spectacle put them ahead of the curve on the contract front. Reputed interest in Brandon Sorsby for the supplemental draft and the Maxx Crosby pursuit that could have easily become another “Jerry wants a star / Jerry won’t pay for a star / what are the Cowboys doing?” cycle – all barely registered on the drama meter in Dallas. And even attempts to manufacture drama around Prescott’s choice of T-shirt, Prescott’s personal life, tinted windows at AT&T Stadium, or Tony Romo’s problems rolled off the Cowboys Star like water off a greased armadillo. Dallas had plenty of headlines. It just didn’t have a season-long soap opera. The rest of the NFC East apparently didn’t get the memo. New York: Jaxson Dart can’t learn the new offense, and Cam Skattebo can’t stop flipping The amount of hype and expectation surrounding Jaxson Dart should have the Giants topping the NFL drama charts all season. Consider that Dart won just four games last year and had over 300 total yards just twice. Couldn’t stay out of the blue tent, refused to slide, and is now struggling at training camp. When Dart actually did slide after a third-down run during Monday’s practice, it made ESPN headlines (“ Dart’s slide receives rave reviews at Giants camp ” and drew effusive praise from his teammates and head coach. “We’ve been begging him to do that for a while,” Giants outside linebacker and defensive captain Brian Burns said. “So, I’m glad that he’s starting to practice it.” Coach John Harbaugh seemed to love it, as well. “I did,” he said. “I clapped. I applauded. I applauded when he did that. It was great.” Well at least the Giants have something to feel good about, because another practice this week didn’t go well at all. This was another day when the offense and Dart were unimpressive. Dart was picked off once. […] He took too many sacks and was at times inaccurate, especially during a 7-on-7 red zone period when he was only 2-for-8 passing. And this is part of a bigger picture in which Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy admitted that while Dart is “super talented,” the second-year quarterback is experiencing “struggles” in camp and has “areas he needs to get better at,” including “seeing the defense.” None of this is going to go down well in New York, where fans and media have an age-old tradition of turning every little thing into a referendum on the franchise. But RB Cam Skattebo may be the real star of the Giants’ offseason variety show. Coming off a rookie season cut short by injury, Skattebo declared that he planned to carry the ball 300 times for more than 2,000 yards in 2026. For context, he had 101 carries for 410 yards as a rookie. The math alone made this irresistible offseason content. And then, perhaps because the Giants’ offseason writers’ room was running out of material, Skattebo attempted a backflip at Fanatics Fest. He did not stick the landing. The video went viral. Skattebo subsequently assured everyone that he was fine and promised, somewhat reassuringly, “ I will not hurt myself before the season. ” everyone: don’t do dumb shit rehabbing a leg injury Cam Skattebo: pic.twitter.com/HuI48m44c3 — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) July 18, 2026 And then the Giants released their depth chart, which nominally shows Skattebo ahead of Tyrone Tracy Jr., but that may not be how the season shakes out for our 2,000-yard man, at least if Dan Duggan’s observations from practice for The Athletic are anything to go by. Cam Skattebo has been the first running back up in team periods on most days, with Tyrone Tracy Jr. taking the majority of snaps in two-minute drives. That figures to be a time share, with Skattebo the 1-A and Tracy the 1-B. Devin Singletary has been the only other back to get significant reps with the first-team offense. Running back remains a position the Giants will seek to reinforce before the season, particularly if they can find a dynamic runner. The quarterback still needs to learn how to slide and has trouble learning the new offense, the running back wants 2,000 yards but may not even be the No. 1 RB on the team. And we haven’t even heard anything about Odell Beckham yet … Philadelphia: Eagles’ social-media team chose violence The Eagles might have the strongest claim to the NFC East drama championship. The roots go back to 2025, when Philadelphia’s offense became a weekly source of friction. A.J. Brown repeatedly expressed frustration with his role, posting cryptic messages on social media and at one point appearing on a Twitch stream and describing himself as “struggling” in a “s— show.” He even told fantasy players to get rid of him. Brown later acknowledged that his frustrations had boiled over, but the underlying problem wasn’t imaginary. The Eagles’ offense had become stagnant, Brown wasn’t getting the ball, and questions about the relationship between Brown and Jalen Hurts became a recurring storyline. Then came the playoff loss to San Francisco. Brown dropped two passes, finished with three catches for 25 yards, and got into a heated sideline confrontation with Nick Sirianni. The Eagles’ head coach and star receiver had to be separated by a dude they call “Big Dom” while television cameras captured the whole thing. Brown subsequently declined to speak to reporters. That provided plenty of offseason material until Philadelphia finally traded Brown to New England in June. Things seemed to quiet down in the City of Brotherly Love, until the Eagles’ own social-media department decided to help. They posted video of Jalen Hurts throwing an interception in practice. Right on Q pic.twitter.com/ons19ZR2Hy — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 12, 2026 Not a clip of Hurts making a spectacular throw. Not a montage of the quarterback looking sharp. An interception. It promptly went viral, with fans and analysts wondering why the organization would voluntarily broadcast a bad play by its franchise quarterback. Hurts is already entering his sixth season with a different offensive coordinator, while his passing — particularly his willingness to attack the middle of the field — remains a subject of criticism. That is not dysfunction. That’s entertainment. Jalen Hurts' rate of throws over the middle of the field, per @FantasyPtsData : + 2024: 13.3% (dead last of 39 QBs) + 2025: 16.3% (35th of 36 QBs) And on attempts less than 10 yards downfield over the MOF (where Lemon thrives): + 2024: 6.1% (38th/39) + 2025: 6.6% (32nd/36) https://t.co/krAk0hwmlm — Dataroma (@ffdataroma) April 24, 2026 And if losing A.J. Brown and changing offensive coordinators wasn’t enough upheaval, the Eagles may also have a couple of early questions about their latest offensive investments if their top two draft picks don’t live up to their draft billing. Our friends at BGN summarize after looking at the Eagles latest depth chart: Nothing shocking about how the wide receivers are listed but it is notable to see Lemon with the starters despite the fact he’s missed a lot of time in camp and didn’t stand out prior to getting hurt. Lemon might not actually be a Week 1 starter with the likes of Cooper and Moore having strong summers. Or at least there could be a heavier receiver rotation than there’s been in recent years. Whereas Lemon is listed with the starters, the Eagles aren’t even pretending that Stowers is a top two tight end right now. With the way the Eagles laid out tight end on this chart, I don’t know that he’s even necessarily TE3. I tend to think Stowers might be a healthy scratch ……

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 29
summary: It is Day 29 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - OCTOBER 8: Nick Folk #6 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates his game winning field goal with seconds left as Jabari Greer #33 of the Buffalo Bills watches at Ralph Wilson Stadium October 8, 2007 in Orchard Park, New York. Dallas won 25-24. (Photo by Rick Stewart/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 29 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We got a big one for you on Day 29 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the most remarkable comeback wins in Cowboys history. It was a game that should have ended in defeat. Tony Romo threw five interceptions, lost a fumble and watched the Bills return two interceptions for touchdowns. Yet with just 20 seconds remaining, Dallas somehow completed an unforgettable rally. Monday, October 8, 2007 Ralph Wilson Stadium, Orchard Park, New York Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 25, Buffalo Bills 24 The Cowboys, who had started the game undefeated, appeared to be on track to become Super Bowl contenders. However, Buffalo had other plans. George Wilson returned Romo’s first interception for a touchdown, and later Chris Kelsay scored another touchdown on a 103-yard interception return after Romo targeted Terrell Owens in the end zone. A Rian Lindell field goal added to the Bills’ lead, making it 17-7. Despite this, Jason Witten caught a late touchdown to cut the deficit to 17-10 at halftime. Dallas struggled to build momentum after the break. Nick Folk connected from 47 and 29 yards, but every time the Cowboys appeared to be climbing back into the game, Buffalo answered. Terrence McGee returned the ensuing kickoff 103 yards for a touchdown following Folk’s second field goal, restoring an 11-point Bills advantage and leaving Dallas trailing 24-13 heading into the fourth quarter. Despite the turnovers, Romo never stopped attacking. Folk added another field goal early in the final quarter to make it 24-16 before the Cowboys’ defense came alive. Dallas forced consecutive punts and gave the offense one final opportunity with less than two minutes remaining. Romo drove the Cowboys 80 yards in just over a minute before finding Patrick Crayton for a four-yard touchdown with 20 seconds left. Marion Barber converted the two-point attempt to cut the deficit to 24-22, but Dallas still needed to recover the onside kick. Buffalo appeared to have the game won, only for tight end Ryan Neufeld to mishandle the football, allowing the Cowboys to recover near midfield. With one final chance, Romo swiftly moved Dallas into Buffalo territory. After a timeout intended to freeze him, rookie kicker Nick Folk calmly drilled a 53-yard field goal as time expired, securing one of the greatest regular-season comebacks in franchise history. Romo finished with 309 passing yards, two touchdowns and five interceptions, making his performance one of the strangest winning quarterback stat lines in NFL history. Witten led the offense with seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown, while Owens added seven receptions for 66 yards. Folk scored 13 points and cemented himself as the hero with the longest game-winning kick of his young career. This game belongs on the countdown because it perfectly captured the resilience of the 2007 Cowboys. Few teams survive six turnovers on the road. Even fewer overcome two defensive touchdowns and a kickoff return touchdown. Dallas simply refused to quit, and when the opportunity finally arrived, Romo, Folk and the special teams delivered one of the defining wins of the era. #Cowboys vs #Bills 2007 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 25, Buffalo Bills 24 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/TvPzoa93y0 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 15, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The Cowboys scored nine points in the final 20 seconds after trailing 24-16. title: 4 Cowboys who need big games against the Seahawks
summary: After a long offseason, the Dallas Cowboys are back in live game action. The Cowboys will travel to Seattle to play in the last game of the week, with all eyes on the initial rendition of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys. Thankfully, the approach so far has been all business with no contractual drama looming over […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Marist Liufau #35 of the Dallas Cowboys lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at AT&T Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a long offseason, the Dallas Cowboys are back in live game action. The Cowboys will travel to Seattle to play in the last game of the week, with all eyes on the initial rendition of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys. Thankfully, the approach so far has been all business with no contractual drama looming over the team. As a result, the team has been laser-focused and is coming off a stellar showing in practice against the Los Angeles Rams. However, as Philadelphia 76ers legend Allen Iverson once said: “We’re talking about practice”. The preseason game is far from meaningless. For some players, they need to use Saturday’s game to stand out from the crowd in hopes of making the team, but who are those players? Who needs to have a big preseason game? Traeshon Holden Should the Cowboys go long at the wide receiver spot, Traeshon Holden has a chance to make the team. This year he’s battling with more veteran competition such as the likes of Marquez Valdez-Scantling and Denzel Mims. Plus, He’s competing with a draft pick in seventh-rounder Anthony Smith and UDFA Camden Brown. That said, the summertime spotlight isn’t anything new to him. He was a standout performer last season during the preseason, which allowed him to hang around on the practice squad. A strong game versus Seattle reminds everyone of who he is and what he’s capable of when the lights are on. He’s had a quiet training camp, and a big game against Seattle will thrust him back into the conversation. Drew Shelton Things have not gone smoothly for Drew Shelton to start off his rookie season. He has struggled at times in pass protection, and has shown that he is a project player. He’s not in danger of being cut, the potential and tools are there, and his status as a fourth-round pick practically ensures that he will be on the team. We should expect to see him play substantially against Seattle while Dallas figures out their reserve rotation. Nate Thomas also hasn’t had a very good outings either, drawing the competition closer within Shelton’s reach. The team added the well-traveled Sebastian Gutierrez to compete for the swing tackle position. If Shelton can put together a solid outing, it would push him ahead of Thomas and he could gain some footing in the coming weeks for the battle at swing tackle. Jay Toia Currently, Otito Ogbonnia is slated to be the team’s primary nose tackle in their 3-4 front. However, behind him is Jay Toia. Toia didn’t have a particularly good rookie season and was primarily counted on to step in to support the run defense. Fast forward to this year, and Toia hasn’t made much of an impact. At this point, he’s very much replaceable, and the other options behind him aren’t that far apart from him right now. Kelvin Gilliam has flashed a few times during practices and will also see a large chunk of action Saturday. The time is now for Toia to show something or be on the hot seat. With a front that features Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams, the Cowboys won’t be as cavalier when it comes to nose tackle should something happen to Ogbonnia. Toia has to have a good game to give the team confidence that he can be relied upon in a crucial season for the team. Marist Liufau Marist Liufau has been dealt a tough hand. Going into the third year of his contract, he has been tasked with playing a new position and changing roles to an edge rusher in a 3-4 defense. Fortunately for him, he has been around the football and made a few plays at practices. The team has also used that opportunity to move around formations and line him up in different spots. It’ll be exciting to see what the plan is for him during the game. There are questions that he needs to answer by playing well. Among the questions, how much has he improved this offseason as an edge rusher? The interior linebacker spot has improved tremendously for the Cowboys, so there’s no real chance that he plays a big role in that spot. The edge rushers are solid for Dallas, but Liufau could elbow his way into the conversation with a sack or forced fumble coming off the edge. He’s one of the most intriguing storylines for Saturday night.

title: Cowboys improved depth on defense should shine in preseason action
summary: For the first time in a long time, it feels like the Dallas Cowboys have some quality depth on their roster. For years, we have talked about how top heavy the Cowboys were over training camp, preseason, and the regular season. This year, things feel a bit different. The defensive side of the ball has […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Otito Ogbonnia #91 of the Dallas Cowboys in a defensive stance during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time in a long time, it feels like the Dallas Cowboys have some quality depth on their roster. For years, we have talked about how top heavy the Cowboys were over training camp, preseason, and the regular season. This year, things feel a bit different. The defensive side of the ball has been praised for most of training camp, especially after a nice day of practice against the Los Angeles Rams. While it’s unlikely we will see a ton of the starters over the course of the Cowboys three preseason games, it sounds like we will see some of them, even if it’s limited action. What we will see for sure is the Cowboys’ new and improved depth compete for roster spots for Dallas, or the other 31 teams if they are waived ahead of the start of the regular season. One of the biggest differences between 2026 and the last few seasons is how much depth the Cowboys’ have in the secondary. In previous seasons, the Cowboys lack of depth in the secondary was an Achilles heel for the team in preseason and regular season action. With Christian Parker running the show on defense now, that changed, and quickly. This offseason the Cowboys made a ton of additions to their secondary by bringing in Cobie Durant, Jalen Thompson, P.J. Locke, Derion Kendrick, Ameer Speed, Caleb Downs, and Devin Moore. All of whom may have been significant upgrades over what the Cowboys had on the field at times in regular season games last season. But it doesn’t stop there. Along with their additions to the secondary, the Cowboys raised their floor on the defensive line over the offseason as well. After bringing in Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, Otito Ogbonnia, Jonathan Bullard, LT Overton, Kevin Gilliam Jr., D.J. Withers, and Tommy Dunn Jr. over the offseason, the Cowboys finally leaned into an identify on the defensive line. With a lot of young, new blood on the defensive side of the ball, the Cowboys should compete well in preseason games given their uptick in talent down their depth chart. While it’s unlikely we see much of Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, DeMarvion Overshown, DaRon Bland, Jalen Thompson, Rashan Gary, or Donovan Ezeiruaku in preseason games, the Cowboys’ coaching staff should get some good evaluations done to finalize their roster over the next three weeks, and these preseason games should be much more interesting to watch with much better depth filling out the roster. Which defensive players are you most interested in seeing Saturday night?

title: Jonah Coleman gives the Broncos another reason to be excited

full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Jonah Coleman (20) of the Denver Broncos runs with the football during the Friday evening NFL preseason football game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Denver Broncos on August 14, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. title: Sean Payton says OC Davis Webb was ‘on point’ vs. Falcons
summary: We saw Davis Webb call plays for one preseason game last season; however, Friday was our first real look at the Davis Webb offense in 2026, and well, it went pretty damn well. The Broncos had a 24-0 lead at halftime, and we saw the offense move the ball up and down the field against […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Offensive coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos looks on against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of a NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We saw Davis Webb call plays for one preseason game last season; however, Friday was our first real look at the Davis Webb offense in 2026, and well, it went pretty damn well. The Broncos had a 24-0 lead at halftime , and we saw the offense move the ball up and down the field against the Falcons’ starting defense with ease. Keep in mind, they did this without starting quarterback Bo Nix, star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, leading rusher JK Dobbins, and starting center Luke Wattenberg. So, it was a fairly impressive first showing by the Broncos offense and Davis Webb. Sean Payton told reporters after the Broncos' first preseason game that the offensive operation was "smooth" "Davis was on point" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 15, 2026 After the game, Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media and was asked how he thought the offense operated vs. the Falcons. Payton told reporters, “It was smooth,” and that offensive coordinator and play caller Davis Webb was “on point”. He also credited the quarterbacks for doing a good job of getting out of the huddle quickly. “It was smooth. I think maybe there was a play or two; we got down to three seconds, but the subs were good, Davis [Webb] was on point. I thought the ‘Q’s’ [quarterbacks] did a good job getting out of the huddle.” All things considered, it was a pretty perfect night for Webb and the Broncos offense. They were without multiple key members of their offense, but still operated smoothly and looked Week 1 ready in the preseason opener. Stidham moved the ball down the field with chunk plays to wide receivers Pat Bryant and Courtland Sutton before letting fullback Adam Prentice pound it in from the one-yard line. We also saw an emphasis on the run game. They had 162 yards rushing on the night, and second-year back RJ Harvey and impressive-looking rookie Jonah Coleman led the way. Harvey got the start and showed some toughness and powerful running between the tackles. Coleman would come in next and showed good burst, power, vision, and contact balance and why coaches have been impressed with the talented rookie back so far. Harvey would finish the night with 5 carries for 16 yards, while Coleman had 4 carries for 24 yards. Payton was asked about his thoughts on Coleman and told reporters that they have been seeing this throughout camp. He liked Coleman’s balance coming out of tackles and thought the running back group overall had a good night. “Just what we’ve been seeing, right? And then you see enough of it, and you’re like, all right. Look, he’s had a good camp, and I liked his balance coming out of some of the tackles. I thought overall, the group had a good night.” Payton, Webb, and the Broncos offensive staff put an emphasis on improving the run game this offseason, and so far, the results have been there. Harvey showed some tough running, but his game will mostly be as a pass catcher while Coleman flashed starter potential. I believe he is going to have a big part in the Broncos’ run game and pair with veteran JK Dobbins as the Broncos’ main ball carriers this season. It was just Week 1 of the preseason, but so far, the Davis Webb experience is off to a hot start.

summary: According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, Broncos reserve linebacker Levelle Bailey suffered a break in his lower leg during Friday’s game vs. the Falcons. He will undergo surgery on his leg and will miss extensive time due to this injury, according to Klis. This is a devastating development for Bailey, who was competing for a […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 07: Linebacker Levelle Bailey #56 of the Denver Broncos during a game between the Denver Broncos and the Tennessee Titans at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, CO on September 07, 2025. (Photo by Kevin Langley/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, Broncos reserve linebacker Levelle Bailey suffered a break in his lower leg during Friday’s game vs. the Falcons. He will undergo surgery on his leg and will miss extensive time due to this injury, according to Klis. Broncos linebacker Levelle Bailey suffers broken leg | https://t.co/24dIoDu7uH https://t.co/AX0BL4c2bo — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 15, 2026 This is a devastating development for Bailey, who was competing for a spot on the Broncos’ 53-man roster this summer. They have two roster spots open behind starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, and Bailey was pushing for one of those spots, or at the very least, competing for a spot on the Broncos’ practice squad. Now, he will be sidelined for a significant amount of time and could be looking at a season-ending injured reserve stint. Bailey joined the team back in 2024 as an undrafted free agent and has been with the team since then. He has bounced on and off the Broncos’ active roster/practice squad and has given the team valuable depth at the linebacker position. With Bailey now sidelined for a significant amount of time, the Broncos’ depth at linebacker has taken a hit. Jordan Turner has been sidelined for most of camp and did not play vs. the Falcons, but he should be nearing a return soon. Rookie Red Murdock led the team in tackles on Friday, while Karene Reid made an incredible diving PBU that led to a Jahdae Barron pick-6 touchdown. Undrafted rookie Taurean York also made some plays late in the game, but still, we could see the Broncos add some depth and competition to this room, especially after losing Bailey for a significant amount of time. The Broncos have a handful of training camp practices remaining, as well as two more preseason games, so there still is plenty of time for this roster battle to figure itself out. Still, this is a tough break for Bailey, who was a contender for one of these roster spots, or at the very least, a member of the Broncos’ practice squad.

title: Sean Payton was pleased with the Broncos’ run game vs. Falcons
summary: The Denver Broncos looked impressive throughout most of the 27-7 preseason win over the Atlanta Falcons outside a couple of special teams miscues. The best aspect to that win could be the underrated run game. Denver outgained the Falcons by over 100 yards on the ground and that was something that head coach Sean Payton […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos rushes against DeMarcco Hellams #23, Ja'quan McMillian #29 and Nate Adkins #45 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of a NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos looked impressive throughout most of the 27-7 preseason win over the Atlanta Falcons outside a couple of special teams miscues. The best aspect to that win could be the underrated run game. Denver outgained the Falcons by over 100 yards on the ground and that was something that head coach Sean Payton was happy about afterwards. “I was pleased with that,” Payton said. “I thought the runners played well and I thought we blocked them pretty well. It’s kind of a heavy front; they’ll play some base. I know we had one fumble, but those guys ran hard.” The player that impressed me the most on the night was rookie Jonah Coleman. His first two carries were a bit disappointing, but after that he was the best runner of the night for the Broncos. His first two carries went for four yards, but his last two went for 20. Coleman has had a good camp and Payton backed that up when asked about his impressions of Coleman during the game. “Just what we’ve been seeing, right? And then you see enough of it, and you’re like, all right. Look, he’s had a good camp, and I liked his balance coming out of some of the tackles. I thought overall, the group had a good night.” His ability to avoid going down with first contact is something he was known for in college and we saw more of that in his runs on Friday night. JK Dobbins is your clear starter this year, but Coleman had himself a good first showing for us fans. It would be good for the team to have hit pay dirt on a midround pick like Jonah. title: Lions training camp notes: Offense thrives in end-of-game scenarios
summary: The Detroit Lions returned to practice after their Thursday night preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals. But on Saturday, it was a short, unpadded practice. Still, the intensity was up pretty high, there were plenty of competitive drills and an interesting focus on late-game scenarios. We’re going to break down each segment of practice in […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) snaps on his helmet during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions returned to practice after their Thursday night preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals. But on Saturday, it was a short, unpadded practice. Still, the intensity was up pretty high, there were plenty of competitive drills and an interesting focus on late-game scenarios. We’re going to break down each segment of practice in our Detroit Lions Day 12 training camp observations. It kicks off with some one-on-one drills. Offensive line vs. Defensive line OL/DL observations were written by Erik Schlitt. In one-on-ones, it appeared coaches wanted to reward a few of the players who performed well in last Thursday’s game. That meant Ahmad Hassanein got the first rep of the drill and got to try his hand at beating Penei Sewell. Hassanein attacked the outside shoulder, but the All-Pro handled him with ease, getting a clear win. Sewell would also clearly win his second rep in the drill, locking up Derrick Moore. Meanwhile, Hassanein rebounded with his next rep, kicking inside and executing a swim move over guard Mason Miller. With Sewell taking on others, that meant Aidan Hutchinson was forced to shift his dance partner, and he kicked over to the other side of the line and faced off against Blake Miller. The rookie handled the All-Pro well on a speed arc move, but when they rematched, Hutchinson sold the speed and swam back inside for the easy win. Juice Scruggs returned to practice and stepped into a starting center role and split his reps against Tyleik Williams, getting ahead of Williams’ power in the first rep, but succumbed to a power bull rush on the second. Other players who won both reps convincingly included Tate Ratledge, who beat Alim McNeill and Levi Onwuzurike; Christian Mahogany, who also beat McNeill and Onwuzurike; and Ben Stille, who convincingly beat Seth McLaughlin and Michael Niese. DBs get physical against WRs Isaac TeSlaa has been dealing with feisty, physical cornerbacks all of camp, but on Saturday, everyone was getting a dose of handsy, rough defensive backs. Let’s start with Ennis Rakestraw, who was looking to rebound from a tough preseason opener. On his first rep, he punched the ball out late against Jameson Williams, something he’s done a few times this training camp. Then, on a rep against TeSlaa, he jammed the second-year receiver so hard that he ended up tossing him to the ground before he could develop a route. But when the two re-repped a play later, TeSlaa broke free on a crossing route for a big gain. Nick Whiteside also tested the limits of defensive contact—and, in my opinion, crossed the line several times. He probably would’ve been called for pass interference on two reps he “won” (vs. TeSlaa and Jameson Williams). But to his credit, Williams was jammed so hard he slipped on one rep, and on the rematch, Whiteside (right on the edge of defensive holding) got his hands on the ball for a near interception. It was another strong series for Rock Ya-Sin, who got a pass breakup on Williams, ripped the ball out late from TeSlaa, and was right on top of Cedrick Wilson Jr. when he caught a short pass. Other quick standouts: Decent couple of reps from WR Tay Martin, who nicely adjusted to a deep shot, hauling in a huge gain opposite Roger McCreary. And it’s worth noting it was Jared Goff throwing to him. Khalil Dorsey clocked four wins during this session. He had tight coverage on Malik Cunningham, broke up a sideline shot to Tarik Black, then elevated to knock away another pass to Black, before getting the better of Black one more time on a comeback route. Air Dorsey pic.twitter.com/O3j25UarUq — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 15, 2026 Seven-on-seven standouts This session included a lot of checkdowns, offering little insight into play. However, there were a few interesting notes on personnel. For one, while there were a lot of substitutions and uncommon players in unfamiliar spots (ie: Sam LaPorta with the third team), one thing that was relatively consistent during these drills was Thomas Harper getting some time in both first-team safety spots, replacing both Avonte Maddox and Chuck Clark at times. Christian Izien, Keith Abney, and Roger McCreary all rotated in the nickel. The most notable play of this section was a great throw from Luke Altmyer (the No. 2 quarterback on Saturday), who dropped a nice ball to Dominic Lovett on a post for a significant gain. Lovett made a nice play on the ball by leaping and snagging the ball with his fingertips. Situational drills Detroit closed the team period of practice with a series of six quick situational drills. The offense cleanly won three, the defense won one, and two were a little more ambiguous. Here’s what happened. Situation #1: Score: 21-23 0:06 left Starting on opponent 44-yard line 1 timeout left The goal here was simply to get a few yards to improve the field goal attempt. Detroit ran the ball right up the middle—with notably Juice Scruggs as the starting center—and Jahmyr Gibbs picked up about 4 yards. Detroit called a timeout with a couple of seconds left and did not attempt the field goal, leaving the “winner” of this drill ambiguous. Situation #2: (second teams) Score: 21-23 0:14 left Starting on own 48-yard line 0 timeouts The purpose here appeared to be using the entire field late in the game and hurrying to the line to spike the ball if stopped in bounds. The second team never got a chance because a shot over the middle to Greg Dortch was overthrown by Altmyer and fell incomplete. That was the end of the attempt, even though there was still time on the clock. Situation #3: (first teamers the rest of the way) Score: 21-23 0:07 left Starting on own 41-yard line 1 timeout left Jared Goff hit Jameson Williams up the middle for a big 28-yard gain, and they were able to call a timeout with one second left. Like the rest of the drills, no field goal was attempted, but this seemed like a clear “win” for the offense. Situation #4: Score: 21-23 0:08 left Starting on own 42-yard line I can’t get into the specifics of this play, but let’s just say it was a very unorthodox screen pass that picked up 18 yards and stopped the clock for another offensive win. (Detroit, again, did not attempt what would’ve been a 58-yard field goal). Situation #5: Score: 20-21 1:12 left Starting on opponent’s 9-yard line Defense has two timeouts left This was an interesting situation. Essentially, the offense could run about 50 of the 72 seconds off the clock with three straight runs, but the defense had incentive just to let the offense score to get the ball back with ample time left. So, despite Gibbs initially getting held up, Tyleik Williams—then several other defenders—hilariously lifted Gibbs off the ground and carried him into the end zone. Situation #6: Score: 20-24 0:05 left Fourth-and-3 on the opponents’ 9-yard line 1 timeout Goff was given a decision: check down quickly to get a first down and take one shot at the end zone, or just take the shot on fourth down. Ultimately, he hit Williams on an out route for the first down, and he stepped out of bounds with 1 second left. On the subsequent play, Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown for the 3-yard touchdown as time expired, although Keith Abney pleaded his case about an offensive pass interference call.

title: Detroit Lions injury news: Several starters return to action
summary: It was a big day at Detroit Lions training camp, as several important players returned to action following the team’s preseason opener. Saturday’s practice was only in shells and a short one, but it’s a key step in getting some critical players back into the starting lineup and earning some valuable reps. Returned to practice: […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed (4) makes a catch during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Sunday, July 20, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It was a big day at Detroit Lions training camp, as several important players returned to action following the team’s preseason opener. Saturday’s practice was only in shells and a short one, but it’s a key step in getting some critical players back into the starting lineup and earning some valuable reps. Returned to practice: RB Sione Vaki (broken nose, poked eye) RB Jabari Small (knee?) C Juice Scruggs (soft tissue) LB Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) EDGE Derrick Moore (groin) CB D.J. Reed (groin) Vaki didn’t do any team work on offense, but was back in his spot on special teams, particularly in the personal protector role on punt coverage. Small missed a couple practices and the preseason opener with what is believed to be a knee injury, but that remains unconfirmed by the Lions. He’s in a tight competition for the RB4 role, so his return is critical for his chances to make the roster. Scruggs was back after missing about a week with an undisclosed soft tissue injury. He appeared to be fully back, and was with the first-team offense as the starting center, jumping Seth McLaughlin. Rodriguez returned and got a ton of work with the second-team defense during nickel looks. I did not see base defense looks with the first-team on Saturday, so it’s unclear if he’s still considered a starter. Moore saw the field for the first time in almost two weeks, and the rookie defensive end went through most of practice. That included some one-on-one work, and plenty of special teams reps for the former Wolverine. Reed got an entire workload after missing some time with a groin injury. He was back as the No. 1 cornerback in both individual and team drills, and looked feisty in coverage against Detroit’s talented receivers. Working with trainers, not practicing: OT Devin Cochran (undisclosed) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) The big news here is that fourth-round rookie Jimmy Rolder was out working with a trainer for the first time since his leg injury early in camp. He was wearing a big sleeve on his leg, but was running at a pretty good pace. We’ll see if he can avoid injured reserve at the start of the season, but it’s worth the reminder that coach Dan Campbell said he’d miss “a while,” but there were subsequent reports that he avoided a major injury, and he will “miss some time.” Cochran did some serious work with a trainer, as he tries to return to the field to give Detroit some much-needed tackle depth. Not practicing: RB Isiah Pacheco (knee) RB Jacob Saylors (ankle) RB Kye Robichaux (broken foot) TE Jackson Meeks (undisclosed) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) C Cade Mays (wrist) EDGE Payton Turner (back) DT Mekhi Wingo (concussion?) LB Damone Clark (undisclosed) S Loren Strickland S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) The Lions did suffer a lot of little injuries during their preseason opener. Saylors had an ankle injury after being tackled from behind, but Campbell downplayed the seriousness of it. “I don’t think it’s serious, but it could be a day or two here,” Campbell said. The bigger injury happened to running back mate Kye Robichaux, who apparently has a broken bone in his foot. “God bless him, dude. He got a foot (injury). It could be – looks like he may have broke a bone in that foot,” Campbell said. “And he’s been so dang just durable all camp, played his heart out. He’s another guy just gives you everything he’s got, maximize everything.” At this point, there is no information on why Jackson Meeks missed practice. After Thursday’s game, Campbell speculated that Mekhi Wingo may be going through concussion protocol, so his absence is not a surprise. Campbell expressed some concern about Strickland’s injury—suggesting they needed to look at imaging before diagnosing him. His absence could be bad news for him, but it’s too early to know.
