title: Jacksonville Jaguars Winners And Losers Preseason Week One: Jags Win Sloppy In New Orleans
summary: Much to the dismay of Bucky Brooks, the Jacksonville Jaguars are back, baby. Playing in the Superdome down on the bayou, the Jags somehow came back and defeated the New Orleans Saints 24-20 after an impressive second half.  It was as “preseason game one” as a game could get with one bad half of ball […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 3: J'Mari Taylor #30 of the Jacksonville Jaguars practices during training camp at Miller Electric Center on August 3, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Much to the dismay of Bucky Brooks, the Jacksonville Jaguars are back, baby. Playing in the Superdome down on the bayou, the Jags somehow came back and defeated the New Orleans Saints 24-20 after an impressive second half. It was as “preseason game one” as a game could get with one bad half of ball and one half that resembled something close to good football. The starters didn’t play so there shouldn’t be too much worry about this lone preseason contest, but that didn’t make it any less ugly, at least in the first half. The backup quarterback position looks like an issue, as does the depth of the offensive line so far this preseason. But hey, at least Cam Little is still good and we won! WINNERS Josh Cameron and CJ Williams While it was largely a quiet afternoon for Jags rookies, two rookie receivers lived up to the camp hype on Saturday in a limited way. Rooks Josh Cameron and CJ Williams looked fine enough when given the opportunities from the backup signal callers. Williams was second on the team in receiving with two catches for 28 yards, with a long of 17. Cameron had just one catch for 17 yards total. Those numbers aren’t popping off the page but the early signs for two young Jags seem fine enough. This pair will probably continue to be the big storyline from camp and preseason as we progress. Yasir Abdullah You know it’s the preseason when Yasir Abdullah gets mentioned on the Winners list. But it’s what we got. Abdullah had a solid day both on defense and on special teams, logging a strip sack in the first half which led to a B.J. Green fumble recovery. The former Trent Baalke draft pick also had a solid punt coverage tackle that lost the Saints seven yards and led to a punt on the next possession. The 2023 draft pick finished with two tackles, his strip sack and a tackle for loss. A lot of guys sleepwalked through Saturday’s game but Abdullah did not. J’Mari Taylor While it wasn’t easy on offense Saturday, undrafted rookie running back J’Mari Taylor was a bit of a revelation. Taylor finished with 78 yards on 22 carries which was highlighted by strong running on the team’s opening drive of the second half and a late touchdown rush. His 32 yards to start the second half led to the team’s first touchdown to Hunter Long. Later, Taylor was rewarded by rushing in the two-point conversion. Taylor then punched one in to help the Jags take the lead in the waning minutes of the fourth quarter. The rookie stepped up and did what he could to earn his roster spot. Fun fact- Long scored the team’s first touchdown of the regular season last year and now scored the team’s first touchdown of the following preseason. Do with that as you will. A solid day at the office for J'Mari Taylor! #JAXvsNO on FOX30 pic.twitter.com/0Mpwn3nHTb — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 15, 2026 LOSERS Pretty Much The Entire First Half I’m not sure that first half inspired any courage in the backups for the Jags. New Orleans almost housed the opening kickoff but scored on their first offensive play anyway. On that touchdown run for the Saints, linebacker Branson Combs absolutely whiffed on making a tackle, so that was cool. During Jacksonville’s first offensive possession, offensive tackle Chuma Edoga went down and didn’t return. With already little depth at that position, having Edoga hurt literally one play into the preseason isn’t exactly ideal. The rest of the first half didn’t get much better, as both Nick Mullens and Carter Bradley threw bad decision picks and the Saints tallied three sacks. At the halftime break, the Jaguar quarterbacks had a combined 53 yards. Zach Wilson of all people had 112 himself for the home team. The Jags also had a handful of drops and four penalties in that opening half. You really can’t script it much worse, outside of two Little field goals. A lot of those problems persisted in the second half as well with players even further down the depth chart, which you can only be so upset about. But the direct backups didn’t look sharp to start the preseason. Bucky Brooks Brooks didn’t seem to be having a lot of fun on the call against the Saints. He has seen far too much bad Jaguars football to be tormented like he was for the first half. I hope someone got that dude a hurricane after the game. He sounded like he needed a drink or five during that debacle. bucky brooks groaning every three minutes should tell you how this game is going — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) August 15, 2026 Let us know your thoughts on who you think was a winner and loser from Preseason Week One and come back next week as we discuss the ever exciting Carolina Panthers vs. Jaguars Preseason Week Two game on August 21.
author: Henry Zimmer

title: Jaguars Depth Fuels Comeback Win Over Saints
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars opened the preseason with a dramatic 24–20 win over the New Orleans Saints. After a difficult first half placed the team in a 20-6 halftime deficit, Jacksonville’s reserves found their rhythm after halftime and fueled a comeback. Penalties, drops, injuries, and early special team struggles ruled the early portion of the day. […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 14: Yasir Abdullah #56 of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates against the Cincinnati Bengals during the NFL 2025 game between Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars opened the preseason with a dramatic 24–20 win over the New Orleans Saints. After a difficult first half placed the team in a 20-6 halftime deficit, Jacksonville’s reserves found their rhythm after halftime and fueled a comeback. Penalties, drops, injuries, and early special team struggles ruled the early portion of the day. However, the Jaguars’ depth players made several key plays late, helping secure the victory and giving the team valuable insight into its roster competitions. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s 2026 Week 1 preseason 24-20 road opener against the New Orleans Saints. Pregame Notes: Both New Orleans Head Coach Kellen Moore and Jacksonville’s Liam Coen went the route of resting the majority of starters following Thursday’s joint practice. The majority of key veterans sat out this one, namely: WR Chris Olave WR Jordyn Tyson (reportedly with a hamstring injury suffered Thursday) WR Devaughn Vele Edge Cam Jordan For Jacksonville, who was active, was probably the more notable list Saturday, with Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs both participating, as both players compete for a starting linebacker role. Game Recap First Half Today’s game kicked off with an immediate explosive surrendered by the Jacksonville kickoff coverage team and defense, allowing an opening 86-yard kick return to Saints’ running back Ty Chandler. Jalen Husky completed the touchdown-saving tackle, though only delaying the later touchdown. WHEELS 🔥 #Saints | 📺: FOX-8 pic.twitter.com/r8wTEHiTJX — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 15, 2026 On the following play, the Saints completed the drive with a nine-yard touchdown run with no less than three missed tackles from the Jacksonville defense from Branson Combs, Jabbar Muhammad, and others. First TD of the #Saints season 🙌 #Saints | 📺: FOX-8 pic.twitter.com/JDpfsyTMxT — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 15, 2026 The following drive featured multiple impressive runs by the Jaguars’ offense from DeeJay Dallas and J’Mari Taylor, and first down conversions from both CJ Williams and Josh Cameron. However, it was all for naught, with Nick Mullens throwing a red-zone interception at the four-yard line. JAYLAN FORD INT! #Saints | 📺: FOX-8 pic.twitter.com/PwzJhQKFki — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 15, 2026 The Jacksonville defense bounced back with a quick three-and-out following a Bransom Combs/BJ Green quarterback pressure of Saints backup Spencer Rattler, resulting in a Ruke Orhorhoro sack to force the punt. Unfortunately, Jacksonville’s backup offense could do little on the ensuing drive, punting it back to New Orleans following their own three-and out, with Mullens sacked on third-and-five. Following another Saints three-and-outs and a Cam Little 54-yard field goal, the Jacksonville defense forced a quick turnover courtesy of Yasir Abdullah. B.J. Green II recovers the fumble for the @Jaguars 🏈 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H2PyH6mMVV — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 The backup Sam linebacker pressured Spencer Rattler, missed the sack, then circled back, turning the missed tackle into a forced red zone fumble, with Wesley Williams. The fumble was recovered by BJ Green who returned the possession to the seven-yard line. Jacksonville added another field goal to cut the Saints’ lead to 1. The New Orleans backups put together a 15-play, 57-yard field goal drive to extend the drive, with both teams trading punts. Following a second first-half false start by Jimto Obidegwu, Carter Bradley forced an ill-advised throw to CJ Williams, resulting in a Saints interception returned to the 28-yard line. The Saints scored two plays later via a first-down, play-action busted coverage from the Jacksonville secondary, followed by a one-yard rub route on the goal line where Ray Lane was unable to beat Delp to the goal line. Following a punt by Jacksonville, New Orleans targeted backup cornerback Corey Ballentine for multiple explosive plays on a 9-play, 84-yard, 1:02 field goal drive to close out the half. Saints 20, Jaguars 6 at halftime Second Half A rough first half for the Jacksonville offense led by Nick Mullens and Carter Bradley resulted in seven possessions with a combined six first downs. However, following the break in action, the team showed signs of life, with an impressive opening drive 10-play, 79-yard, 6:07 touchdown drive. With multiple explosive receptions by Chanler Brayboy and two explosive rushes via J’Mari Taylor, the team moved into the Saints’ red zone. The drive was capped by a 1-yard Hunter Long touchdown catch (and two-point conversion by Taylor) to cut the Saints’ lead to six. Following a missed 52-yard field goal by New Orleans, Bradley led Jacksonville down the field for what looked to be a go-ahead drive, with Carter hitting Trebor Pena with an end zone strike. However, the ball was dropped, resulting in a Jacksonville field goal and a three-point New Orleans lead. Jacksonville would eventually secure their first lead of the game with 4:55 remaining in the matchup, via a two-yard J’Mari Taylor rush, following a 43-yard Trebor Pena reception. An exciting finish to the game ensued as the Saints offense drove to the Jaguars’ 2-yard line with 1 second remaining on the clock, as Jabbar Muhammad deflected the games’ final pass attempt to secure the Jacksonville victory. It’s a 1 and 0 Victory Monday in Duval. Jabbar Muhammad with a CLUTCH PBU 🙅‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/6F5g3PS9fh — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Biggest play of the game: Yasir Abdullah pressuring the quarterback? Wesley Williams forcing the fumble? BJ Green recovering the fumble? A great team effort! Stay with the play! #JAXvsNO on FOX30 pic.twitter.com/BCMsKv2lQn — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 15, 2026 Favorite highlight: The Jaguars keep fighting, taking the lead with 4:55 remaining in the fourth quarter J'Mari Taylor powers it in for the TD 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VlV72BrEXy — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Notable performances : QB Nick Mullens: 3/7 for 33-yards (4.7 YPC), no TDs, 1 INT, sacked once (17.9 passer rating) RB J’Mari Taylor: 22 carries for 78-yards (3.5 YPC), TD, with a long of 13 WR CJ Williams: 2 receptions for 28-yards, 14.0 YPR, on five targets DL Ruke Ohrhorhoro: 3 tackles, 0.5 sacks DE Danny Striggow: 3 tackles, 1 solo, 0.5 sacks LB Yasir Abdullah: 2 solo tackles, 1 sack DT Albert Regis: 1 QB sack View the full box score here Game balls: Special Teams: Jalen Huskey Two special teams tackles (three total), including a hustling TD-saving one to open the game Defense: Yasir Abdullah A QB pressure, two solo tackles, a sack with fumble forced on the play (Wesley Williams’ assist) Offense: RB J’Mari Taylor Taylor looked impressive early on with just seven tough carries in the first half for 20-yards. However, following the half, his box score production quickly ramped to match the on-field vision and drive, ending the day with 22 carries for 78-yards (3.5 YPC), and a touchdown. Injuries: As a note, the following Jacksonville players left Sunday’s game due to injury: OL Chuma Edoga The Jaguars’ veteran depth offensive lineman left the field of play on the opening offensive play and did not return. Live blog: Catch up on all the big plays and best moments from Saturday’s game in our live blog ! What are your notables from Saturday’s game, Jaguars fans? Who surprised you most or disappointed you with their play? Let us know in the comments.

title: Andy Reid gives single Chiefs injury update after preseason Week 1
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs dropped their preseason opener to the Los Angeles Rams 20-12 on Saturday. Frustrating as even exhibition losses can be, most NFL fans know that player health can be the most important indicator of a successful preseason contest. With one exception, the Chiefs seemed to come out of Saturday’s game healthy. In […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Chukwuebuka Godrick #72 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs dropped their preseason opener to the Los Angeles Rams 20-12 on Saturday. Frustrating as even exhibition losses can be, most NFL fans know that player health can be the most important indicator of a successful preseason contest. With one exception, the Chiefs seemed to come out of Saturday’s game healthy. In the fourth quarter, international tackle Chu Godrick was announced as questionable to return due to an ankle injury . After the loss, Godrick was the only injured player head coach Andy Reid highlighted. “As far as injuries go,” the coach began, “really, it was just Chu Godrick had an ankle sprain. Other than that, there were no other injuries.” Encouragingly, Reid did not mention rookie Jadon Canady. Canady briefly entered the medical tent in the fourth quarter before returning to the game. Per Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest , the following players did not dress for Saturday’s game due to injury: wide receiver Jimmy Holiday (undisclosed), right guard Trey Smith (hip) and linebacker Drue Tranquill (back). Defensive backs Chamarri Conner, Kader Kohu and L’Jarius Sneed all missed the contest due to knee injuries. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the active/physically-unable-to-perform list and has not yet participated in training camp practices. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes, tight end Travis Kelce, wide receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, cornerback Mansoor Delane, pass rusher Ashton Gillotte and newly signed defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah were dressed on the sideline but did not enter the game. Several other players had short workloads. Running back Kenneth Walker exited the game after the first offensive snap. The starting offensive line of tackles Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore, guards Kingsley Suamataia and Kahlil Benson and center Creed Humphrey were replaced after the first offensive possession. On defense, defensive tackle Chris Jones played only the first defensive snap. Defensive end George Karlaftis and linebacker Nick Bolton left the game during the first defensive series.

summary: The rookies headlined the Kansas City Chiefs’ 20-12 preseason-opening loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 15: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Cyrus Allen (13) runs the ball during the first half against the Los Angeles Rams on August 15th at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The rookies headlined the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 20-12 preseason-opening loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid acknowledged that as he opened his post-game press conference “We were able to get a good look at some of our young guys,” Reid told local media. “I thought there was some real production on both sides of the ball from the young guys.” Rookie running back Emmett Johnson led the team in rushing, but wide receiver Cyrus Allen made a lot of noise with just two catches for 20 yards. He stood out in training camp for having chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes, but he was a reliable target for the backup quarterbacks on Saturday as well. This guy sure doesn't play like a rookie… pic.twitter.com/LeLd962yEI — Arrowhead Pride (@ArrowheadPride) August 15, 2026 “He has been doing well in camp,” Reid said about Allen. “[It] looked like he picked right up from there. I thought he did a nice job for the most part there on catching the football and route running; he has some quickness to him. [We] look forward to getting him fully healthy and ready to go.” Early on, Allen caught a third pass for a chains-moving run after the catch from quarterback Justin Fields that showed off his elusiveness. The play was called back for offensive pass interference by teammate Jalen Royals, but Allen’s movement is a clear differentiator from the rest of the group, whether it’s before or after the pass gets to him. “He has a good feel, and he has good quickness,” Reid described Allen. “He knows how to set routes up, which sometimes takes a while for young guys to learn, but he has a good feel for that.” Cyrus Allen told me, "My biggest pet peeve is not to be open." — Sam McDowell (@SamMcDowell11) August 15, 2026 The fifth-round rookie wideout looks like a veteran on the field, and has since training camp started. Aside from going up and securing a high pass from quarterback Garrett Nussmeier, he also secured a pass low and away from a defender in tight coverage earlier in that drive. With the fourth spot in the Chiefs’ receiving corps up for grabs, Allen has done everything he can to stand out from the competition of Royals, Nikko Remigio and others.

title: Final Score: Rams defeat Chiefs 20-12 in NFL Preseason Week 1
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost the first preseason game of the 2026 campaign to the Los Angeles Rams by a score of 20-12. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson led the Chiefs in rushing with 59 yards over 12 attempts, while seventh-round pick rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier completed 13 of 19 passes for 98 yards. Second-year […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Place kicker Harrison Butker #7 of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a second quarter field goal during the NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost the first preseason game of the 2026 campaign to the Los Angeles Rams by a score of 20-12. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson led the Chiefs in rushing with 59 yards over 12 attempts, while seventh-round pick rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier completed 13 of 19 passes for 98 yards. Second-year tight end Jake Briningstool led Chiefs receivers with 29 receiving yards over three receptions. Third-year safety Jaden Hicks led the defense with seven total tackles and added a pass breakup to stop an early drive in the red zone. Kicker Harrison Butker was the only scorer of the day for Kansas City, making all four of his field-goal attempts. First Quarter The Chiefs’ defense opened the game by forcing a three-and-out, capped by a third-down pass breakup from Nohl Williams. Kansas City’s offense picked up a quick first down on a pass from Justin Fields to Brashard Smith, but the drive stalled after an offensive pass interference penalty on Jalen Royals. The Rams moved 73 yards on their second possession before the Chiefs’ defense tightened up inside the 10-yard line. Safety Jaden Hicks broke up a third-down pass in the end zone, forcing Los Angeles to settle for a field goal. Taking an early 3-0 lead. On the Chiefs’ next possession, Fields connected with Armstrong for 17 yards, picking up another early first down. Once again, a penalty put Kansas City behind the sticks, eventually leading to another punt. Second Quarter The Chiefs’ defense opened the second quarter with another three-and-out. Felix Anudike-Uzomah created pressure off the edge that resulted in a holding penalty, which Kansas City declined before the Rams punted. Kansas City turned to rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier, who got the offense moving. A holding penalty wiped out a touchdown run from rookie running back Emmett Johnson, forcing the Chiefs to settle for a Harrison Butker field goal to tie the game 3-3. Rookie quarterback Ty Simpson used a couple of rollout passes to move the chains for Los Angeles. Safety Jaden Hicks helped halt the drive with a tackle for loss followed by a quick tackle on a short completion. Harrison Mevis connected on a 40-yard field goal to give the Rams a 6-3 lead. Nussmeier responded with another productive drive, connecting with Cyrus Allen for 10 yards, Johnson for 11 and finding Jake Briningstool on a well-executed tight end screen. Butker finished the drive with a 35-yard field goal, sending the game into halftime tied 6-6. Third Quarter The Chiefs came out of the halftime break and quickly went three-and-out. After giving up an 11-yard run on the second play of the Rams’ ensuing possession, Kansas City’s defense settled in and forced a punt after three short gains. The Chiefs leaned completely on the running game on their next possession, handing the ball off 11 times for 54 yards without attempting a pass. Kansas City lined up to go for it on fourth-and-1, but a false start by Hunter Nourzad pushed the offense back. Harrison Butker came on and drilled a 59-yard field goal to give the Chiefs a 9-6 lead. The Rams opened their next possession with a holding penalty, and the Chiefs’ defense took advantage of the setback to force a quick three-and-out. Fourth Quarter The Chiefs opened the drive by giving up a 13-yard sack. Facing third-and-21, Nussmeier took a deep shot downfield that fell through the arms of Jason Brownlee. The Rams followed the drop with a 40-yard punt return to the Chiefs’ 23-yard line. Los Angeles quickly took advantage of the short field, with Ty Simpson finding Dean Connors for a 9-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 13-9 lead early in the fourth quarter. Chris Oladokun took over at quarterback, and his first pass was initially ruled an interception before replay assist overturned the call. Oladokun followed with a 15-yard scramble, but the drive eventually stalled and Kansas City punted. Simpson came back out firing, completing passes of 22, 13, 23 and 16 yards before connecting with Connors for his second touchdown of the game, extending the Rams’ lead to 20-9. Oladokun answered with a productive drive of his own, including completions of 13 and 27 yards to running back Jaydn Ott. The drive stalled at the Rams’ 8-yard line, and Harrison Butker connected from 26 yards to cut the deficit to 20-12. After Kansas City’s onside kick attempt failed, Rams running back Jordan Waters broke off a 26-yard run before Los Angeles finished the game with a series of kneel-downs. Special teams notes Kicker Harrison Butker made all four of his field-goal attempts, including a 59-yard kick. Punter Matt Araiza landed three of his five punts inside the 20-yard line. Rookie running back E.J. Smith had a notable kick return that gained 30 yards. Wide receiver Nikko Remigio led all punt returners with a 19-yard gain on an early punt.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Rams’ Winners & Losers: Ty Simpson is bringing the future
summary: Ty Simpson was pinpoint accurate in his debut for the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, as the first-round pick led his team to a 20-12 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. Starter Stetson Bennett got just two drives to open the game before leading to Simpson, a potential glimpse into the future and the rest […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams passes as defensive end Vincent Anthony Jr. #98 of the Kansas City Chiefs defends during the preseason game at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ty Simpson was pinpoint accurate in his debut for the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, as the first-round pick led his team to a 20-12 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. Starter Stetson Bennett got just two drives to open the game before leading to Simpson, a potential glimpse into the future and the rest was history. But Simpson’s gain was definitely Bennett’s loss. Presume to be Matthew Stafford’s backup in Week 1, Bennett was so obviously outshined by the rookie that many will loudly question if Sean McVay has the right depth chart. Did Simpson surpass Bennett in only one game? There was definitely one winner and one loser among them. There is more to come on Simpson, as well as all encouraging and discouraging performances by Rams players that came out of this game. Welcome to the first “Rams winners & losers” of the 2026 season. Winners Ty Simpson, QB The Rams’ offense was far from high-flying with Simpson under center. However, we always knew it would be . The preseason environment is tough on reserve quarterbacks. Teams across the NFL can barely field five competent offensive linemen. Their backups are even worse. Simpson effectively played with third stringers and still did not take a single sack in credit to his mobility. And while things weren’t necessarily dynamic or amazing, Simpson checked every single box someone could realistically want from him. Mobility? We saw it and he made some impressive throws on the move. Accuracy? Check. Arm strength? On display. Poise? We saw a whole lot of it. 120 seconds of Ty Simpson slicing thru the defense 21/25, 190 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs thoughts? pic.twitter.com/Aj7B2M1hs3 — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) August 15, 2026 The moment simply did not look too big for the rookie quarterback. He understands that if all goes according to plan that he won’t see the field in the regular season. This was his time to reward the Rams for their leap of faith by taking him in the first round and showing fans what they have to look forward to in life after Matthew Stafford. Simpson completed 21 of 25 passes (84%) for 190 yards and two scores. Of his four completions; (1) he was hit on a hail mary attempt one second before the end of the first half, (2) was a throwaway out the back of the end zone on an RPO, (3) there was a drop mixed in, and (4) a pass was batted at the line of scrimmage. I can’t remember a single errant throw from Simpson on Saturday. He was the definition of under control. It’s a fair criticism that the training wheels were on and the offense overall was dink and dunk. However, that changed late into the second half and Simpson started airing the ball out. He got better as the game went on. Two preseason contests remain to assess his abilities. If he continues this trajectory, the Rams are in good hands long term. Shaun Dolac, LB Davis Allen, TE Sometimes the most telling thing the Rams can do is not subject an individual player to the preseason. That was the case for both of Dolac and Allen in this game. Dolac was a mainstay in the exhibition games a year ago—now he was dressed in street clothes and watching from the sidelines. Allen was probably always safe. He was listed as a co-starter in the team’s recently released unofficial depth chart . Fans have been skeptical of whether he becomes the odd-man out after the second-round draft selection of Max Klare. Saturday was confirmation that both are effectively locks to man the 53-man roster. Dean Connors, RB Much is made of Jarquez Hunter being LA’s fastest running back. Connors looked like he was moving at a completely different speed. The rookie UDFA ran six times for 22 yards (3.7 average) with a long of 11. He also caught all four of his targets for 29 yards and two touchdowns, including one on a screen play from Simpson. It sure seems that Connors should be moved up the depth chart and competing with Hunter rather than being the last on the field. Ty Simpson throws a dart to Dean Connors for the touchdown. LARvsKC on @NFLnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8hOWM5GIRT — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Nick Andersen, DB Similar to Connors, Andersen could have been the best athlete to step onto the field for the defense Saturday. He broke up a team-leading two passes and also led the unit it tackles with eight. He made a tackle for loss on the first drive of the game while the Chiefs played NFL veterans and key role players. The Rams have a lot of depth at safety and Andersen has an uphill battle to make the team. Still, if LA is serious about improving on special teams, then this seems like someone they should entertain keeping for that purpose. Brennan Presley, WR Presley was one of the Rams’ more effective preseason receivers a year ago. He was the most consistently productive pass catcher again on Saturday with multiple long runs after the catch. Xavier Smith was the primary punt returner. Why not see if Presley could contribute in this fashion as well? Presley did return kicks later in the game and did fine in this role. Presley caught all four of his targets for a team-leading 58 yards. Ty Simpson zips it to Brennan Presley for a 23-yard pick up. LARvsKC on @NFLnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NomnCI9rqT — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Losers Jarquez Hunter, RB If you were waiting for Hunter’s breakout moment it never came. He did break an 11-yard run on a sweep. It’s a sign of where Hunter stands that Ronnie Rivers did not see the field. This is not an automatic death kiss for the second-year running back. Rivers is a veteran that has plenty of preseason experience. There simply may not be much more to learn with Rivers and that could be the reason why LA held him out. Or Hunter is already buried behind Rivers and could be looking for a new team in a couple of weeks. He didn’t show enough to change his trajectory. Max Klare, TE Max Klare is not on the “losers” list because of performance. He was Simpson’s favorite target and caught seven passes for 37 yards. He looked the part as a second-round pick. But Klare was playing late into the game. He could realistically be on the same development program as Simpson—meaning that if all goes according to plan we won’t see much of the rookie in the regular season. That is a somewhat disappointing outcome given his draft status. Stetson Bennett, QB Ty Simpson looks a whole step above Stetson Bennett to me. — RamsActive (@ramsactive) August 15, 2026 Bennett played only two drives but did not put much on tape to convince the Rams he deserves to be Stafford’s understudy. We’ve seen plenty of Bennett over the last four preseasons and he’s never touched the level we saw from Simpson. The backup quarterback competition may actually not be much of a battle after all. The Rams may just be slow playing Simpson’s development and making him earn the role. Adding a veteran, if the stars align, also makes sense. Desjuan Johnson, EDGE Similar to Klare, Johnson played well but ws still in the game late. He was a situational contributor for the defense last year. If the Rams thought he’d have that role again in 2026, he simply would not be on the field late into a preseason contest as he was. This is a concerning sign for someone who has done well since converting from the defensive interior.
author: JB Scott

title: Undrafted safety steals show for Rams against Chiefs
summary: While it would seem impossible to outshine quarterback Ty Simpson in his preseason debut, L.A. Rams safety Nick Andersen gave the first-round pick all the competition for attention that he could handle. Andersen, an undrafted rookie out of Wake Forest, has made an outstanding case to make the Rams 53-man roster after his debut performance […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Safety Nick Andersen #45 of the Los Angeles Rams breaks up a pass intended for wide receiver Jason Brownlee #89 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the 2nd half of the preseason game at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images While it would seem impossible to outshine quarterback Ty Simpson in his preseason debut, L.A. Rams safety Nick Andersen gave the first-round pick all the competition for attention that he could handle. Andersen, an undrafted rookie out of Wake Forest, has made an outstanding case to make the Rams 53-man roster after his debut performance in Saturday’s 20-12 win over the Kansas City Chiefs. That pass defense from Nick Andersen 😮‍💨 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYp8K pic.twitter.com/zwFdf8U43b — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 15, 2026 A five-year letterman for the Demon Deacons, Andersen appeared in 57 games over five seasons, totaling an incredible 228 tackles over the past two seasons alone as a starter. Andersen, who was first-team All-ACC in 2025, had eight career interceptions at Wake Forest, including four as a true freshman in 2020. He set a school record with 27 passes defended, and he had a couple of more in his NFL debut. Standing 5’11, weighing 197 lbs, Andersen was anything but “highly touted” going into the 2025 draft. In fact, you’re more likely to come across a draft profile for “Nick Anderson” with an o instead of an e than you are to find information about L.A.‘s breakout star on Saturday. Andersen had four tackles, but was flying around the field and seen everywhere from behind the line of scrimmage to breaking up passes 40 yards downfield. Had to look up Nick Andersen,played at WF… should be a key special teamer + backup safety. That PBU on that potential KC TD was impressive af. Great effort. #RamsHouse — Kung Fu Kenny (@MSBred93) August 15, 2026 His best shot to make the Rams will be as a special teamer. The Rams are not likely to give Andersen much run on defense this season, but he was surprisingly athletic at his pro day, just not when it comes to speed. Also in the defensive back room, Nick Andersen showcased his athleticism. His 35-inch vertical, 10-foot-1 broad jump, 6.82 three-cone and 17 bench reps reinforced what he believes already shows up every Saturday. “A lot of people are fast,” Andersen said. “But are you fast on the football field?” Andersen was one of the more productive players in Wake Forest history over his career, finishing eighth all-time in program history with 368 tackles. It’s not easy to stand out in a preseason game when you weren’t on anyone’s radar the morning of, but somehow Anderson comes out looking as good as any Rams player who wasn’t drafted in the top-15 picks.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams-Chiefs preseason final score: Ty Simpson leads L.A. to win in NFL debut
summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Kansas City Chiefs by a final score of 20-9 in their first preseason game of 2026, as rookie quarterback Ty Simpson led the way with two touchdown passes to running back Dean Connors. It was a low-scoring affair for about three quarters, until the Rams pulled away after Simpson […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams scrambles during the third quarter in an NFL preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams beat the Kansas City Chiefs by a final score of 20-9 in their first preseason game of 2026, as rookie quarterback Ty Simpson led the way with two touchdown passes to running back Dean Connors. It was a low-scoring affair for about three quarters, until the Rams pulled away after Simpson caught fire in the second half. Simpson went 21-of-25 for 190 yards, along with those two touchdowns, and no interceptions. The running back room as a whole looked solid on Saturday, a credit to the blocking of L.A.s third unit offensive line, but it was Simpson and Connors who really put the game out of reach. 21/25, 190 passing yards, 2 touchdowns. A great start to the Preseason for @RamsNFL rookie QB @ty_simpson06 . pic.twitter.com/QgkzQleVcl — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Stetson Bennett got the start Fourth-year quarterback Bennett, vying to prove himself worthy of the backup role behind Matthew Stafford, went 4-6 for 38 yards. But it was Simpson who starred, as Sean McVay clearly wants to give his rookie ample opportunity to gain experience in an NFL environment. And the results were quite good. Even of the play calling was largely vanilla, Simpson continuously executed and gave his receivers a chance to make plays after the catch, opening up on couple throws late in the game to fellow rookies Max Klare and CJ Daniels. Simpson looked and played like the best quarterback on the field on Saturday, for the Rams. Rams defense against KC backups L.A.’s defense held their ground against Justin Fields and Garrett Nussmeier, holding the Chiefs to a few field goals and keeping Kansas City out of the end zone, with the help of a couple penalties. The standout of the day was Rams safety Nick Andersen. That pass defense from Nick Andersen 😮‍💨 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYp8K pic.twitter.com/zwFdf8U43b — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 15, 2026 The former Wake Forest standout has made a strong case to make L.A.’s final roster as secondary depth and special teams starter. Speaking of special teams, playoffs scapegoat Xavier Smith had a nice showing in the return game, while Ethan Evans got his punts off without a hitch and Harrison Mevis made his kicks with 2 field goals and 2 extra points. It’s preseason, so we aren’t seeing best on best, but you can only play who is in front of you, and by the end of the game, the Rams were playing well in front of their opponent. L.A. came away from this game looking good. They have two more preseason games to tune up, and then it’s the real thing. Always room for improvement, but so far for the Rams and Simpson, so good.

title: Rams-Chiefs preseason Week 1 game thread
summary: The Los Angeles Rams travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs for some preseason Week 1 NFL action. This game will not be Matthew Stafford vs. Patrick Mahomes. That should come later in the regular season. This game will apparently feature some Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson, so there’s a lot to watch for […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett IV (13) warms up prior to a game against the Kansas City Chiefs at at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Los Angeles Rams travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs for some preseason Week 1 NFL action. This game will not be Matthew Stafford vs. Patrick Mahomes. That should come later in the regular season. This game will apparently feature some Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson, so there’s a lot to watch for Rams fans on Saturday. Similar to the Rams, the Chiefs also may be rolling out some quarterbacks that KC and other NFL teams will want to see . You never know which of these players will make a strong enough impression to stick with their current roster or find themselves with a real chance to play elsewhere. For the Rams, their QB situation is seemingly still being figured out as far as who will be the official backup to the Matthew Stafford in 2026. There is a chance that the true backup for 2026 isn’t on the roster, yet. However, Bennett and Simpson should get the chance to show they are ready starting against the Chiefs. Now, it’s preseason, so take it with a grain of salt, but all you can do is play in the situation you are in, and though it’s preseason, it’s assumed that Bennett and Simpson will want to play well. That aside, if you are going to make mistakes, make your mistakes in practice and in preseason, and learn from them. So, will we learn anything from this matchup? Both teams and fanbases should learn something, but will those lessons learned impact the regular season? We don’t know yet. Either way, enjoy today’s game. This will be the only game thread, so hang out here as long as you’d like! Comment away! And know that we are getting closer and closer to live NFL action.

title: Rams-Chiefs preseason: Keys to victory
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will open their 2026 preseason schedule Saturday afternoon against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. The game is scheduled for August 15 at 4 p.m. ET, and with the Rams expected to keep their starters on the sideline, the focus will be less about the final score […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will open their 2026 preseason schedule Saturday afternoon against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. The game is scheduled for August 15 at 4 p.m. ET, and with the Rams expected to keep their starters on the sideline, the focus will be less about the final score and more about evaluating the players fighting for roster spots. Preseason games are about competition, development and establishing depth. For the Rams, there are several keys that could determine whether they walk away from Kansas City with a win—and, more importantly, whether they come away with positive answers heading into the rest of August. These might not be the most elaborate keys to victory against Kansas City, but sometimes we don’t need to get lost in the details when its only a preseason game… 1. Get Consistent Quarterback Play With the starters expected to sit, the quarterback competition becomes one of the biggest storylines. Ty Simpson has been confirmed as part of the Rams’ preseason plans, while Stetson Bennett’s status has been less certain. Whoever receives the majority of the snaps needs to demonstrate command of the offense. That means getting the team into the right plays, avoiding turnovers, and consistently moving the chains. The Rams don’t need spectacular quarterback play. They need efficient quarterback play. 2. Win the Line of Scrimmage This game could be decided by players who won’t necessarily receive much attention during the regular season. The Rams need their backup offensive linemen to protect the quarterback and create running lanes. On defense, the young defensive linemen and edge rushers need to establish themselves against Kansas City’s offensive line. Preseason games are often won by the teams that control the trenches. If the Rams can consistently generate pressure while keeping their own quarterbacks upright, they’ll put themselves in position to control the game. The offensive line will likely feature AJ Arcuri, Wyatt Bowles, Dylan McMahon, Beaux Limmer, and Keagen Trost. There is some NFL starting experience with that group so their should be some expectation for the offense. 3. Create Turnovers Mistakes will happen. It’s preseason football. The Rams just need to be on the winning side of those turnovers when they happen. The Rams’ defense has plenty of young and developing players who need opportunities to make plays. One of the easiest ways for backups to separate themselves is by creating turnovers. A strip-sack, interception, or fumble recovery could dramatically change the game while also giving a player valuable momentum heading into the next preseason matchup. The Rams don’t need their defense to unveil everything Sean McVay and the coaching staff have planned for the regular season. They simply need to play fast, tackle well and take advantage of mistakes. 4. Special Teams Special teams could be one of the most important areas of the game. Players competing for roster spots need to show they can contribute outside of their primary position. Coverage units, returners and specialists will all have opportunities to make an impression. For a fringe roster player, one excellent special teams performance can be the difference between making the roster and becoming a practice-squad candidate. In addition, the Rams need to get off on the right foot with their kicking game. Harrison Mevis returns this year as the starting place kicker and needs to make sure there are no question marks as the team enters the regular season.

title: Rookie pass catchers have major opportunity in preseason opener
summary: If you’ve been waiting to see Max Klare and C.J. Daniels take the field for the Los Angeles Rams, your wait is finally almost over. With a slew of Rams expected to sit out the preseason opener against the Kansas City Chiefs Saturday, younger potential contributors will get a chance to shine. Klare and Daniels, […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 31: Max Klare #86 of the Los Angeles Rams practices during the Los Angeles Rams Training Camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’ve been waiting to see Max Klare and C.J. Daniels take the field for the Los Angeles Rams, your wait is finally almost over. With a slew of Rams expected to sit out the preseason opener against the Kansas City Chiefs Saturday, younger potential contributors will get a chance to shine. Klare and Daniels, two draft picks who have generated plenty of intrigue this offseason, will be at the top of the list of the most interesting players actually taking the field. Klare may need the reps as much as any Rams skill-position player, if for no other reason than the fact his position room is arguably the deepest on the whole roster. Los Angeles will use plenty of tight ends this season, but with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson and Davis Allen already ahead of him on the depth chart, playing time will likely be scarce this year barring injury or an extreme showing in the lead-up to Week 1. Still, there’s a reason the Rams spent a Day 2 pick on Klare this year. He was a productive player at both Ohio State and Purdue, and he’s got obvious receiving upside, even if he’s not your prototypical in-line, blocking “Y” tight end. It can’t possibly hurt his quest for playing time if he shows out against the Chiefs (or New Orleans Saints or Los Angeles Chargers after that). Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, Davis Allen, and now – meet Max Klare! Ahead of his preseason debut, the Rams No. 61 overall pick catches up with @DarrenMHaynes , and let's us know how much sleep he'll really get tonight! 😴 #RamsHouse | @CBSLosAngeles pic.twitter.com/pOqLfEHPyv — Sports Central LA (@SportsCentralLA) August 15, 2026 Daniels is currently listed as a third-stringer on the Rams’ depth chart, unsurprisingly so, but the rookie from Miami has been turning heads since he first got to the team facility. He’s an older rookie at 24 years old, but he brings decent size to the field at 6-foot-2 and 197 pounds (one inch taller and seven pounds lighter than Davante Adams, for comparison) and has a well-rounded skill set that complements the star receivers, Adams and Puka Nacua, well. One of the biggest talking points of the offseason regarding the Rams’ roster and depth has been the third receiver spot. While Jordan Whittington is a fine option for the role and Konata Mumpfield is also ahead on the depth chart for now, Daniels’s upside offers a tantalizing prospect for an L.A. offense that’s always looking for more firepower. He might not leap into a true backup role just on the back of his preseason performances, but this is a chance for him to show why a player with his ceiling deserves more opportunities when the games really matter. Playing like he belongs. 🎥 @tae15adams on @cjaaaay_ 's progress throughout training camp. pic.twitter.com/9nXAYoaCIk — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 2, 2026 Of course, this won’t be an exact replica of what we could see from Klare and Daniels if the offense was at full strength. Matthew Stafford and the other main offensive weapons almost certainly won’t see any action Saturday or throughout the preseason. Even Sean McVay is taking a backseat . That actually offers an interesting dynamic for the passing game, since these two pass catchers will try to shine and break through the heavy traffic in front of them on the depth chart while getting targeted by Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson, two guys currently in the heat of the backup quarterback battle. It goes without saying that there’s a lot riding on the passing attack over the next few weeks. But this is why these games do matter. These are valuable snaps and moments for guys who may not be on the roster bubble but who will have limited chances to earn regular-season playing time. Pay close attention to Nos. 86 and 6 when the Rams face the Chiefs.

title: Ty Simpson is bothering Matthew Stafford, in all the right ways
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will get their first look at rookie quarterback Ty Simpson in a preseason game on Saturday and the 13th overall pick will have plenty to prove against the Kansas City Chiefs. Not just to fans, not just to skeptics, and not just to coaches, but also to himself. He would also […]

(Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams will get their first look at rookie quarterback Ty Simpson in a preseason game on Saturday and the 13th overall pick will have plenty to prove against the Kansas City Chiefs. Not just to fans, not just to skeptics, and not just to coaches, but also to himself. He would also probably like to prove something to Rams starter Matthew Stafford. Simpson noted this week that he “bothers” Matthew Stafford a lot , but that’s what he should be doing in what could be his only season behind the 2025 MVP. Shrugging with the self-awareness of a man who has learned that pride is the enemy of preparation, “I probably bother Matthew a lot,” Simpson admitted. “In a type of way to where he probably thinks I’m annoying. Sometimes I’m like, ‘All right, maybe that’s the one for tomorrow.’ But no, we actually talked this morning. He asked me, ‘Hey, how do you feel about the game and stuff?’ The best advice he gave me was just, man, go let it rip. It’s nothing that you haven’t done before.” The Rams play the Chiefs at 1 PM PT on Saturday, with Stetson Bennett getting the start and Simpson coming into the game sometime later. In a way, Bennett’s performance is more important. Can the Rams count on him as a backup? But all eyes will be on the rookie. Even Stafford’s. Here are Saturday’s pre-game links! “Simpson puts Rams first by being last” ( Sporting News ) He has not gotten the reps. Not the ones that matter. While Matthew Stafford — who has thrown for more than 50,000 career yards and delivered Los Angeles a championship — commands the huddle highlighted by Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Kyren Williams team, and Stetson Bennett — the former Georgia star who collected two national title rings — steadies the reps Stafford doesn’t, Simpson has been the third man in a two-man race, a voice without an echo, a student without a desk. But absence has taught him presence. “I’m not getting as many of the reps as Stetson and Matthew, so I want to make sure that I get those throws in that they got on the field,” Simpson said. “Not get caught up in just sitting around and not being locked in. I want to be locked in mentally and locked in physically as well.” Simpson “ready to show who I am” ( LA Times ) What do you expect to see from Ty Simpson on Saturday? The Rams don’t have a commitment from Donald, who remains retired after sitting out the past two seasons. Even if he comes back, Solak argued the 35-year-old should be viewed differently than the player who spent a decade wrecking game plans in Los Angeles .“ Will you be watching Rams-Chiefs preseason game? On Friday, I created a poll asking who will be watching the game. So far, it looks like more of the fans plan on watching the game! That’s great, and I hope you’ll check out our game thread! Rams Preseason Opener: Who Will Play and Who Won’t vs. Chiefs (si.com) “The Los Angeles Rams will play their first preseason game on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium against the Kansas City Chiefs. Here are the players who won’t play, might play, and will definitely play during the preseason, along with who to watch.“ 5 players to watch: Rams at Chiefs, 2026 Preseason Week 1 (therams.com) “Head coach Sean McVay talked about using the preseason to see how Simpson will respond to a pocket collapsing, and how he is “reacting and playing within (his) rules” while also playing instinctually. Saturday will be the first extended opportunity for him to showcase all of those things in a live game setting after working through them during Rams Training Camp. “I’m super excited,” Simpson said after practice on Thursday. “It’s the first time I get to play a game not only in a Rams uniform, but in an NFL uniform, and I’m just really ready to show just who I am.” Rams’ Ty Simpson is ready for his name to be called Saturday in preseason debut (ocregister) “In the Rams’ first-round draft pick’s recollection of events, throwing for just 73 passing yards and completing 5 of 9 attempts against USF, he wasn’t nearly as ready as he should have been. I was not as ready as I probably should have been and the team suffered for it,” Simpson said. “I look back on it as something that I have learned and told myself I wouldn’t do that again.” The 23-year-old signal caller’s place on the Rams is a rarity. title: Tre Tucker, Malik Benson as Raiders’ main return men is solid option
summary: Klint Kubiak and Rob Leonard aren’t the only Las Vegas Raiders play callers meticulously pouring over training camp practices, accompanying film, and previous year’s game tape to make key decisions on starters and overall depth. While the jobs of the head coach (and primary offensive play caller) and the defensive coordinator, respectively, tend to garner […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - AUGUST 03: Segun Olubi #50, Malik Benson #19 and Connor Heyward #34 of the Las Vegas Raiders practice during the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on August 03, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Klint Kubiak and Rob Leonard aren’t the only Las Vegas Raiders play callers meticulously pouring over training camp practices, accompanying film, and previous year’s game tape to make key decisions on starters and overall depth. While the jobs of the head coach (and primary offensive play caller) and the defensive coordinator, respectively, tend to garner most of the attention — as is the case with Kubiak and Leonard — special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis is slated to make critical choices, too. Similar to how the rookie head coach (Kubiak) and rookie defensive coordinator (Leonard) are deciding starters at important positions on offense and defense, the veteran special teams boss is charged with identifying the best options to bolster and breath life into a unit that face planted — hard — in 2025. DeCamillis is overseeing a lively kicker competition between veteran Matt Gay and undrafted rookie free agent Kansei Matsuzawa . Both have showcased accuracy and had bouts with misses recently in training camp practices and the battle is ongoing. However Matsuzawa hitting the upright on his lone field goal attempt against the Arizona Cardinals in the preseason opener coupled with not getting a kickoff attempt into the landing zone for a penalty isn’t the impression an undrafted rookie wants to deliver the coaching staff. Then, our Matt Holder not only called out another special teams competition, but hilariously gave me a shut out while doing so : The competition between Tyler Duzansky and Alex Ward for the long snapper spot. There’s also the long-dormant portion of the Raiders’ special teams: The return game. One of the promising signs of training camp practices in that regard is seeing explosive wide receivers veteran Tre Tucker and rookie Malik Benson cutting their teeth as kick and put returners. That duo, along with others competing for the gigs, can breath some life into a return game that hasn’t visited the end zone since the 2011 (Jacoby Ford’s 101-yard kickoff return on October 16) and 2018 (Dwayne Harris’ 99-yard punt return on December 24) seasons. The main kick and punt returners at #Raiders training camp continues to be Tre Tucker and rookie Malik Benson. pic.twitter.com/MaCOphbl6N — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) August 7, 2026 Veteran wide receiver Devin Thompkins got most of the work returning kicks in the Raiders 27-14 loss to the Cardinals in the preseason opener. The 26-year-old free-agent addition returned three kickoffs for 91 yards (30.3 average per return) with a long of 33. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. and Benson each field a kickoff and returned them for 22 and 21 yards, respectively. Thompkins also had the lone punt return for 10 yards. Tale of The Tape Tucker provides the most curious case in regards to the return duties competition. This is due to the fact he was a prolific kick returner during his collegiate career at Cincinnati — 67 total returns for 1,670 yards and two touchdowns; season high in 2021 with 22 returns for 557 yards and a score — and it was a logical assumption when the Raiders made the wideout their third-round pick (100th overall) in the 2023 NFL Draft, Tucker would get his fair share of opportunities to do that job in Las Vegas. Yet, in his three seasons in the league, Tucker’s career count reads: One kick return for 23 yards, and that lone statistical mark is from last season. It’s quite understandable why the 25-year-old’s participation rate in that particular department is near non-existent, when you consider Tucker being an integral part of the offense and limiting his exposure to potential injury is a prudent move. But unlike previous years, Las Vegas bolstered it’s explosiveness and speed at the wide receiver position by adding Jalen Nailor and Benson in free agency and the draft, respectively, and also having incumbents Dont’e Thornton Jr. and Shedrick Jackson on the 90-man roster. So there’s a window for Tucker to get more exposure in an element which he shined in college. Flip it to Benson and the Raiders’ sixth-round pick (195th overall) in the 2026 draft is impressing the coaching staff this offseason. Highlighted as one of the rookie risers in training camp with his explosiveness and electricity on offense and special teams, the 6-foot-1 and 195-pound Oregon product certainly has the juice to make an impact as a punt returner as he housed one of his nine returns last season for the Ducks (nine total for 161 yards and a score — an 85-yard scamper against USC ). That return showcased not only Benson’s timed speed (4.37 second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine) but how much of a smooth strider he is which makes it look effortless. “You saw the speed in college, and obviously, coming from college, I did see a little bit more of — there’s not a lot of great punters, and what he’s going to have to show us is he’s going to be able to catch an NFL punt, which is a lot different than a college punt, in my opinion,” DeCamillis qualified when asked about how Benson helps the return game. “So, that’s going to be where it’s at. But I mean, he’s got playmaking ability, he’s tough, he puts his head in there, and I’m excited to have the guy, for sure.” Malik Benson continues to flash. Aside from the Nailor TD, he had the highlight of practice: a leaping, acrobatic grab over Darien Porter on the left sideline. Worked with 1s, 2s and 3s today. A guy to watch in Thursday’s preseason opener. https://t.co/CHTqReGhQo — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) August 10, 2026 The Competition It’s highly plausible Tucker’s importance on offense outweighs the impact on special teams and if that occurs once again, reserve running back Dylan Laube and free-agent addition and wide receiver Dareke Young options for DeCamillis to man kick return duties. Laube, drafted in the sixth-round (208th overall) in the 2024 draft, paced Las Vegas with 33 kick returns for 855 yards (long of 38) last season. Young, on the other hand, is a Seattle Seahawk import and an imposing 6-foot-2 and 224 pound and made the most out of his limited opportunities returning kickoffs last season with 10 returns for 322 yards (long of 60). To maximize roster potential, Benson can mix in on kickoffs also Jackson, who clocked an impressive unofficial 4.25-second 40-yard dash at Maryland’s Pro Day back in 2023. And of course, Thompkins who received plenty of work on Thursday. Over on the punt return side, Tucker is mixing in with Benson but keep an eye out for Jermod McCoy, the Raiders’ fourth-round pick (101st overall) in the 2026 draft. A prospect with first-round talent that dropped in the draft due to concerns with a knee injury he suffered at Tennessee, McCoy has the explosiveness and athleticism to do the job — health permitting, of course. “Yeah, no question. We didn’t see that in spring because he wasn’t able to practice as much,” DeCamillis said when asked about McCoy as a punt returner. “He did have one today that looked good in that drill, so hopefully we can get him going because he’s definitely going to be a plus if we can get him out on the field for sure.

title: Raiders Mailbag: Can Fernando Mendoza win starting quarterback job in preseason?
summary: I hope everyone enjoyed Fernando Mendoza’s debut during Thursday night’s preseason game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Arizona Cardinals, as Raiders football is finally back! Despite the loss, it was good to see a few guys start to separate themselves or close the gap on the depth chart. That also gives us some actual […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders stands on the field during a break in the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images I hope everyone enjoyed Fernando Mendoza’s debut during Thursday night’s preseason game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Arizona Cardinals, as Raiders football is finally back! Despite the loss, it was good to see a few guys start to separate themselves or close the gap on the depth chart. That also gives us some actual ball to talk about for this week’s mailbag! Q: Can Fernando win the starting QB spot in the preseason? A: He definitely can! I’ve been saying for a while now that I think this competition is less about Mendoza versus Kirk Cousins and more centered around the rookie being ready to get thrown into the action, meaning Cousins’ performance is kind of irrelevant. The reports are that the veteran has been the better and more consistent quarterback so far in training camp, and he was solid against the Cardinals, going five-for-six with 50 yards and a touchdown on his only drive of the game. However, Mendoza played pretty well too, and we know that the plan is for him to take over at some point. After the game Friday morning, Klint Kubiak said that Mendoza is likely going to get reps with the starting offense moving forward. So, if he keeps playing well over the next couple of weeks, he could easily be the Week 1 starter. I still think Cousins is the favorite, but the door is certainly open for the No. 1 pick to win the job during the preseason. Q: I keep hearing about Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers competing for the starting right guard spot. I’m happy one of those high draft picks is in line to start, but does Spencer Burford have the left guard position completely locked up? Shouldn’t there be a three-man (or four if you add Trey Zuhn III) battle for both Guard positions? I’d love to see JPJ and Rogers starting, based on their draft positions. A: It certainly seems that way. Based on the training camp reports, Burford has taken all of the first-string left guard reps while Powers-Johnson and Rogers have been rotating on the right side. Also, for what it’s worth, Burford only played in the first series while Powers-Johnson got extra reps with the second-team offense and continued to split time with Rogers. I agree with you that it should be a three-man competition, and the ideal situation is that JPJ and Rogers are starting while Burford is a veteran backup. However, Kubiak and Co. don’t seem to agree with us, barring a shake-up during next week’s practices. As far as Zuhn goes, it looks like he’s in the mix more at right tackle. He’s been getting more reps there during practice and exclusively lined up at that spot during the first preseason game. Q: How does Zuhn look out there? He has great size (height) and athleticism, but short arms. Does it seem like he has the makeup (and extensive college experience) to be an OT? Isn’t OT more valuable than G? A: I’m not at training camp, so I don’t have any insights other than what’s been reported. It sounds like the coaching staff is training him to be as versatile as possible while simultaneously trying to determine what his best position is in the NFL. Zuhn has been spotted lining up at center, guard and tackle during camp. That sets up a situation where the team, at the least, has a competent backup who can fill in if any of the starters. That being said, he did play well at right tackle against the Cardinals, and personally, I think he has a better shot at sticking on the edge than playing inside. I worry about Zuhn’s lack of play strength at guard, and his athleticism is more beneficial at tackle since there’s more space involved in playing the latter position. And yes, generally speaking, a tackle is more valuable than a guard. Q: The Raiders seem to have a good number of decent players at CB and IOL. Do you see them making preseason cutdown trades to get something of value? Specifically thinking of guys like Jordan Meredith, Decameron Richardson and maybe even JPJ. A: I touched on Powers-Johnson being a trade candidate if he doesn’t win a starting job a couple of times this offseason ( here and here ), so that’s definitely on the table in my eyes. However, I think Rogers or even Meredith getting traded is less likely. Depth is too important at a position like offensive line, especially after last year’s debacle and the fact that the Raiders are going to have a young quarterback take over at some point. JPJ is just in a little different circumstance since he’s entering year three, which is viewed as the “make-or-break” season in the NFL. Plus, the current regime isn’t the one that drafted him, and he was a starter for the last two coaching staffs. Taking all of that into consideration, it wouldn’t surprise me if Powers-Johnson asks for a trade if he gets relegated to backup duties under Kubiak. Whereas Rogers was drafted by John Spytek and has one more year on his rookie contract than JPJ does, giving the current coaching staff more time to develop Rogers into a starter. Richardson, or one of the other corners on the roster bubble, is also a trade candidate. However, he’s going to have to have a strong showing during the next two preseason games after barely playing last year and missing Thursday’s contest for the birth of his child (congrats!) to have any significant trade value. There are a lot of variables at play, but if Richardson, Darien Porter, Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy are all ascending during camp, the math may not work out to keep all of them. Even if all are on the 53-man roster, only two outside cornerbacks are on the field at the same time, and Eric Stokes has one of those spots locked down. So, it’d make sense to flip one of the young corners for either a player who can fill another need or a draft pick. Q: I heard a podcaster say something to the effect of Treydan Stukes will probably be a safety now, but he’s the “slot CB of the future.” And I was kinda like… huh? What’s more valuable for team building, a Pro Bowl-level slot CB or a Pro Bowl Free Safety? A: It depends on the defense a team is running, and there can be some crossover between the two positions where a free safety can be in slot coverage at times. It seems like Kubiak wants Rob Leonard to run a variation of Mike Macdonald’s defense, which leans pretty heavily on a good nickelback. Think about how important Nick Emmanwori was to the Seahawks’ Super Bowl run, and he was lined up over the slot on 449 out of 944 total snaps last season, per Pro Football Focus . Granted, Emmanwori is the “big nickel” or strong safety type and barely lined up on the backend of Seattle’s defense. But the Seahawks’ best corner, Devon Witherspoon, had the second-most slot coverage snaps on the team last year to emphasize how important that role is in Macdonald’s defense. And to the point above about the crossover, third-most among the team’s defensive backs was free safety Coby Bryant. So, a good slot corner/nickelback carries more value in that system. But if we’re following the money, Alontae Taylor is the highest-paid pure nickel corner at about $19.3 million per year, per Over The Cap . That would barely crack the top five for safeties, with Derwin James ($25.2 million), Kyle Hamilton ($25.1 million), Kerby Joseph ($21.25 million), Antoine Winfield Jr. ($21 million) and Budda Baker ($18 million) leading the position. Granted, James is in slot coverage a lot, and Hamilton lines up all over the field. Those two are kind of in a class of their own, where they’re very unique in that they can do just about everything at a high level and are almost positionless. The other three safeties above are primarily backend defenders who can offer some value covering the slot, though. In other…

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Cian Slone #48 of the Las Vegas Raiders sacks Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter of the preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Part of what the NFL preseason is about is giving players on the roster bubble a chance to take center stage and make a name for themselves. That always includes several rookie undrafted free agents fighting to be one of the 53 men left standing at the end of training camp. The morning after the Las Vegas Raiders’ bout with the Arizona Cardinals, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked which UDFAs have stood out to him so far. Kubiak named three players: edge rusher Cian Slone and wide receivers Chase Roberts and E.J. Williams. “Cian [Slone] on defense has done some good stuff,” the coach said. “[At] the wide receiver position – we’ve got a few guys that have showed up between Chase [Roberts] and our and our young man from Indiana [E.J. Williams Jr.]. They got some good snaps [Thursday]. Overall, those are the kind of guys that come to mind.” To clarify, the question wasn’t specific to the Raiders’ first preseason game, so Kubiak was likely speaking more generally and about training camp as a whole. But all three did suit up and play against the Cardinals. Slone had a sack with a nice win around the edge and a couple of tackles against the run, while Williams hauled in a 41-yard catch that was Las Vegas’ second-most explosive play of the game. Roberts was quieter with just two targets, catching one of them for a 12-yard gain and dropping the other. As far as snap counts go, Pro Football Focus had Slone getting 21 on defense with Roberts recording 14 on offense and Williams with just seven. So, it sounds like those three are doing all the right things in camp to help their chances of making the team, as getting a shoutout from the head coach is a big accomplishment at this stage. In Other Raiders’ Links: Fernando Mendoza to get 1st team reps: “Friday morning, Kubiak said the coaching staff is working on a plan to get Mendoza more practice reps with the first-team offense,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “He did note that it’s important that all of the team’s quarterbacks get work with the first team. But it’s clear, Kubiak thinks Mendoza is ready for more challenges.” Treydan Stukes isn’t a run-of-the-mill safety: “It’s no secret that Stukes had a slow start to camp where he was relegated to second- and even third-team snaps,” via S&BP’s Ray Aspuria . “He’s ramped up first-team looks as of late but that shouldn’t be surprising. His hybrid role of nickel and safety positions is complex but he’s gaining confidence.” Dont’e Thornton Jr. expected to return: The wide receiver has missed several practices and the first preseason game with an injury, but Kubiak said he expects Thornton to return at some point during the preseason, via ESPN’s Ryan McFadden . Mysterious absence explained: Cornerback Decamerion Richardson surprisingly didn’t play on Thursday night, but it was for a good reason. Kubiak said Richardson had a baby, according to The Athletic’s Sam Warren . Congrats to the Richardsons!
