title: Minnesota Vikings 13, New York Giants 10: Vikings Get Win, But Injury Concerns Loom
summary: The Minnesota Vikings kicked off their 2026 preseason on Saturday afternoon, and they did not meet the primary goal of every preseason game, as they have a couple of potentially significant injury concerns that they are awaiting word on. Carson Wentz’s one-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price made the ultimate difference on the scoreboard, as […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 15: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a third quarter touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings during the pre-season game at MetLife Stadium on August 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings kicked off their 2026 preseason on Saturday afternoon, and they did not meet the primary goal of every preseason game, as they have a couple of potentially significant injury concerns that they are awaiting word on. Carson Wentz’s one-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price made the ultimate difference on the scoreboard, as the Vikings defeated the New York Giants by a final score of 13-10 at MetLife Stadium in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL preseason, but the greater concern is with safety Jamal Adams, who was carted off the field with what appears to be a significant non-contact leg injury . Quarterback Max Brosmer was also unable to finish the game for the Vikings as originally planned, as he was pulled after one series with what was reported to be an injury to his right wrist. The Vikings got the football first, with Kyler Murray leading the offense onto the field. All of the offensive starters, with the exception of Justin Jefferson, got onto the field for the Vikings, and they put together a decent drive. They established the run early, with both Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason getting a run for double-digit yardage on the drive. Jones had a run for 17 and Mason had one for 15. The drive stalled when a pass from Murray to Jones on a third down in the red zone fell incomplete, and Will Reichard connected on a 35-yard field goal to give the Vikings an early 3-0 lead. The Giants then took over for their first possession and managed to pick up one first down before their first possession ended, courtesy of a sack by Dallas Turner to end the drive. When the Vikings took the field on offense again, J.J. McCarthy brought them onto the field at quarterback. They went three-and-out after what looked to be a busted play on first down, a run from rookie Demond Claiborne, and an incomplete pass. The Giants took over again and put together a fairly long drive, and it looked to have stalled out on another sack, this one a huge hit on Jaxson Dart by Jay Ward that sent Dart to the medical tent temporarily. BIG FOOTBALL HITS ARE SO BACK. Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/11JOVdunxm — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 However, the Giants converted on a 3rd-and-23 on a screen play from Jameis Winston to Devin Singletary, and then a couple of plays later Dart returned and lofted a 15-yard touchdown pass to rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields to give the Giants a 7-3 lead just over a minute into the second quarter. It was on that play that Adams suffered the injury that sent him to the injury tent. After spending significant time in the tent, the call was ultimately made to bring the cart to the sideline and take him back to the locker room. Many of his teammates were seen comforting Adams on the sideline, and the initial reactions seemed to point to the injury being a fairly significant one, although no announcement had been made as to the nature or the severity of the injury by the time the game had concluded. We will bring you updates as soon as we have them. McCarthy and the Vikings took the field again after the Giants’ touchdown and pushed into New York territory, but a holding penalty and a false start helped to stall out the drive, and the Vikings were forced to punt. McCarthy also threw a 20-yard pass to Tai Felton that would have converted a first down and hit Felton between the 1 and the 3 on his uniform, but it fell to the turf incomplete. After a Giants punt, the Vikings took over deep in their own territory, inside the 10-yard line with less than four minutes left before halftime. The Vikings appeared to get a first down that would have taken the clock to the two-minute warning, but a penalty took it off the board, and McCarthy was sacked on the first play after the two-minute warning, so the Vikings punted it away. That allowed the Giants to tack on a 46-yard field goal by Ben Sauls to send the game into the locker room with a score of 10-3. The Giants got the first possession of the second half, and the Vikings’ defense forced a quick three-and-out, taking over inside their own 10-yard line after yet another special teams penalty. Carson Wentz took over at quarterback and got things started with a 28-yard pass to Myles Price to get the offense going, and followed it up with a 17-yard pass to Jeshaun Jones to get into New York territory. Ultimately, the drive stalled again, and the Vikings again called upon Will Reichard to do Will Reichard things. He did, connecting on a 54-yard field goal, cutting the New York lead to 10-6 with eight minutes left in the third quarter. On the Giants’ next offensive play, Brandon Allen’s pass was intercepted by undrafted free agent linebacker Jacob Roberts, who took the return down to the New York 27-yard line and set the Vikings up with outstanding field position. . @Jacobrob3rts_ gets his hands on the INT! 📺: #MINvsNYG @FOX9 pic.twitter.com/vtWx02TfhR — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) August 15, 2026 The Vikings pushed down into a goal-to-go situation, and a pass interference call in the end zone then gave the Minnesota offense a first-and-goal down at the 1-yard line. Then, after another pass interference call in the end zone made it first-and-goal from the 1 again, Wentz found Price in the end zone, and Price made a very nice one-handed catch for a Minnesota touchdown, with Reichard’s extra point giving the Vikings a 13-10 lead with four minutes left in the third quarter. . @Vikings WR Myles Price with the gorgeous one-hander in the end zone 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eJNwJzB8Vm — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 At the start of the fourth quarter, the Vikings got to Allen again, as his deep pass to the left was picked off by undrafted free agent safety Jacob Thomas for the team’s second pick of the day. That gave the Vikings the ball near midfield. . @Vikings S Jakobe Thomas comes up with the INT! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r53CBYWBgf — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Unfortunately, the Vikings could not take advantage of the interception and punted it back to the Giants, pinning the Giants inside their own 10-yard line. The two teams then exchanged punts again, and it’s worth noting that the Vikings had to put Carson Wentz back into the game at quarterback, as Max Brosmer. . .who came in for Wentz after the touchdown. . .appeared to have suffered some sort of injury to his right wrist and did not return. After being pinned inside their own 5-yard line after a Brett Thorson punt, Allen put together his best drive of the day, hitting a series of completions to get the Giants into Minnesota territory as the fourth quarter wound down. An offensive pass interference penalty stalled their efforts, however, and they were forced to punt it away. Wentz and the Vikings ran out the clock from there, and the Vikings got out of MetLife Stadium with their first victory of the preseason. We now await word on the injuries to Jamal Adams and Max Brosmer and hope that they’re not too bad. Keep your fingers crossed, folks. The Vikings’ next preseason game will see them return to U.S. Bank Stadium next Saturday afternoon at noon Central time, as they’ll play host to another new head coach, as Jesse Minter and the Baltimore Ravens will come to the Twin Cities, with a couple of joint practices leading up to that at the Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center. The Minnesota Vikings take down the New York Giants in their 2026 preseason opener by a score of 13-10. Thank you to everyone who got their coverage of this week’s game right here at The Daily Norseman!

summary: The primary objective of every preseason game is to just make it through without any significant injuries. During the second quarter of the preseason opener, the Vikings had to call […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Jamal Adams #54 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The primary objective of every preseason game is to just make it through without any significant injuries. Unfortunately for the Minnesota Vikings, it looks like they might not have met that first objective in their preseason opener against the New York Giants. During the second quarter of the preseason opener, the Vikings had to call on the cart for safety/linebacker Jamal Adams, who appears to have suffered some sort of a leg injury on a play where the Giants scored a touchdown. The nature of the injury has not been disclosed at the present time. Adams signed with the Vikings a couple of weeks ago and originally started as a linebacker, but was moved back to the safety spot by Brian Flores and was apparently being used all over the defense. His role has apparently not been completely defined yet. Adams spent last season with the Las Vegas Raiders and played all seventeen games after dealing with a litany of injuries over previous seasons. He seems to be the sort of player that Flores could use in all sorts of different ways in his defense. Once we get an update on what sort of injury Adams has suffered, we will update this post. For now, we will just be hoping that it isn’t as serious as it appears to be at first glance. Keep your fingers crossed, folks. EDIT : This appears to be where the injury took place. It’s a non-contact injury, which is never a good thing. Non-contact injury for Jamal Adams (32) on NYG’s cement turf. Brutal. He was going to contribute heavily to this defense. pic.twitter.com/fE0fcxSJF1 — Thor Nystrom (@thorku) August 15, 2026

full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Caleb Banks #95 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ladies and gentlemen. . .we’ve made it! For the first time since 4 January, the Minnesota Vikings. . .or a reasonable facsimile thereof. . .will be taking to the field for some hot National Football League action. Today is the first of their three preseason games for the 2026 season, as they visit the place where they played their final road game of last season, MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. There, they will face the New York Football Giants and their new head coach, John Harbaugh. Here’s everything you need to know going into today’s game. Date and Time : Saturday, 15 August 2026, noon Central Time Location : MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey Weather : Clear skies, temperatures in the low 80s, winds out of the north at ~5 MPH Television Coverage : FOX 9 in the Twin Cities area, local affiliates in several markets around the Midwest ( courtesy of 506 Sports ), NFL+ or ESPN Unlimited for out-of-market viewers Radio Coverage : Vikings Radio Network , SiriusXM Channel 382, SiriusXM App Channel 820 Bonus : KFAN (which, again, is doing a simulcast for both radio and TV this season) has promised that Justin Jefferson will be joining the broadcast for the entirety of the third quarter of today’s game. So we’ve got that going for us. Which is nice. Line : Man, if you’re betting on preseason games. . . Chris’ Prediction : Chris’ only prediction is that Chris is going to continue not to do predictions for preseason games Three Keys 1) No significant injuries – I say it every year. . .this is the most important thing about every preseason game, and it will continue to be the most important thing about every preseason game this year. Get in, get some reps, get out, get ready for the next one. 2) Quarterback snap distribution – Now that the hierarchy has been established, it will be interesting to see exactly how the snap count goes for each of the quarterbacks. From what I’ve seen online, Kyler Murray and the starters will be set to play a series or two, depending on how things go. How long does J.J. McCarthy go after that? How do things get divided between Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer after McCarthy departs? We’ll find out. 3) Depth chart battles – One of the best parts of any preseason game is watching the guys at the bottom of the depth chart who know they’re fighting for spots working their tails off to make an impression. We’re going to see a lot of that today. Which of these young players, whom we may or may not have heard a lot of going into today, are we going to be talking about when this one is over? Bonus) PUNTER FIGHT! – In one corner, you’ve got the longtime veteran, Johnny Hekker. In the other corner, you’ve got the young Aussie and International Player Pathway participant, Brett Thorson. The battle to officially replace Ryan Wright starts today. Can you feel the excitement, people? I can damn sure feel the excitement. Know the Foe : Big Blue View Twitter/X/Whatever we’re calling it today : @DailyNorseman FaceBook : https://www.facebook.com/thedailynorseman There you have it, folks! We are ready to go for the first preseason game of 2026! As I mentioned yesterday over in the Feed , we will only be doing one Open Thread for game days going forward rather than the quarterly ones we’ve done in the past. So, if you’re going to be hanging out with us, all you have to do is keep it right here the whole time. Next week, we. . .or I. . .will try to get back more into the flow of how game weeks are supposed to go with a “how to watch” post and other stuff. We did supply a full Minnesota Vikings roster for the preseason for you to reference, which we hope you’ll find helpful. With that, enjoy today’s game, and here’s hoping that everyone comes out of this one healthy and that a good time is had by all. SKOLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL VIKINGS!!!!

On Saturday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel returned to the fields behind Gillette Stadium for a ticketed practice for yet another full-pads session. To recap the action, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook. In […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 09: Andy Borregales #36 of the New England Patriots lining up for a kick during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 9, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots’ first preseason game is in the books, but training camp rolls on. On Saturday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel returned to the fields behind Gillette Stadium for a ticketed practice for yet another full-pads session. To recap the action, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eyes for better or worse. Standout of the day WR Romeo Doubs: The arrow continues pointing up for the Patriots’ free agency investment, and Saturday might have been his best practice to date. Doubs’ chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye continues to develop nicely, and the pair connected for three touchdowns during the session, including twice in 11-on-11 work. His most impressive grab came in the left-hand back corner of the end zone. Doing his best Randy Moss impression, Doubs out-jumped cornerback Charles Woods to come away with the contested catch. His ability to win 50-50 balls like this could be an asset for the Patriots this year, and the team and its quarterback should feel very good about his progression over the last few practices. Go up and get it Romeo! 😳 pic.twitter.com/mCw2kjlSmQ — New England Patriots (@Patriots) August 15, 2026 Other performances of note QB Drake Maye: Primarily operating in the low red zone, Maye had a productive day. He wasn’t perfect by any means, completing 10 of 16 passes with a pair of would-be sacks in full-team work, but he spread the ball around well and found the end zone on multiple occasions. His connection with Romeo Doubs stands out, but he also showed tremendous trust in Kayshon Boutte on a 40ish-yard deep ball. All in all, a good day for New England’s QB1. WR Mack Hollins: Coming off a preseason opener that was ag mixed bag, in part due to quarterback play, Hollins had a solid practice hauling in two touchdowns from Drake Maye. Both plays were nearly identical and saw the big-bodied wideout high-point a play-action throw perfectly over the middle of the field. While not challenging for a regular starting spot in a crowded receiver room, Saturday served as a reminder that his size and physicality at the catch point can be tough to defend. ED Gabe Jacas: While it is clear that he has plenty to work on, the Patriots continue showing trust in Jacas by putting him in high-quality practice situations. On Saturday, the second-round rookie saw his first reps with the starters in an 11-on-11 setting. Replacing Dre’Mont Jones, who left the session early, he registered a run stuff against Will Campbell on his first snap and later also registered a pressure against Drake Maye that could have been a sack in live action. CB Carlton Davis III and CB Charles Woods: Carlton Davis and Charles Woods being on the field after recently missing time due to injury was good. Their performance, on the other hand, was not. Davis looked rusty at times and gave up three catches in team work, including touchdowns to Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins as well as the aforementioned deep ball to Kayshon Boutte. Woods, on the other hand, was beaten twice for touchdowns by Doubs. K Andy Borregales: After going just 2-for-5 in the preseason opener , Borregales had a perfect day on Saturday. He split the uprights, which were narrower than normal NFL goal posts, on all six of his attempts. Maybe his mental toughness had something to do with this, maybe Julian Ashby’s return to the long snapper spot did. Regardless, the second-year kicker bounced back well from Thursday’s debacle. Other players worth highlighting include Kayshon Boutte, whose twisted deep grab was one of the plays of camp so far. On the flip-side, DeMario Douglas had a quiet day while Karon Prunty surrendered a pair of touchdowns. Meanwhile, Jacob Rizy is the new backup center with Ben Brown out for multiple weeks and Andrew Rupcich sent to season-ending injured reserve. The Patriots will be back on Sunday for a walkthrough that will not be open to the general public. As always, though, Pats Pulpit will have you covered and bring you updates straight from Foxborough.

title: What signing two O-linemen, other Saturday moves mean for the Patriots
summary: Coming out of their preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts, the New England Patriots made some changes to their roster. In light of some injuries along the offensive line, they signed free agents Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski on Saturday. In corresponding moves, the team placed fellow O-lineman Andrew Rupcich on injured reserve and released […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 06: Andrew Rupcich #67 of the New England Patriots arrives to New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Coming out of their preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts, the New England Patriots made some changes to their roster . In light of some injuries along the offensive line, they signed free agents Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski on Saturday. In corresponding moves, the team placed fellow O-lineman Andrew Rupcich on injured reserve and released long snapper Niko Lalos. In addition, running back Terrell Jennings was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement . Let’s dissect what the moves mean for the Patriots. Hits keep coming along the O-line The Patriots’ interior offensive line had already been relatively thin, but the preseason opener delivered a significant blow to its depth. Not only will nominal No. 4 Ben Brown miss multiple weeks after leaving the Colts game in the first quarter, Andrew Rupcich getting placed on season-ending injured reserve removes the projected No. 5 from the equation as well. As a consequence, the group now looks as follows : Interior offensive line (10): Alijah Vera-Tucker (75 | LG), Jared Wilson (55 | C), Mike Onwenu (71 | RG), Ben Brown (77), James Hudson III (51), Mehki Butler (63), Jacob Rizy (64), JonDarius Morgan (69), Darrian Dalcourt (—), Joe Michalski (—) The starting trio of Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu looks good on paper, while Brown is a proven and versatile backup. However, the rest of the group is a question mark particularly with Brown set to at least miss the remainder of the preseason and Rupcich out for the year. The Patriots need to quickly find somebody to step up and possibly challenge for the fifth spot. On paper, James Hudson and Mehki Butler are best positioned to be that somebody. Throwing-at-the-wall approach up front Darrian Dalcourt entered the NFL as a rookie free agent in 2024, and spent time with four teams — Baltimore, Washington, Carolina, Cleveland — before coming to New England. Joe Michalski went undrafted last year and after one season on Denver’s practice squad has now found his way to Foxborough as well. Neither has appeared in a non-preseason game at the pro level. Both have decent size, but their careers so far show that they should not be trusted to suddenly step in and compete for the top backup interior spots on the roster. If anything, the team is using the “throw it at the wall and see what sticks” approach at the moment. Caleb Lomu factor After the Patriots selected offensive tackle Caleb Lomu in the first round of this year’s draft, executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf spoke highly about his flexibility and how the team could even envision him playing inside. That has indeed happened in practice, if only for a handful of reps. That said, with the interior situation murky and Lomu not in line to start for the Patriots this season — Will Campbell and Morgan Moses are locked into the left and right tackle jobs, respectively — the club might reconsider his role. If nobody else is able to provide proper depth behind Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu, maybe the team will turn to the 21-year-old. Lomu will be on the 53-man roster anyway, but his value in 2026 might prove higher should he also be a candidate to offer guard and even center depth. This, in turn, could be bad news for James Hudson, Mehki Butler and the other depth interior linemen. Another player out for the year With Rupcich going to IR, the Patriots now have five players on the list who are ineligible to be reactivated at a later point and therefore out for the season: Injured reserve (5): TE Julian Hill, WR Jimmy Kibble, WR Jeremiah Webb, RB Myles Montgomery, OL Andrew Rupcich The list would be six long had Terrell Jennings not been let go with an injury settlement on Saturday. This, however, did open the door for him to possibly rejoin the club at a later point in time. Long snapper competition over, again To be fair, it was never much of a competition to begin with. But one could dream, right? Fact is, with Niko Lalos now being cut by the Patriots for a second time this offseason, Julian Ashby is the only long snapper remaining on the roster. Unless his previous ankle injury or another ailment keeps him out for extended stretches of time, or he somehow forgets how to snap the football, he will be the team’s snapper for a second straight season — as had been the expectation throughout the offseason even after Lalos was signed twice.

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 2: Terrell Jennings #26 of the New England Patriots celebrates after scoring a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Gillette Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Terrell Jennings will have an opportunity to return to the field in 2026. The New England Patriots reached an injury settlement with the third-year running back on Saturday, according to the NFL transaction wire. He will now head to waivers with a shot to catch on elsewhere. If unclaimed, the move opens the possibility for a return to Foxborough later in the campaign as an unrestricted free agent. Crossing that bridge would have to wait until the settlement’s timeframe is complete. Jennings, 25, had been placed on injured reserve in the hours leading up to last Thursday’s preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts. The 6-foot, 222-pound running back was in contention for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart behind incumbents Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The position also includes 2026 draft pick Jam Miller, 2025 undrafted free agent Lan Larison and veteran August additions Hassan Haskins and JaMycal Hasty , who all saw the field for what became a 13-13 tie at Gillette Stadium. A former rookie minicamp tryout, Jennings originally signed with New England as a member of the 2024 UDFA class. The Florida A&M product went on to spend parts of the past two years on the 53-man roster after reaching the league limit in standard elevations from the practice squad. Jennings rushed for his first career touchdown last fall before finishing the journey to Super Bowl LX on injured reserve. He has totaled 115 yards from scrimmage over the course of 37 touches. The stay has also brought two kickoff returns and three tackles through 79 snaps on offense and 69 snaps on special teams. With the settlement, five players currently reside on injured reserve for the Patriots. The season-ending list includes tight end Julian Hill, wide receivers Jimmy Kibble and Jeremiah Webb, running back Myles Montgomery, as well as guard Andrew Rupcich, who was sent to IR amid a series of moves announced on Saturday.

title: Patriots sign two interior offensive linemen in wake of preseason opener
summary: The New England Patriots have added two free agents after attrition hit the trenches in the preseason opener. The organization signed interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski on Saturday, as Mike Vrabel had signaled prior to the 15th practice of training camp in Foxborough. “Yep, I think we’re going to sign two guys […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 04: Alabama Crimson Tide offensive lineman Darrian Dalcourt (71) during the Chick-fil-A Kickoff Game between the Miami Hurricanes and the Alabama Crimson Tide on September 4, 2021 at Mercedes Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Michael Wade/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots have added two free agents after attrition hit the trenches in the preseason opener. The organization signed interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski on Saturday, as Mike Vrabel had signaled prior to the 15th practice of training camp in Foxborough. “Yep, I think we’re going to sign two guys this morning, and we’ll get those names out to you or jersey numbers or whatever, but hopefully they’ll be out there,” the head coach told reporters . “But they just showed up this morning.” Both were in for a tryout that also included former UMass offensive tackle Ryan Mosesso, per the NFL transaction wire, as the club navigates injuries up front. During Thursday night’s 13-13 tie with the Indianapolis Colts, proven interior backup Ben Brown exited 18 snaps into his start at center. And in the final quarter at Gillette Stadium, so did the contending Andrew Rupcich, who had drawn the start at left guard and logged 58 snaps before limping to the sideline. Dalcourt, 25, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Alabama in 2024. The former national champion, who started 19 of his 39 games between center and guard for the Crimson Tide, has since made stops on the practice squads of the Baltimore Ravens, Washington Commanders, Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns. He stands in at 6-foot-3, 320 pounds. Michalski, 25, went undrafted out of Oklahoma State in 2025. While a member of the Cowboys, he started 35 of his 59 games and finished as a two-time team captain, two-time All-Big 12 honorable mention and five-time Academic All-Big 12 selection. The 6-foot-5, 305-pound center spent his rookie regular season on the practice squad of the Denver Broncos and was released in January as the calendar turned to the playoffs. The Patriots officially placed Rupcich on season-ending injured reserve and waived long snapper Niko Lalos to make room on the 91-man roster. Rupcich, 27, had joined New England’s practice squad in 2025 and re-upped on a futures contract in February. Offering depth at the guard spots as well as center, the 6-foot-6, 325-pound product of NAIA Culver-Stockton began his NFL career with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He appeared in 12 games, including two starts, while in Nashville before reuniting with a familiar coaching staff late last September. Lalos, 28, served as the Patriots’ long snapper for the August opener in place of incumbent Julian Ashby. The 6-foot-5, 269-pound convert from defensive end first signed after a workout in March. He was waived in May and returned last week to handle 12 preseason snaps on special teams. The Dartmouth alum entered the NFL with the New York Giants as an undrafted free agent in 2020 and appeared in six games during his rookie year, recording six tackles, one fumble recovery and one interception. Tours with the New Orleans Saints and XFL’s Seattle Sea Dragons followed. The Philadelphia Eagles will visit Foxborough for joint practices ahead of next Saturday’s 7 p.m. ET preseason matchup.

title: Patriots O-lineman Ben Brown dealing with multi-week injury
summary: The New England Patriots’ offensive line depth suffered a blow in the first quarter of their preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts. Ben Brown, who had started the game at center and projects as the top interior backup entering 2026, exited the contest and was unable to return. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, he […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots center Ben Brown (77) warms up before a preseason game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Natalie Reid-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots’ offensive line depth suffered a blow in the first quarter of their preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts. Ben Brown, who had started the game at center and projects as the top interior backup entering 2026, exited the contest and was unable to return. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, he won’t be for a while. “Ben is going to be a few weeks,” Vrabel said during a press conference ahead of the Patriots’ training camp practice on Saturday . “Four-to-six, eight, 10, 12. Even numbers. But it will probably be extensive throughout the rest of the preseason for sure.” Brown remained down following a sack against backup quarterback Tommy DeVito on Thursday night. He required assistance walking off the field and into the blue medical tent on the sideline, which he left straight for the locker room. In his place, undrafted rookie Jacob Rizy took over as New England’s center. Whether or not that arrangement will remain in place heading into next week’s joint practices and preseason game with the Philadelphia Eagles will be seen. The Patriots did sign two free agent interior linemen — Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski — to their active roster on Saturday to improve the depth at the position. Brown, 28, started his career as an undrafted rookie with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2022, and through stints in Seattle, Arizona and Las Vegas found his way to New England during the 2024 season. He has since played 31 games with 14 starts for team, and after signing a two-year, $5 million contract extension in December 2025 projects as its No. 4 interior linemen behind starters Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu.

title: Romeo Doubs ‘progressing the right way’ at Patriots training camp
summary: New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs is progressing comfortably in Foxboro, as highlighted by his three highlight-reel touchdowns during Saturday’s training camp practice. After a slow start to the summer sessions, the Patriots’ free agency signing has put together another impressive practice following a stretch of strong performances last week. Head coach Mike Vrabel […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 11: Romeo Doubs #87 of the New England Patriots in warmups during a joint training camp between the New England Patriots and the Indianapolis Colts on August 11, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs is progressing comfortably in Foxboro, as highlighted by his three highlight-reel touchdowns during Saturday’s training camp practice . After a slow start to the summer sessions, the Patriots’ free agency signing has put together another impressive practice following a stretch of strong performances last week. Head coach Mike Vrabel spoke with the media before the session, noting that he’s seen a lot of positive things from Doubs, who’s “trending in the right direction.” “I think [wide receivers coach Todd Downing] found where Romeo can really help us — be big, fast and aggressive, and I think that showed up in some practices that you saw,” Vrabel said. “It’s just figuring out what they do best, seeing what you can realistically improve, and then put them in those spots to help build their own confidence, and then also a place where they can help the football team.” Doubs secured all three of his receptions in the same high-pointing motion, reaching over defensive backs Carlton Davis and Charles Woods. “I feel exactly where I am. I think I’m progressing the right way,” Doubs said after practice about how he feels he’s performed. “[I’m] just taking these days one day at a time. I’ve learned early on that this is a day-to-day league. So, I plan on continuing to keep that the same way.” Lining up out wide in Drake Maye’s offense, the receiver capped off a 1:05-minute drill with a score. After a 40-yard Kayshon Boutte completion to set the unit up in the red zone, Maye floated a high pass to Doubs, who went up over Woods for the catch. During the final 11-on-11 period, Maye targeted the 26-year-old in the corner of the end zone again, extending over Woods for a second time. Doubs then celebrated by heaving the ball into the air as fans cheered from the bleachers. “This is a game I’ve been playing for a long time. Obviously, this takes work, so I have worked on this a ton,” he said of his ability to make those plays in the red zone. “In the end, I’m just going out there, playing fast, playing physical and just making sure I put the team in a better position.” The former Green Bay Packer also acknowledged that things are starting to slow down for him. New England ranked 20th in the NFL last season in red-zone efficiency, converting inside the 20-yard line just 55.7% of the time. Doubs, standing 6-foot-2 and 210 pounds, with 21 career touchdowns, debuts with the Patriots as a red zone threat for Maye and the offense.
author: Andrew Guindon

title: Patriots training camp recap: Romeo Doubs, receivers shine in red zone
summary: The New England Patriots were back to work on Saturday following their first preseason contest on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts. Here’s what went down on the Gillette Stadium practice fields. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 120 minutes (10:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. ET) Conditions: Sunny, temperatures in the mid 80s There was no easing back into action […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs (87) does a drill during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots were back to work on Saturday following their first preseason contest on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts. Here’s what went down on the Gillette Stadium practice fields. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 120 minutes (10:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. ET) Conditions: Sunny, temperatures in the mid 80s There was no easing back into action for the Patriots, as they donned full pads on a sunny day in Foxboro. Work was also centered around red zone and end-of-game situations. Attendance Absent: CB Christian Gonzalez, WR Kobe Prentice, DB Eric Butler, LB Chad Muma, LS Niko Lalos, OLB Xavier Holmes, OL Andrew Rupcich, OL Ben Brown, WR Kyle Dixon, DL Christian Barmore Injured: OLB Dre’Mont Jones Returnee: LS Julian Ashby, CB Charles Woods (red non-contact jersey) Limited: LB Christian Elliss PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler It was a lengthy injury list for the Patriots in their first practice back, headlined again by cornerback Christian Gonzalez. “I’ve talked about his professionalism, everybody else’s. So, this isn’t anything [contract related],” Mike Vrabel said about the corner. “It was something that happened in practice, and he’s where he’s supposed to be when he needs to be there. Treatment, working with Frank [Piraino] and doing those things.” New England did see top edge rusher Dre’Mont Jones depart practice early. Jones walked to the medical shed with head trainer Jim Whalen during a 1-on-1 period before departing practice with a member of the training staff. Elsewhere, offensive lineman Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich were out after suffering injuries Thursday night. Brown, according to Vrabel, will be sidelined for multiple weeks likely through the end of preseason. Those injuries led to New England signing depth lineman Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski, which will lead to two corresponding roster moves. Muma and Holmes’ absences were injury related. Takeaways Doubs’ day: Free agent addition Romeo Doubs appeared to have his best week of practice last week. Mike Vrabel saw it similarly. “I saw it the same way,“ Vrabel said. ”Just new offense, new year, figuring out the player, getting to know him. Really, a lot of positive things, I think, trending in the right direction.“ Doubs continued that progression on Saturday, as he hauled in multiple high-point touchdowns throughout the practice. That was highlighted by two in full-team work, as he climbed the ladder over Charles Woods to cap off Drake Maye’s end-of-game situation. In the next red zone period, Doubs got Woods again in the front right of the end zone. Red zone success: Doubs wasn’t the only wide receiver to find success in the red zone. Early in that day, Mack Hollins was the top target hauling in two play-action crossers from Drake Maye and worked the end line to haul in a third touchdown courtesy of Tommy DeVito — which led to a new version of the usual obscure celebration from the veteran receiver. A.J. Brown also got in on the fun as he dusted cornerback Carlton Davis on a whip route along the goal line and later scored on a play-action slant. Hunter Henry also caught a pair of scores from Maye, while Kyle Williams then adjusted and fought through Brandon Crossley to snag a fade route for a score from DeVito. Jacas’ reps: With Dre’Mont Jones leaving practice, rookie edge defender Gabe Jacas repped with the top defense opposite of Elijah Ponder. Jacas’ physicality was noticeable on multiple occasions as he powered into the backfield for multiple run stuffs. His best rep of the day came against Will Campbell, where Jacas powered through the tackle with a stab move for what likely would have been a sack in live action. Corner struggles: Saturday marked the first day Carlton Davis participated in full-team periods since suffering a hamstring injury on July 28. His return was rather rocky. Davis surrendered a hand full of touchdowns in 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 red zone work before getting beat downfield by Kayshon Boutte in an end-of-game drive. Charles Woods also returned to practice in a red non contact jersey and repped opposite Davis with Christian Gonzalez sidelined. Woods was on the wrong side of multiple touchdowns by Doubs. Borregales bounce back: It was a rough preseason opener for Borregales Thursday night as he missed three field goals, including the potential game-winner. Back with long snapper Julian Ashby on Saturday, Borregales bounced back connecting on all six of his field goal attempts while working on the skinny field goal posts. Other notes: While Doubs capped off Maye’s one-minute drive, it was Kayshon Boutte who sparked it hauling in a long go route down the left sideline over Carlton Davis. DeVito’s one-minute drive ended with the defense standing strong, as pressure forced back-to-back incompletions to end the drive. Efton Chism III found the end zone working a scramble drill with Tommy DeVito in red zone work. Jack Westover had an impressive diving catch along the goal line with Mike Brown tight in coverage. Strong day for all three tackles (Will Campbell Marcus Bryant, Caleb Lomu) in 1-on-1 periods. With Brown and Rupcich absent, the second string offensive line featured: Marcus Bryant, Mehki Butler, Jacob Rizy, James Hudson, Caleb Lomu. K.J. Britt repped next to Robert Spillane with Elliss limited and Muma sidelined. Rookie Namdi Obiazor also had an impressive run stuff with the second unit. Karon Prunty recorded a pass breakup on Kayshon Boutte in the end zone. Preview The Patriots will hold a closed walkthrough on Sunday with just the media in attendance. A busy week then lies ahead with the Philadelphia Eagles coming to town for a pair of joint practices on Wednesday and Thursday.
author: Brian Hines

title: Devon Witherspoon extension sets floor for Christian Gonzalez contract with Patriots
summary: While there has been no contract extension movement between the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez so far, one external domino has fallen. Devon Witherspoon, who was drafted in the same first round as Gonzalez, has just been made the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history by the Seattle Seahawks. Witherspoon and the reigning world champions […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 14: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots stands on the sideline during the national anthem prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at Gillette Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images While there has been no contract extension movement between the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez so far, one external domino has fallen. Devon Witherspoon, who was drafted in the same first round as Gonzalez, has just been made the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history by the Seattle Seahawks. Witherspoon and the reigning world champions reached an agreement on a four-year, $132 million contract extension that reportedly includes over $101 million in guarantees. At an average annual value of $33 million, the deal tops the two-year, $62.2 million deal signed by the Cleveland Browns’ Denzel Ward in July. Gonzalez, who is represented by the same agent as Witherspoon, will surely keep a close eye on those numbers and the overall structure of the deal. The Pro Bowler is himself looking to become the highest-paid cornerback in football. Back in July, Patriots owner Robert Kraft claimed that the organization had an offer on the table that would meet those requirements. Whether that is still relevant with Witherspoon now signed will be seen. Fact is, Witherspoon’s $33 million per year is the new benchmark now and a number Gonzalez will want to best with his own extension. So far, however, the two sides apparently have not made significant progress since the Patriots used the fifth-year contract option to keep the 24-year-old — who is 18 months younger than his Seattle counterpart — tied to the club through 2027. Gonzalez nonetheless had been an active participant in practice before suffering an injury during earlier this week. “Working hard, conditioning, but will not be practicing. He’s not ready to get back out there and practice yet,” said head coach Mike Vrabel on Saturday. “I’ve talked about his professionalism, everybody else’s. So, this isn’t anything like that. It was something that happened in practice, and he’s where he’s supposed to be when he needs to be there. Treatment, working with Frank [Piraino] and doing those things. But, obviously, my job is to be on the same page with everybody here, players and coaches. And I’m confident that that’s what we are doing, and everybody has a plan each and every day.”

title: Patriots vs. Colts snap counts from NFL preseason
summary: The New England Patriots’ preseason opener against the visiting Indianapolis Colts was not necessarily filled with points or offensive fireworks, but it nonetheless offers quite a bit of excitement. After all, it was a first chance for the new-look team to showcase itself to its fans in a game setting and another opportunity for players […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: The New England Patriots take to the field prior to a game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ preseason opener against the visiting Indianapolis Colts was not necessarily filled with points or offensive fireworks, but it nonetheless offers quite a bit of excitement. After all, it was a first chance for the new-look team to showcase itself to its fans in a game setting and another opportunity for players to keep building their cases for the 53-man roster. In that regard, Mike Vrabel and his assistance have plenty to evaluate. Even though nearly a third of players on the active roster did not take the field, a majority — 60 different players — did. While not everybody had the same level of involvement, their roles, performances and exposure gives coaches and analysts alike another data point to assess the team with the 53-man cutdown deadline looming. Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 13-13 tie at Gillette Stadium . Offense Total snaps: 73 | Time on the field: 30:23 | *denotes starter RG/LT James Hudson III* (60; 82%), LG Andrew Rupcich * (58; 79%), C Jacob Rizy (55; 75%), WR Nick DeGennaro (46; 63%), QB Tommy DeVito * (43; 59%), LT Marcus Bryant * (43; 59%), RT Caleb Lomu * (43; 59%), RB Lan Larison (41; 56%), TE Eli Raridon * (39; 53%), WR Efton Chism III (32; 44%), QB Behren Morton (30; 41%), RT/LT Dametrious Crownover (30; 41%), LG/RG Mehki Butler (30; 41%), WR Kobe Prentice (27; 37%), WR Kyle Williams (26; 36%), WR Cameron Dorner (23; 32%), TE/FB Jack Westover (23; 32%), RB Jam Miller * (22; 30%), WR Tejhaun Palmer (19; 26%), C Ben Brown * (18; 25%), WR Kayshon Boutte * (16; 22%), TE Tanner Arkin * (16; 22%), RG JonDarius Morgan (15; 21%), WR Mack Hollins * (13; 18%), RT Lorenz Metz (13; 18%), TE C.J. Dippre (9; 12%), RB Hassan Haskins (5; 7%), RB JaMycal Hasty (5; 7%), TE Mitch Van Vooren (3; 4%) With Drake Maye absent, the Patriots gave backup quarterbacks Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton a chance to show what they could do, and both had positive moments. Still, their pecking order seems set in stone, which is why other positions were more interesting to watch. First up were the wide receivers, which saw four of the top seven take the field. Mack Hollins and Kayshon Boutte both saw a handful of snaps early in the contest, while Kyle Williams and Efton Chism saw comparatively extended playing time. Among the depth wideouts, undrafted rookie Nick DeGennaro received the most opportunities — a result of him, like others, not being used extensively during Tuesday’s joint practice. The other skill positions also did not see any of the top options involved, with the exception of Eli Raridon. A roster lock at tight end, the third-round draft pick led his position group with 39 snaps and four targets (of which he caught one for 8 yards). The most actively-used running back was Lan Larison, a potential sign that the team is taking a close look at him in the RB3 competition. Along the offensive line, the expected candidates were the first men up. Marcus Bryant and Caleb Lomu started at left and right tackle, respectively, and clearly appear to be ahead of the competition at the position. Along the interior, the injury suffered by Ben Brown opened the door for Jacob Rizy to see considerable snaps at center. Defense Total snaps: 65 | Time on the field: 26:42 | *denotes starter LB Khalil Jacobs (50; 77%), CB Karon Prunty * (40; 62%), ED Bradyn Swinson, (38; 58%) CB Channing Canada (32; 49%), CB Brandon Crossley (32; 49%), S Peter Manuma (32; 49%), DT Eric Gregory * (30; 46%), ED Quintayvious Hutchins * (29; 45%), CB Kobee Minor (28; 43%), S Mike Brown * (28; 43%), LB Chad Muma * (27; 42%), LB Namdi Obiazor (27; 42%), S Dell Pettus * (27; 42%), S John Saunders Jr. * (27; 42%), DT Joshua Farmer * (25; 38%), ED Gabe Jacas * (25; 38%), DT Isaiah Iton (24; 37%), DT Leonard Taylor III (23; 35%), DT Jeremiah Pharms Jr. (23; 35%), CB Kenneth Harris (22; 34%), S Eric Butler (22; 34%), ED Amari Gainer (21; 32%), CB Marcellas Dial Jr. (21; 32%), ED Jesse Luketa (17; 26%), DT Casey Rogers (15; 23%), LB K.J. Britt * (14; 22%), LB Riley Wilson (8; 12%), CB Kindle Vildor * (8; 12%) None of the Patriots’ projected defensive starters appeared in the game, which allowed the depth pieces to see considerable action. Tops among the group was undrafted rookie Khalil Jacobs, who seemingly elevated himself to the fourth spot on the linebacker depth chart in recent practices. However, with K.J. Britt getting the start and playing generally well in his limited action, and with Chad Muma having an inconsistent day, the competition for the depth spots at LB still seems to be wide open. Up front, second-year edge Bradyn Swinson and his 38 snaps led the way. Swinson also showed his disruptiveness even though. he was not a starter. That honor belonged to rookies Quintayvious Hutchins and Gabe Jacas; the latter — like Swinson — was also actively involved on special teams and at one point challenged by head coach Mike Vrabel to play with better effort. The defensive tackle rotation saw every one of the players on the field play between 15 and 30 snaps, with the highest-quality opportunities being given to Joshua Farmer and Eric Gregory. The former is seemingly a roster lock, while the latter appears to be on the bubble. In the secondary, Kindle Vildor only played eight snaps as a starting outside cornerback but he bolstered his case by registering an interception. While low snap counts might be an ominous sign for some players — LB Riley Wilson among them — they are probably not in Vildor’s case. At this point in time, he very well looks to be in a solid position in the race for the CB5 role. Accordingly, kicking game usage plays an important role during preseason. In that sense, the aforementioned Bradyn Swinson and Gabe Jacas are both noteworthy players on the top of the list. title: Game Day Preview: Saints welcome Jags to kick off preseason
summary: Saints football is finally back! For the first time in eight months, the Black and Gold will return to the turf of the Caesars Superdome to take on somebody other than their own teammates as they welcome the Jacksonville Jaguars to town. Trevor Lawrence has some bad memories of this building, and now, his former […]
full_text: Saints football is finally back! For the first time in eight months, the Black and Gold will return to the turf of the Caesars Superdome to take on somebody other than their own teammates as they welcome the Jacksonville Jaguars to town. Trevor Lawrence has some bad memories of this building, and now, his former running back will be wearing the other team’s jersey. Let’s break down the details and give you what you need to know before the game. Game: New Orleans Saints vs Jacksonville Jaguars (Preseason Week 1) Location: Caesars Superdome Time: 3:00 p.m. CT TV: Fox 8 (local), ESPN Unlmtd (national) Radio: WWL Line: NO -2.5 Matchup The first preseason is always a fun opportunity to see what players are going to take advantage of their chance, because more often than not, the starters won’t play. Spencer Rattler will get the start for the Saints under center as he looks to seal his spot as the backup to Tyler Shough. Iowa State player Hunter Dekkers will also get his chance to take that spot as well, as he is expected to play in today’s contest. The Saints are, of course, battling injuries as Bryan Bresee and Dillon Radunz have both been lost for the season with ACL injuries. Rookie Jordyn Tyson is experiencing a hamstring issue and will miss some time, as well as veteran Cam Jordan, who just returned to the Big Easy on a team-friendly deal. On the other side, Jacksonville is struggling with offensive line issues as well. They will be looking to iron those out before the season so that 2026 can be a better run than 2025 in Florida. This will be a fun game regardless as we are just anxious for football, but I will be keeping a close eye on the rookies for the Black and Gold and just how quickly they can make an impact for Kellen Moore’s team, which is looking to go to the playoffs for the first time since the newest Hall of Famer, Drew Brees, retired after the 2020 season.

title: 7 winners, 3 losers from Giants-Vikings: Malachi Fields, Jack Kelly shine in loss
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Let’s review the New York Giants’ preseason-opening 13-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings as only we can, with our unique ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ review of who played well and who did not. Kudos to … Malachi Fields — The rookie wide receiver had a 15-yard touchdown catch from a scrambling […]
full_text: Malachi Fields celebrates a touchdown catch on Saturday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Let’s review the New York Giants’ preseason-opening 13-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings as only we can, with our unique ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ review of who played well and who did not. Kudos to … Malachi Fields — The rookie wide receiver had a 15-yard touchdown catch from a scrambling Jaxson Dart that perfectly illustrated the kind of weapon he can be. He worked for the quarterback and used his size, athleticism, and strong hands to haul in the touchdown pass. Fields finished with three catches for 34 yards. – Gets Sacked – Taken out of game for concussion protocol – Comes right back and throws a dime to Malachi Fields for the TD The Jaxson Dart experience (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/QT7Q0Fpwhy — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) August 15, 2026 Braxton Berrios — I will just come out and say it. If Berrios gets through the preseason healthy, he is making the roster. Berrios was the first punt returner and was on the first kickoff return group with Deonte Banks. He had two 15-yard punt returns and caught a pass for 9 yards. Darius Alexander — The second-year player was a better pass rusher than run defender as a rookie. Saturday, things looked the same. Alexander had a sack, a tackle for loss, and a quarterback hit. Chauncey Golston — The versatile backup edge defender/defensive end had a tackle for loss and two quarterback hits in limited action. Odell Beckham Jr. — Beckham had just two catches for 6 yards, but I am including him simply because seeing him playing in a Giants uniform in MetLife Stadium at this point was cool. Odell Beckham Jr. CATCH pic.twitter.com/1YJ9uc6ONc — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) August 15, 2026 Isaiah Likely — The Giants’ new tight end has been forming a good relationship with Dart during training camp, and it showed up on Saturday. Likely had just two catches for 11 yards in brief action, but both were third-down grabs that created first downs. Jack Kelly — The sixth-round pick was impressive. As he has been all summer. Kelly had a team-high five tackles. He was a big part of the reason Darius Alexander was able to get his sack. Exceptional blitz design by Dennard Wilson for the #Giants Darius Alexander commits and then drops to spy, which isolated LB Jack Kelly against the RB, and Kelly WALKS the RB into McCarthy. CB blitz w/ Golston dropping into coverage. JJ steps up into a waiting Alexander, sack pic.twitter.com/Jo92hQOwMD — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 Wet Willies to … First-half run defense — The Giants’ run defense has been an issue for years. Harbaugh has made fixing it a MAJOR emphasis. The Giants were playing on Saturday without front seven starters D.J. Reader, Shelby Harris, Brian Burns, and Tremaine Edmunds. With that in mind, it might be tempting to shrug off the fact that the Giants gave up 5.2 yards per carry in the first half (62 yards on 12 rushes), but we should not. There were 17- and 15-yard runs on Minnesota’s first offensive series. All of that indicates that the defensive line depth is not good enough. GM Joe Schoen needs to be looking for upgrades, especially at the backup nose tackle spot, when teams trim their rosters from 90 to 53 players. Brandon Allen — The third-string quarterback entered the game midway through the third quarter. He threw his first pass directly to Minnesota linebacker Jacob Roberts, giving Minnesota the ball at New York’s 27-yard line. The Vikings capitalized with a 1-yard touchdown pass from Carson Wentz to Myles Price. Allen threw a second interception later, trying to fit a deep throw down the sideline to wide receiver Ryan Miller. The ball was intercepted by safety Jacob Thomas, a result you could see coming from the press box as soon as Allen let the ball go. Allen might be a great guy. We know he is a favorite of Giants’ quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan. There has to be a better option out there somewhere for the Giants as their third quarterback. Deonte Banks — With Paulson Adebo and Greg Newsome not playing, the 2023 first-round pick played the entire first half. Unfortunately, Banks did not carry the momentum of a good training camp into the game. He committed back-to-back penalties on second-quarter passes by J.J. McCarthy, a defensive holding and an illegal contact. Other cornerback notes: Art Green had a pass interference penalty on third-and-goal from the 1-yard line. Korie Black had a pass interference penalty. Rookie Colton Hood had an illegal contact penalty and gave up a 17-yard completion from J.J. McCarthy to Myles Price. Kwillies to … Jaxson Dart — The second-year quarterback did some good things, some bad things, and had an unfortunate, unwanted visit to the medical tent for a concussion check. Dart threw a beautiful 15-yard touchdown pass to Fields. That was an improvised scramble play with Dart moving to his left, the kind of unscripted play on which Dart excels. Dart found his new favorite target, Isaiah Likely, for two first downs. On the negative side, Dart took two sacks. The first one bothered me more than the big hit he took on the second one because it appeared to be his fault. He had an opportunity to throw the ball, chose not to, and ended up holding the ball and running himself into a sack. Dart led the league in sacks with the quarterback being at least partially responsible last season, and he needs to get better about not causing negative plays.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants QB Jaxson Dart ‘puzzled’ after yet another concussion test
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart started the 2026 season in the most familiar way possible for Giants’ fans: A trip to the blue tent to be evaluated for a concussion, followed immediately by a touchdown on an improvised pass play. The headline of the day was the two-play sequence to end the first quarter […]
full_text: ﻿Jaxson Dart before the preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings. | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart started the 2026 season in the most familiar way possible for Giants’ fans: A trip to the blue tent to be evaluated for a concussion, followed immediately by a touchdown on an improvised pass play. The headline of the day was the two-play sequence to end the first quarter and start the second. Dart took a massive hit on a 2nd-and-10 blitz from the Vikings when Dart failed to identify the blitzer and running back Tyrone Tracy failed to pick up the blitz. How it feels getting blown out in your Week 1 fantasy matchup pic.twitter.com/CEbT6gocpk — PFF Fantasy (@PFF_Fantasy) August 15, 2026 Dart got up gingerly after the hit and was immediately called to the blue tent to be evaluated for a concussion while Giants fans held their breath. He surprisingly returned for the first play of the second quarter, and immediately found rookie Malachi Fields once the play broke down. Dart missed two games with a concussion last season, and was tested for concussions on four other occasions. He was “puzzled” by the concussion test on Saturday. “As far as the blue tent, I really respect the rules and the thought behind the NFL has of keeping players healthy and reviewing things, but at the same time, I’m still puzzled by it just feeling like every time that I get hit, I find my way in there,” Dart said. “Which at times, I still try to wrap my head around, but that’s all that I’m going to say about that situation.” Dart said he got the wind knocked out of him on the hit. In defense of the officials, Dart did lay on the MetLife Stadium turf for a few seconds before getting to his feet. Head coach John Harbaugh’s immediate thought when Dart went down was “we need to block better. That’s what my feeling was.” Harbaugh had no hesitation putting Dart back in the game because he knew the quarterback was “fine.” This is what happened when Dart re-entered the game: Such a Jaxson Dart play. Dart leaves the medical tent, play breaks down, he extends, and finds rookie Malachi Fields for a tuddy. Elite job by Fields to work upfield after the drag and find space in the back of the EZ. pic.twitter.com/p971QwKVl6 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 Dart started the game and played the first quarter — and the first play of the second quarter — for the Giants, though his stat line was unimpressive for a quarter’s worth of work. He finished the day completing 3 of 4 passes (75 percent) for 26 yards (6.5 per attempt) and a touchdown. Dart was also sacked twice, once on each drive. This was about what we’ve come to expect from Dart: Big hits, big plays, and play that seems more impressive than his stats. Dart left the game after his touchdown and will now go back to practice with a list of things to work on.

title: What did we learn from the Giants’ loss to the Minnesota Vikings?
summary: Yeah baby, NFL football is back! Well, sort of. We naturally get hyped to see our team on the field again after seven months with no New York Giants football. Three things can be said, though, with almost complete certainty: See: Victor Cruz; Tre Hawkins III; Jalin Hyatt; Greg Dulcich as examples of both kinds […]
full_text: Malachi Fields and Jaxson Dart celebrate a touchdown vs. the Vikings. | Getty Images Yeah baby, NFL football is back! Well, sort of. We naturally get hyped to see our team on the field again after seven months with no New York Giants football. Three things can be said, though, with almost complete certainty: Some new player will excite us, and it will be a harbinger of his performance in the real season to come. Some other new player will excite us, and he will turn into a pumpkin once the real season starts. There’s no way to tell the difference at this point. See: Victor Cruz; Tre Hawkins III; Jalin Hyatt; Greg Dulcich as examples of both kinds of players. Perhaps of more interest was how the Giants under a new coaching staff would operate. How often will Dart line up behind center? How often will Arvell Reese be back in coverage vs. rushing the passer? Will the offense be more run-oriented? Will the kicking situation be clarified? Will anyone stand out in the disturbingly unsettled secondary and wide receiver corps, including veterans such as Odell Beckham Jr.? So with that in mind, who and what stood out for better or worse in the Giants’ 13-10 loss to the Vikings? The offense is anything but a well-oiled machine so far The Vikings are not a great team to play your first preseason game against. Brian Flores’ defense has flummoxed the Giants’ offense in regular season games for two consecutive years. Many defensive coordinators run vanilla defenses in the preseason, but not Flores. He stacked the box and liberally blitzed Jaxson Dart in the first half. That’s a good thing in the sense that Dart needs reps recognizing the blitz and countering it. It’s a bad thing, though, when you don’t recognize it and your running back (in this case, Tyrone Tracy) doesn’t pick up the blitzer. The result was Dart’s first trip of 2026 to the blue tent. After the first couple of drives, the offense settled down a bit. Cam Skattebo in particular had several nice runs and looks fully recovered from last year’s gruesome injury. The run blocking seemed effective with rookie Sisi Mauigoa and fullback Patrick Ricard leading the way. What we didn’t see, though, was the free-wheeling deep ball offense of the Brian Daboll era. Most of the passes were short, quick-hitters. Dart alternated between under center and shotgun, but wasn’t especially effective either way. The longest completion by far was a screen pass by Jameis Winston to Devin Singletary on third-and-23, which Singletary, competing to keep his spot on the roster, turned into a 40-yard gain. Odell Beckham Jr., back in blue again, had two catches for 6 yards in the first half, but was not seen by Winston as he broke free down the middle for what would have been an easy TD. Just as well, because the stadium might have collapsed from the roar if Winston had hit him. You had to feel sorry for Beckham, who was open downfield at least three times and never saw the ball come his way on any of those plays. The guy can still get open. The larger question, which couldn’t be answered today, is whether the Matt Nagy offense will be much more conservative than what we’ve gotten used to the past few years. We’ll have to see the Giants against a more conventional defense to get a better feel for that. What we do know is that today they passed 21 times (completing 16), but for only 160 yards, while rushing 25 times (not including scrambles) for 70 yards. Not a lot to get excited about. Oh, and…maybe the Giants need to go shopping for a QB3. Brandon Allen was awful, getting intercepted twice in the second half. On the second one OBJ was wide open on the other side of the field and Allen never looked his way. As for the kicking game: Only Ben Sauls got a chance and he kicked a 46-yard field goal down the middle. Let’s hope that the starting IDLs stay healthy One big question mark for the defense is how the Giants will adjust to the loss of Dexter Lawrence in the interior. We didn’t get much of an answer to that question today, because neither D.J. Reader nor Shelby Harris, the Giants’ two off-season acquisitions to try to replace Lawrence, played. Their replacements in the starting lineup today, though, did not distinguish themselves. Darius Alexander, whose calling card is his pass rush potential, did not look good against the run early on, though he made a couple of tackles later, one for a loss of 4 yards. Leki Fotu and Josh Tupou, who started in the interior, got pushed around on the Vikings first drive. Fotu did have a breakup of a screen pass, however. No need to get worried just yet, but let’s hope that Reader and Harris stay healthy. The second level of the defense is promising. The third level? TBD Tremaine Edmunds did not play, but first round pick Arvell Reese was active in limited playing time with a tackle and an assist. The eye-catcher, though, was rookie Jack Kelly, who seemed to be all over the field, with two tackles and three assists. The defensive backs, though? A different story. Paulson Adebo did not play (not that he’s had a good camp, anyway), but Deonte Banks (twice), Colton Hood, Korie Black, and Art Green were all called for pass interference. And that was without Justin Jefferson playing and Jordan Addison only playing a little. Is it too early to get excited about Malachi Fields? In his first NFL action, rookie Malachi Fields caught all three of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown. A nice stat line, but on the surface nothing spectacular. It was the TD, though, that encompassed what we love about Jaxson Dart and what the addition of Fields to the offense may mean: 6 + 0 = 6 Jaxson Dart ➡️ Malachi Fields for the touchdown! pic.twitter.com/siBIlNxdHm — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 15, 2026 Dart’s first read was not open and he started to get inside pressure, so he rolled out to his left. Meanwhile Fields, who had run a short in-breaking route from the right side, began to slow down when it looked like Dart was about to throw. Once Dart escaped to the left, Fields broke toward the end zone and beat his man. Dart saw him, twisted his body back, threw a perfect pass off his back foot, and Fields went up and got it for the TD. Imagine an offense with Fields, a healthy Malik Nabers, and OBJ all on the field at the same time, or at least two of the three since I don’t expect to see 11 personnel a lot with this coaching staff. Add in Isaiah Likely, who only played briefly and caught 2 passes for 11 yards. This could turn out to be a pretty dangerous passing offense…if the Giants’ coaching staff is willing to let it be.

title: Giants-Vikings: Positional grades from preseason Week 1
summary: The New York Giants era under John Harbaugh has officially started with New York hosting the Minnesota Vikings early on Saturday. The Giants featured plenty of under-center, heavier personnel runs, with an 11 personnel package that used Isaiah Likely all over the formation. Likely was the focal point in clutch situations for Matt Nagy and […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart celebrates with rookie receiver Malachi Fields. | Getty Images The New York Giants era under John Harbaugh has officially started with New York hosting the Minnesota Vikings early on Saturday. The Giants featured plenty of under-center, heavier personnel runs, with an 11 personnel package that used Isaiah Likely all over the formation. Likely was the focal point in clutch situations for Matt Nagy and the Giants, but the establishment of a physical rushing attack was noteworthy and unsurprising. Jaxson Dart and the starters played a couple of series, while several younger players competing for starting roles saw action throughout the first half. Dennard Wilson flashed creative five-man pressure packages with interior defenders that “ wasted ” interior blockers, which was coupled with corner blitzes. Wilson featured linebacker-plug blitzes, schemed LB blitzes vs. running backs, and incorporated secondary blitzes as well. This defense should be much more refreshing than the previous one. Here are the grades for Preseason Week 1. Quarterback Dart was shaky at times, but he showcased his excellent ability to buy time on his touchdown pass to Malachi Fields, which came moments after he exited the medical tent following a concussion check: Such a Jaxson Dart play. Dart leaves the medical tent, play breaks down, he extends, and finds rookie Malachi Fields for a tuddy. Elite job by Fields to work upfield after the drag and find space in the back of the EZ. pic.twitter.com/p971QwKVl6 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 Dart was not perfect and his play wasn’t overly polished, but he does flash play-making skills. And, through no fault of his own, he did have a trip to the medical tent, which has become synonymous with the young quarterback. Jameis Winston was 8 of 9 for 89 yards with 40 yards coming on the Devin Singletary third-and-long screen. Brandon Allen’s first pass was intercepted by a sitting linebacker on a slant to Odell Beckham Jr. Allen then took a sack on third down that ended his second offensive drive. He then threw an interception on third down to start the fourth quarter. Dart struggled but flashed bright, per his rookie season; Jameis was efficient, but Allen was bad, which brought the grade down slightly. Grade: C+ Running Back It was great to see Cam Skattebo on the field. He rushed for 19 yards on four carries, with a few strong stiff-arms and a long run of 7 yards. Tyrone Tracy Jr. added a pair of carries for five yards but had a tragic blown pass protection assignment that resulted in Dart’s trip to the medical tent. Singletary continues to prove himself as a reliable depth piece. He converted the third-and-long screen pass from Jameis Winston that set up the Jaxson Dart touchdown to Fields. Dante Miller, Eric Gray, and Damon Bankston received carries in the second half – none made much of an impact. Tracy’s blown assignment in pass protection was the most impactful part of the running back room, followed by Singletary’s elite screen on third down. Grade: C- Wide Receiver Rookie Malachi Fields caught a 15-yard pass for a touchdown on an excellent, and savvy, route adjustment on a broken play. Fields showed processing and his size on his touchdown catch; he added another catch for 11 yards and another slant for eight yards in the final minute of the first-half. Fields added a special teams’ tackle. The crowd cheered as Odell Beckham Jr. took the field, and on each of his two receptions ( for six yards ). Beckham Jr. was streaking down the field wide open on a Cover-0 call that Winston checked down. Ryan Miller and Dalen Cambre added some catches late, as well as Isaiah Hodgins, but no one moved the needle much in the game. Grade: B- Tight End Isaiah Likely was a focal point of the offense on the Giants’ first drive. Both third downs were designed to Likely, with the third-and-ten being a backside slant that was jumped by Brian Flores’ safety. Likely did, however, convert on the fast four third-and-3: The #Giants convert on their first third-down before punting on a third-and-ten sack. Nagy employed a fast four to free up a quick spot route to Likely as the No. 2 w/ the No.3 pushing vertical. pic.twitter.com/XuToDmvW4n — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 Likely will have a major role even when Malik Nabers returns from injury. Chris Manhertz played early and often, along with Patrick Ricard to establish physicality with the rushing attack. Theo Johnson caught one pass for 6 yards, and Thomas Fidone II mostly played with Allen in the second half, so statistics were hard to come by. Grade: B+ Offensive Line Andrew Thomas did not play, giving Marcus Mbow the opportunity to start at left tackle. The first -team offensive line was solid, despite surrendering three sacks to Brian Flores’ defense. The Flores’ defense did disguise one sack very well, which was the fault of running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. It was great to see Francis Mauigoa using his strength at the point of attack to spring positive runs from the Giants: Love to see this block by Francis Mauigoa pic.twitter.com/Pb8fqB1mRu — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 The second team offensive line struggled to generate push at the point of attack and they were marginal in pass protection. Rookie J.C. Davis was beaten on a third-down sack of Allen. Overall, the first unit was solid. Grade: B Defensive Line The defensive line was without D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris. Darius Alexander flashed, but was also controlled on more than a few plays, leading to chunk gains on the ground for Minnesota. I would have liked to see them be more sturdy, albeit they made a few stops. Alexander played through the first-half and into the third quarter. He came away with a sack on a third-and-5 that was beautifully designed by Dennard Wilson: Exceptional blitz design by Dennard Wilson for the #Giants Darius Alexander commits and then drops to spy, which isolated LB Jack Kelly against the RB, and Kelly WALKS the RB into McCarthy. CB blitz w/ Golston dropping into coverage. JJ steps up into a waiting Alexander, sack pic.twitter.com/Jo92hQOwMD — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 Alexander added two quarterback hits. He was solid, overall. Leki Fotu played in the second half; both him and Bobby Jameson-Travis read a second-down red zone screen, and it was Fotu who knocked the pass down. Marlon Davidson knocked down a pass, and did an excellent job following Carson Wentz’s eyes to do so on third-and-long in the fourth quarter. Grade: C E dge Kayvon Thibodeaux made an excellent tackle down the line of scrimmage, but was also pinned on a pin-pull concept. Minnesota successfully ran off-tackle early in the game, setting a physical tone that was too reminiscent of the porous run defense from last season. However, New York solidified in key situations and forced Minnesota into several third and manageable situations. I hope to see more usage of Chauncey Golston this year, or at least a clearer role. He flashed with an excellent TFL on the edge, and I believe that is well within his wheel-house. Trace Ford continued to hustle as a back end piece, and he made a great tackle for a loss at the end of the game. Grade: B Linebacker Arvell Reese earned a STOP on the first drive of the game: Arvell Reese quickly worked through a block and met Jordan Mason at the LOS. Decisive and physical. New York Giants, we have a LB. pic.twitter.com/LGW1gAwwlj — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 15, 2026 Kelly had an excellent blitz where he was isolated and BLEW UP the running back in protection, which led to a third-down sack. Depth linebacker Caleb Murphy had an excellent STOP on the goal line late in the third quarter; Jack Kelly stopped Demond Claiborne on the subsequent play.
