title: Survey results: Defense is the main attraction against the Vikings
summary: The 2026 NFL preseason is officially under way, and the New York Giants will open their own preseason by hosting the Minnesota Vikings at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. today. The first preseason game is about setting benchmarks on the road to the season opener. It’s the first opportunity for the coaching staff to get […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks on the field during practice. | Getty Images The 2026 NFL preseason is officially under way, and the New York Giants will open their own preseason by hosting the Minnesota Vikings at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. today. The first preseason game is about setting benchmarks on the road to the season opener. It’s the first opportunity for the coaching staff to get eyes on their team in live action against a real opponent, not just teammates on the opposite side of the ball. It gives the coaches a chance to see where their team is after a tough training camp, as well as provide a baseline for improvement going into next week’s game against the Miami Dolphins. For this week we wanted to know which side of the ball the Giants’ fanbase is most interested in seeing; offense, defense, or special teams. On one hand, it’s predictable that the defense came out on top. After all, it’s been a major pain point for fans over the last two years, and fans are desperate for improvement. We’ve also been getting glowing reports of the defense out of camp, with dominant linebacker play as well as pleasant surprises from the defensive line and secondary. Rookie Arvell Reese, in particular, has been a star of camp, while Abdul Carter has simply taken practices over at times. The two could be cornerstones of the Giants’ defense for a long time, and if the reports out of camp are accurate, they might be setting the stage for post-season honors. Reese currently has the fifth-best odds to win Defensive Rookie Of the Year (+850), while Carter is currently twelfth in the odds for defensive player of the year (+4,000), per FanDuel . Fans want to see improvement, and are also curious to see if the defense that beat writers have been reporting on is for real. On the other hand, this somewhat runs counter to the sentiment at the national level. There is real concern among national analysts regarding the Giants’ offense. The opinion of most at the national level outside the Giants’ fanbase is that the defense should be “fine” at worst, with the potential to be a Top 5 unit at best. However, there are questions as to whether the offense concocted by Matt Nagy, Greg Roman, and Brian Callahan* can function at an NFL level. * I’ve heard the three coaches referred to as the “Unholy Trinity” which sounds like a try-hard Black Metal power trio . There are questions as to whether the Giants’ receiving corps can be of NFL caliber without Malik Nabers, whether Jaxson Dart can develop into a consistent passer who can win over the middle, and questions whether the running game can be consistent given the concerns about the passing game and Cam Skattebo’s longevity. And to be fair, quite a few fans also mentioned in the poll that they want to see Dart function under center and with improved footwork. They want to see the legion of new receivers on the field, the types of plays called by Matt Nagy, and they want to see just what kind of running game Greg Roman is cooking up. Personally, I was somewhat expecting more fans to answer “Special Teams”. I find myself intrigued by the incredibly young battery of Ben Sauls, Dominic Zvada, and Ben Mann. Likewise, special teams play will have a big impact on the bottom third of the roster, and will shape multiple position groups. Regardless of how you responded, we’ll be getting our first look at the 2026 New York Football Giants soon.

title: New York Giants mailbag: Roster questions, Chauncey Golston’s role, more
summary: Norm Weiss asks: Ed, I’m sure you haven’t been overwhelmed with Damon Bankston questions. Have you seen enough from him to see him making the 53 man roster? I live in New Mexico and had the pleasure of seeing him play at UNM. His play strength and speed are much greater than his measurables. He […]
full_text: Norm Weiss asks: Ed, I’m sure you haven’t been overwhelmed with Damon Bankston questions. Have you seen enough from him to see him making the 53 man roster? I live in New Mexico and had the pleasure of seeing him play at UNM. His play strength and speed are much greater than his measurables. He is an explosive athlete, as seen by his 2 returns for touchdowns last year on only 12 returns. He can run surprisingly well between the tackles as well as outside due to his short distance quickness and vision. He is also a good receiver out of the backfield. BTW, he led the Texas 5A division in rushing yards as a high school senior. I think he and Banks would make a dynamic kick return duo. Do you think he has a chance? Ed says: Norm, all I can really go by is the distribution of practice reps. Bankston gets a few second-team reps, and a lot of third-team reps. He hasn’t really stood out. Unless that changes, he is not making the 53-man roster. John Harbaugh said the other day that he likes Bankston’s talent, but that Bankston is behind the other backs in terms of his understanding of the offense. Ed Helinski asks: Have the Giants indicated that they’ll return to West Virginia for training camp in 2027? Instead, how about having camp at SUNY Cortland and its excellent facilities? The Jets held camp there from 2009-2014. Ed says: The Giants did not build their own practice facility, and they aren’t spending millions of dollars now to renovate it, to spend additional money moving training camp to a remote location. As far as I know, they plan to train in East Rutherford next summer. That would only change if something construction-related made that unworkable. If they had to move, The Greenbrier would likely be their first choice. It has everything, with the exception of an indoor practice bubble. Michael Spina asks: If you could ask Harbaugh any question at all about this team, and he had to answer it as fully and truthfully as possible, what would you ask him? Ed says: Michael, I don’t think I would ask him a question about this team at all. I think I might ask him a question about legacy. No head coach has ever won a Super Bowl with two teams. I think I would ask him how much it would mean to him to be the first, and whether or not he would consider his tenure with the Giants a success if he does not at least get the team to a Super Bowl at some point. Thomas Shelby asks: Are the Giants allowed to practice in Met Life Stadium? Ed says: Thomas, yes, they are “allowed” to. I have seen them do it on occasion over the years. But, NFL teams do not generally practice in their home stadiums. They have practice facilities for that where they have locker room, practice bubbles, meeting rooms, weight rooms, and all of their equipment. The Giants’ facility is on the other side of the Meadowlands Sports Complex parking lot. The conditions are the same. In terms of home field advantage, that is created by the fans. It takes playing good football, getting fans excited, filling the stadium with your own fans rather than fans of the opposing team. The Giants have not played enough good football in recent years to make that happen. Joseph Rivage asks: Hi Ed, my question regards Jaxson Dart. Like many others last season, I saw a QB with potential franchise ability. It looked like they finally got “the guy”. So far this season though it seems like he’s struggling a little with fitting into the new system that Nagy is implementing. Do you think there’s a cause for concern or is it just growing pains for a young player adjusting to this new system and by extension the offense as a whole? Ed says: Joseph, what gives anyone the idea that Dart is “struggling”? The offense is learning an entirely new system from the ground up. It is normal that offenses are behind defenses at the beginning, especially in a circumstance like this. The reality is that an offensive install is far more cumbersome and complicated than a defensive one. Dart has, to my eyes, looked fine. He has been comfortable under center. He is learning new things. That’s how you grow as a player. It’s practice, and it isn’t supposed to be perfect. It’s supposed to be hard. Don’t get yourself all tied up in knots about anything you read or hear from the daily practice reports. Steve Goodyear asks: Thoughts on Kubas? Can he play a viable backup center? Does he make the roster? Ed says: Steve, I doubt Jake Kubas is making the roster. He worked all spring and summer as a third-team guard, until the injuries to John Michael Schmitz and Lucas Patrick forced him to take reps at center over the past week. With practice reps and preseason playing time, though, comes an opportunity. So, I won’t say it is impossible for Kubas to make the roster. Just unlikely. Matthew Burns asks: What can you tell us about the Giants’ Strength & Conditioning/Performance Staff? Are they new to the G-Men? Were any of the coaches with Harbaugh in Baltimore? Ed says: Matthew, not much, to be honest. The Giants’ official website lists nine members of that staff. Aaron Wellman, Sam Coad, Drew Wilson, and Matthew Frakes are holdovers. Sam Rosengarten, Chris Allen, and Ron Shrift come from the Ravens. Mark Naylor comes from the Arizona Cardinals. Brian Ellis worked in Baltimore for a couple of years, but was most recently at Baylor. Henry Jacukiewicz asks: Ed, my question is about Chauncey Golston. What do you see as his role ? I thought he was a good pickup but he seems to have faded into the background. Ed says: Henry, Golston is a good player who lost playing time last season after the Giants were able to draft Abdul Carter. He also dealt with injuries and played in only 10 games. Golston will be the fourth edge defender, and will play in some situations as a hand in the ground defensive end. He is nice depth to have because he can fill a number of different roles when needed. Jeffrey Smith asks: Hi Ed, have not heard a peep about either Jack Kelly or Chauncey Golston this summer. any comments about either of them? BTW, I think Jack Kelly is a great name for a NY Giant LB. Ed says: Jeffrey, see above for thoughts on Golston. As for Kelly, we have written about him a number of times. He is playing with the second team ahead of Darius Muasau, and has had a nice camp. He has shown surprising range in coverage, and should be a nice backup. ctscan123 asks: Anyone on the roster bubble that we could maybe swing a trade for rather than cut? Only name that comes to mind is Ben Sauls… Think we could get anything for him? Anyone else? Ed says: CT, here is the problem with trading players at the deadline. There are 32 teams cutting their rosters from 90 players to 53. That’s 1,184 players who are going to lose their jobs, meaning they will be available to other teams. Unless a team really loves one particular player, there are going to be a plethora of players available at every position via the waiver wire or free agency. It is very difficult to get anything for a player another team knows you don’t have room for and are about to cut. It happens occasionally, and I’m sure GM Joe Schoen will look for opportunities, but they aren’t easy to find. David Clancy asks: Curious about the WR competition. I know you’ve been doing the 53 man roster predictions as lock, bubble, longshot but I’m curious about 1. What you think harbaugh and Co. Will do? (I.e what you think will happen) 2. What you would do? Ed says: David, there are three preseason games and a lot of practices to be held before that decision has to be made. I am not going to answer it today, because all of the evidence has not yet been collected and the answer could be different in three weeks. I will answer that when I make my final 53-man roster projection. Dave Nelson asks: What are biggest differences in the way training camp and/or practices are being run between Harbaugh and previous coaching regimes (Shurmur, Judge, Daboll)? Do you sense a different level of player engagement or buy-in? Ed says:…

title: NY Giants news: Giants set for first preseason game in John Harbaugh Era
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the team takes on the Minnesota Vikings in their first preseason game. A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp — an inside look | ESPN.com A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp begins with something he calls “wise words.” This […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the team takes on the Minnesota Vikings in their first preseason game. A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp — an inside look | ESPN.com A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp begins with something he calls “wise words.” This is where individual players get up and share a daily message. It’s inspiration or advice, and the order for who speaks is selected based on seniority. Harbaugh used “wise words” throughout his Ravens tenure. Just not always to start meetings. Often, it was after practices. He also employed something called “spotlight” in Baltimore during which a guy would tell his backstory to the team. Veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. used “wise words” last Tuesday to say: “Yesterday’s touchdown doesn’t win you today’s game.” His point being you can’t rest on the laurels of a good practice. You have to bring it again the following day. Beckham had his second straight strong practice that afternoon. Jaxson Dart is buying into system "I think it's so cool that we have as many coaches as we do that have had head coaching experience, who have done it at such a high level" Jaxson Dart talks about the experience on the Giants' coaching staff: pic.twitter.com/VjfKoYBjdf — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 13, 2026 Odell Beckham Jr.’s quest to make every play count in game that doesn’t | The Record Odell Beckham Jr. is living in two football worlds right now and his current place with the New York Giants has very little to do with his spectacular past. Admittedly, it’s incredibly difficult to separate the two. Which 10 Giants players have the most to gain — and lose — in the preseason opener? | The Athletic C Bryan Hudson. No player has a bigger opportunity than what has been presented to Hudson this week. Starting center John Michael Schmitz has been sidelined since suffering a concussion last Friday. Backup center Lucas Patrick has been sidelined this week while managing a lingering knee injury. With the top two centers on the shelf, Hudson has taken every first-team rep for the past week. That will continue Saturday for Hudson, who impressed in limited action during last year’s preseason. The Giants must have reservations about relying on the 33-year-old Patrick, who has been plagued by injuries throughout his career. The 25-year-old Hudson has a chance to establish himself as the younger, more dependable backup center option. Giants veteran Evan Neal might have shot to make roster after all | New York Post If the 53-man roster is going to include 10 offensive linemen, then the 6-foot-7, 340-pound Neal could steal one of the five backup jobs now that he is listed as a co-second-teamer with Aaron Stinnie at right guard. “I’ve seen great growth from Evan in his ability to take coaching and his ability to try to understand not just how things look on paper but what certain alignments mean to him,” first-year offensive line coach Mike Bloomgren said. “I think he is seeing more in his stance, and he’s playing with more confidence. Listening to other people in the building, they feel like he’s taken some good steps. We’ll see what he’s able to do in these [preseason] games.” Will John Harbaugh trust another rookie kicker after Dominic Zvada’s 62-yard bomb? | New York Daily News Harbaugh knows Zvada’s potential and also his history of inconsistency. That’s why he said: “He does have a big leg, but the bottom line is you got to kick it straight consistently.” And it’s one reason Harbaugh pointed out that lefty Ben Sauls, the other kicker in this competition, “has a very good leg, too.” Zvada clearly has been the better kicker in camp. Most days, with a handful of exceptions, Sauls has missed one or two and Zvada has missed none. Harbaugh and Horton have worked with Zvada on tinkering with the mechanics and operation to help him. The coach so far is splitting time between the two kickers to make it a fair, summer-wide battle. Giants’ fearless rookie insists he can ‘win right now’ if he starts in Week 1 vs. Cowboys | NJ.com Colton Hood is not shying away from his chance to win a starting job. He said he has no doubt he can start in the NFL from the get-go. “Yeah, for sure,” he said. “Like, no question. I know I can…I just know the type of player I am — my technique. My athleticism, I think, is up there with the best of the best. I know I can go out there and compete — and not just compete, but win. So I definitely think I can go out there and win right now.” 1 Player Each NFL Team Should Cut Before the 2026 Season | Bleacher Report New York Giants: WR Jalin Hyatt. Recovering from a torn ACL, wideout Malik Nabers might be ready to play in Week 1. The Giants re-signed Darius Slayton and inked Darnell Mooney and Calvin Austin III to deals in free agency and then drafted Malachi Fields in the third round of the draft. Assuming they all make the roster, Hyatt would be buried on the depth chart. It’s also worth noting that Odell Beckham Jr. has stacked solid performances at training camp in his second stint with the team. He could provide veteran leadership in the receiver room. Hyatt lacks a clear path to a meaningful role in New York and may need a fresh start elsewhere. title: Five Jets winners from the preseason opener against the Buccaneers
summary: The Jets’ first preseason game of 2026 is in the books. Let’s talk about five players who helped themselves. Cade Klubnik: Klubnik got a surprise start in the preseason opener due to a Geno Smith ankle injury. Any rookie quarterback tends to get overanalyzed in exhibition games. Klubnik didn’t do anything spectacular, but he was […]
full_text: New York Jets quarterback Cade Klubnik (10) walks off the field following a loss to Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a preseason opening game between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jets’ first preseason game of 2026 is in the books. Let’s talk about five players who helped themselves. Cade Klubnik: Klubnik got a surprise start in the preseason opener due to a Geno Smith ankle injury. Any rookie quarterback tends to get overanalyzed in exhibition games. Klubnik didn’t do anything spectacular, but he was efficient and did more bad than good. He also avoided any glaring mistakes on his way to a 5 for 7 night. Klubnik was the best of the three Jets’ quarterbacks and took a step toward earning the backup quarterback job. Will McDonald: McDonald has become a bit of a forgotten man at defensive end after the Jets added two players at his position in free agency and then picked Will McDonald second overall. Joseph Ossai’s injury allowed McDonald to start. He might have been facing backups, but you don’t get to choose your competition. You can only control your performance. McDonald got on the board a sack in limited action. Braelon Allen: For the next couple of weeks Allen has the stage to himself in the competition to be the second running back behind Breece Hall due to Isaiah Davis’ knee injury. The key for the third year back is to show he has recovered from his own knee injury that ended his 2025 season early. Allen broke a 31 yard touchdown run in the first half. Again, the competition was not starting level, but him running away from defenders suggests he still has a second gear. Mory Bamba: The first time I noticed Bamba, he was beaten cleanly in the red zone. He was able to recover to break up the pass on the play, but that was due mainly to a poor throw. For the rest of the game, Bamba was noticeable for all the right reasons. Often tested in coverage, he held up with 4 passes broken up. He also stood out on special teams. This was one of the stronger preseason cases I’ve seen an off the radar make to earn a surprise roster spot in recent memory. Jason Sanders: I’m going to be a tad controversial here. While both kickers technically had a perfect night, I can’t find anybody who believes Cade York actually made his 38 yard field goal attempt as time expired in the first half. It seems likely the officials blew the call. Sanders meanwhile connected from 47 yards out on his only field goal attempt. I would assume the coaches will take note of this as they grade the kicking competition.

title: Five takeaways from the Jets’ preseason opener against the Buccaneers
summary: The Jets’ preseason opener in 2026 is in the books. What was notable from this game? Here are my thoughts. Cade Klubnik was solid. There generally is an overreaction to rookie quarterback’s first preseason game. I’ll try and offer a reasonable take. The Jets didn’t put a ton of complex concepts on Klubnik’s plate, but […]
full_text: New York Jets quarterback Cade Klubnik (10) looks to pass the ball during a preseason opening game between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jets’ preseason opener in 2026 is in the books. What was notable from this game? Here are my thoughts. Cade Klubnik was solid. There generally is an overreaction to rookie quarterback’s first preseason game. I’ll try and offer a reasonable take. The Jets didn’t put a ton of complex concepts on Klubnik’s plate, but you can only execute the plays you are given. Klubnik did his job effectively in limited action, completing 5 of 7 passing attempts for 56 yards. I didn’t see any glaring errors or ill-advised decisions so I think we can label this NFL debut a success. I wish we saw more of Klubnik. The Jets pulled the rookie after two series. I can’t say I agreed with the decision. I guess you could make the argument that with Geno Smith temporarily sidelined that Klubnik’s value as the backup quarterback makes him too important to risk with extended preseason action. Here’s the thing. Klubnik’s primary job with the Jets this season if he takes the field won’t be to win games. It will be to develop. I think low pressure game reps against depth and practice squad players can have a real benefit. He is likely to succeed against this sort of competition, which can be a confidence boost. And preseason is a great place to learn professional passing concepts. At the very least it would have been nice to see him get a chance to run a two minute drill instead of whatever the Jets were trying to do at the end of the first half. I actually might prefer to keep Brady Cook as QB3 over Bailey Zappe at this point. I’m as shocked to be writing that as you are to be reading it. That tells you a lot about how bad this night was for Zappe. I know one of his two interceptions was really Arian Smith’s fault. Still, his decision making was all over the place, and his throws were labored. Cook at least was able to make a few plays in the fourth quarter outside structure. Is there any chance Cook could pull that off against starting NFL defenses? Well, we saw him fail over and over trying it at the end of last season. At least I could take a few positives from what Cook did, though. I can’t say the same for Zappe. He started the night competing for the QB2 spot. He’ll need to play much better the next two weeks to even be considered as QB3. Isaiah Williams started over Omar Cooper. I’m not sure this is significant at this point, but I’m also not sure it’s insignificant. Is Williams about to blossom into a quality starting wide receiver? The recent reports from training camp have certainly been glowing. Is Cooper struggling to the point where he won’t see much playing time early in his rookie year? Are the Jets just trying to motivate Cooper? Will the roles be flipped next week? For his part, Cooper did have a big 26 yard catch right before halftime to set up a field goal. Then again, maybe it’s a bad sign that Cooper was on the field at that point of the game. The NFL really needs to reconsider preseason. This is as much about the rest of the league as it is this game. I thought the first half was fun. It was good to see the starters for a series. Then we got a look at rookies, key reserves, and developmental players. The deeper we got into the game, the more the quality fell. Eventually guys who will struggle to make these practice squads saw an appreciable number of snaps. It showed in the quality of play. If you want to use preseason snaps to prepare your starters for the regular season, there’s value in preseason. If you want to get your key backups work in a game situation, again that makes sense. If you want to use the exhibition games to develop young players who might have a future on your team, I can see it. But if we’re just giving snaps to guys who aren’t going to be in the NFL, I really have to question why we need three exhibition games. And if you’ve watched games so far this weekend across the league this has been a common theme.

title: Eagles-Ravens preseason observations: Position battle updates, injury news, and more
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles kicked off their 2026 preseason schedule with a LOSS to the Baltimore Ravens. Final score, which doesn’t matter, but we’re logging it here anyway: 24 to 7. To no surprise, the Eagles barely played any starters in this game. You could say that any football is better than no football but this […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 15: Kelee Ringo #7 of the Philadelphia Eagles intercepts a pass intended for Xavier Guillory #16 of the Baltimore Ravens during the first half of the preseason game at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles kicked off their 2026 preseason schedule with a LOSS to the Baltimore Ravens. Final score, which doesn’t matter, but we’re logging it here anyway: 24 to 7. To no surprise, the Eagles barely played any starters in this game. You could say that any football is better than no football but this was mostly a boring game. The Eagles’ offense mustered just 100 yards on their first 31 plays before Cole Payton finally led a scoring drive later in the fourth quarter. Read on for some noteworthy moments from Saturday night. NOTABLE POSITION BATTLE UPDATES: BACKUP QUARTERBACK Andy Dalton got the start on Saturday night. The offense ran nine plays for 12 yards and three punts while he was in. Not exactly sharp. He finished 3/6 for 20 yards and 57.6 passer rating. Tanner McKee wasn’t much better. He was 6/10 for 35 yards and a 66.7 passer rating. This outing reflected what we’ve seen from the QB2 battle in training camp thus far; no real separation between these two. SAFETY Marcus Epps — who isn’t injured to our knowledge — did not dress for this game while Michael Carter II did. Advantage: Epps, who has been taking most of the first-team safety reps in camp. PUNT RETURNER Britain Covey was first up at punt returner . KICK RETURNER Quez Watkins and Elijah Moore were first up at kick returner. FIRST QUARTER OBSERVATIONS Sean Mannion called the game from the sideline, not from the booth. It was previously unclear where the first-time play-caller would be located for his offensive coordinator duties. The Eagles’ captains for the opening coin toss: Jeremiah Trotter Jr., Tank Bigsby, Byron Young. Rookie tight end Eli Stowers was flagged for holding on the Eagles’ first play from scrimmage, which wiped out a Bigsby run. The Eagles’ starting offensive line for this game: LT Fred Johnson, LG John Ojukwu, C Willie Lampkin, RG Drew Kendall, RT Markel Bell. Fred Johnson had a false start to knock the offense back to 3rd-and-15. The Eagles’ first drive: three plays, three yards, punt. Nice little throwback to the 2025 offense. A.J. Epenesa dropped into coverage and gave up an explosive play. Perhaps not the best way to utilize him. A blitzing Jeremiah Trotter Jr., who started at linebacker next to Jihaad Campbell, got to Tyler Huntley for a sack. That’s an aspect of Trot Jr.‘s game that stands out in a good way. Ty Robinson beat his blocker to sack Huntley and put the Ravens’ offense in 3rd-and-17. Robinson has picked it up a bit more recently after a slow start to camp. . @T_ROB99 with the takedown pic.twitter.com/3D6zKPZmFQ — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 15, 2026 Hollywood Brown had a chance to make a defender miss for a big gain but got tackled instead. Just hasn’t had an impressive summer. Tank Bigsby bobbled a low throw by Andy Dalton into a pick six … that was ruled incomplete upon review since the ball hit the ground. Gotta like Willie Lampkin’s effort. Willie Lampkin (61) on 3-15… finish to the echo of the whistle. pic.twitter.com/1jhLO1EDXu — Ryan Fowler (@_RyanFowler_) August 15, 2026 The Eagles shuffled their offensive line after their first drive … with Lampkin bumping out to right guard and Kendall moving to center. Paying tribute to the 2025 offense, the Eagles went three-and-out on their second drive as well. Six plays, seven yards, two punts to start the game. Darius Cooper dropped a pass that led to the Eagles having a third straight three-and-out. Bad drive-ending drop by DC. SECOND QUARTER OBSERVATIONS Tanner McKee entered the game on the Eagles’ fourth drive. New offensive line configuration: LT John Ojukwu, LG Micah Morris, C Jake Majors, RG Willie Lampkin, RT Markel Bell. The Eagles’ fourth drive: three plays, seven yards, punt. Four straight three-and-outs. Kelee Ringo and Michael Carter II were seemingly beat in coverage on the Ravens’ first touchdown. Yeah, nothing really there. Bad angle. https://t.co/gKRrfCstED pic.twitter.com/sbsxWk0Wut — Shane Haff (@ShaneHaffNFL) August 16, 2026 Cooper caught a McKee pass over the middle to give the Eagles their first first down of the night! Will Shipley had some solid runs to the right side, where Markel Bell was blocking. Jake Majors got hit with a holding penalty. The Ravens got away with a pass interference penalty on Danny Gray that prevented a first down. Mac McWilliams gave up a catch on a play where he also got called for defensive holding. Adding to not a good night for him. Ringo got called for a clear defensive pass interference to give the Ravens a goal-to-go situation. And then he instantly redeemed himself with a tremendous catch in the end zone for an interception! . @KeleeRingo with the INT! pic.twitter.com/BFglxDmkI3 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 16, 2026 Eli Stowers made two short catches — each for three yards — to end the first half. THIRD QUARTER OBSERVATIONS Shaun Wade has a good pass breakup on a play where he trailed and initially allowed the ball to be caught before punching it out while going to the ground. A blitzing Smael Mondon Jr. nearly got a sack but instead settled for a forced incompletion. Uar Bernard saw his first-ever snap in the NFL! Clint Hurtt gave him a head pat and a smile after that play. Josh Weru his first-ever snap in the NFL! He pressured the Ravens’ quarterback into an imcompletion and generated multiple pressures! Helped that he was unblocked on one but he looked athletic and had good closing speed. McKee failed to pull the trigger on a blitz and got sacked. Another new offensive line configuration: LT Myles Hinton, LG Micah Morris, C Jake Majors, RG Michael Jordan, RT Cameron Williams. Shaun Wade gave up a catch and run after the catch … but hustled back to knock the ball out of the Ravens’ hands for a fumble and Eagles recovery (Ambry Thomas)! You like to see that kind of effort. Another takeaway! pic.twitter.com/HMecL70reZ — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 16, 2026 Cam Latu had a bad drop. McKee sailed a pass over Darius Cooper’s head on 3rd-and-8 for yet another three-and-out on offense. FOURTH QUARTER OBSERVATIONS Deontae Lawson had a bunch of flashes. Veteran safety J.T. Gray got his hand on a pass for a deflection … on the same play where Ambry Thomas was flagged for illegal contact. A lot of penalties. It looked like Uar Bernard was going to get a run stop in goal-to-go … but the Ravens’ running back broke through his tackle for a touchdown. Good effort to be in position but obviously has to figure out how to finish the play. New guy David Blay had a couple nice moments. Played with physicality. Cole Payton entered the game with a little over 11 minutes left. Tarron Jackson notched a sack. Ty Robinson, playing in the game with six minutes left in the fourth quarter, got flagged for a late hit on the quarterback. Myles Hinton was flagged multiple times. Cole Payton looked good as a runner. Micah Morris got flagged for holding on a play where Payton took off running. Payton capped off a 9-play, 59-yard scoring drive with a touchdown pass to Erik Ezukanma. Gotta like how the rookie quarterback kept his eyes downfield and had nice touch on the throw for the TD. . @ColePayton9 finds @erikezukanma for the score! pic.twitter.com/TPPaNpgEAk — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 16, 2026 EAGLES INJURY NEWS Jakorian Bennett got banged up on the Ravens’ first drive. He spent some time in the medical tent before heading into the tunnel. UP NEXT The Eagles are off tomorrow, Sunday, August 16 before returning to practice on Monday. Then Tuesday is a travel day ahead of two joint training camp practices against the New England Patriots on Wednesday and Thursday.

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles will start the 2026 NFL preseason on the road against the Baltimore Ravens on Saturday night. We won’t get a chance to see much of the new offense under OC Sean Mannion, as the team notoriously keeps things vanilla in the preseason, but we might get an opportunity to see at least […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 10: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Darius Cooper #80 catches the ball during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 10th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles will start the 2026 NFL preseason on the road against the Baltimore Ravens on Saturday night. We won’t get a chance to see much of the new offense under OC Sean Mannion, as the team notoriously keeps things vanilla in the preseason, but we might get an opportunity to see at least a few plays with the starters. The team really focuses on practicing their game day operations, and Mannion will experiment with how he wants to call plays — and from where. It’ll be really fun to watch some of the depth players, and some of the rookies making early names for themselves — like OL Markel Bell. title: Eagles News: Did Philadelphia tease a new (old) helmet?
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles fans are freaking out after the Eagles posted a video featuring a helmet they haven’t worn since 1973 – InquirerIt’s been a while since Eagles fans last saw white helmets paired with kelly green wings on the field in Philly. The last time came […]
full_text: Sep 16, 1973; Philadelphia, PA, USA; FILE PHOTO; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Roman Gabriel (5) lined up under center against the St. Louis Cardinals at Veterans Stadium. Mandatory Credit Herb Weitman-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles fans are freaking out after the Eagles posted a video featuring a helmet they haven’t worn since 1973 – Inquirer It’s been a while since Eagles fans last saw white helmets paired with kelly green wings on the field in Philly. The last time came over 50 years ago, in 1973, but after the team posted a seemingly innocent video that featured the retro style, some fans are dreaming of a potential return. The video, posted Wednesday afternoon, featured Jalyx Hunt and new defensive back Riq Woolen blindly trying to match up different team helmets, but the comments were all focused on one thing: the white kelly green helmet that was curiously included in the lineup. […] So it raises the question: Are the Eagles teasing a return of the vintage look? Well, it’s complicated. Eagles Film Review: Tyler Steen is a perfectly capable starting guard – BGN Sometimes, it’s alright to just say a player is average right now. Not everything has to be a hot take about something being terrible or amazing. I don’t look at Steen and see a player the Eagles desperately need to replace. I also don’t see a clear long-term starting right guard who has already answered every question and deserves a 2nd contract as soon as possible. Right now, I think Steen is an average NFL starting guard. And that isn’t necessarily a criticism. Finding competent offensive linemen is difficult, and Steen has already shown that he possesses traits worth developing. His athletic ability is legitimate. He gets out of his stance extremely quickly, moves very well for his size, understands combination blocks, and can execute difficult assignments in space. His zone blocking in particular gives you something to work with, especially when you consider what Sean Mannion’s offense will ask from linemen. Five things to watch in the Eagles-Ravens preseason game – PhillyVoice 1) Who is first up between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee? Jalen Hurts hasn’t played in a preseason game since he took a late cheap shot out of bounds against the Jets in 2022. The Eagles are installing a new offense under Sean Mannion, which is perhaps a reason to get Hurts some live game reps, but I would be shocked if he took any snaps. So, who will start then? The Eagles have tried all offseason to say that Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee are co-QB2s. Well, unless they come out on the field together Saturday night, one will start, and one won’t. No matter how the Eagles spin it, the guy who starts is the QB2, and the other guy is the QB3. On Thursday, Nick Sirianni declined to answer who would play first, saying that the team still had to think it through. Dalton has gotten more second-team snaps than McKee this summer, so my guess is that it will be him. And how they play matters, for trade purposes, since one or the other could be dealt to another team. Trades and Roster Thoughts – Iggles Blitz TE now feels like the more complicated position group. Dallas Goedert is TE1 and Johnny Mundt is TE2. Rookie Eli Stowers has struggled this summer, but will clearly make the roster. Assuming the Eagles keep a fourth TE, you are likely choosing between Cam Latu and Grant Calcaterra. The argument for Latu is that he can play FB or TE, is the better blocker and is excellent on STs. Calcaterra is the more gifted receiver and athlete. I would keep Latu, since you already have Stowers who could develop into a role player for the passing game. The Eagles have had a strange loyalty to Calcaterra so you can’t write him off. The Eagles could trade for a TE. I’m sure they will be taking a long hard look around the league to see who might become available. Eagles preseason opener: 6 pressing questions ahead of Saturday’s game vs. Ravens – The Athletic Which player further down the depth chart should fans watch Saturday? Berman: Maximus Pulley is not a name fans might know yet, but he’s a sleeper for the 53-man roster. The Eagles lack safety depth. Pulley, an undrafted rookie from Wofford, has taken work with the second-team defense and could be in line to make the roster with a strong finish to the summer. Also, I mentioned Weru above. Bernard gets more of the attention; Weru, a native of Kenya, was an international rugby player who is now learning football. He’s shown flashes in camp rushing around the edge. One note on Bernard and Weru: the NFL doesn’t have any film on them. There’s no college tape. Any promise they show might entice teams to claim them if the Eagles plan to waive one or both and use the international player exemption on the practice squad. That’s why I’m also curious how much they play in this game. What Sean Mannion hopes to accomplish in his debut as a play caller – NBCSP This is the first time we’ll see rookies like Eli Stowers, Markel Bell and Cole Payton, the first time we’ll see newcomers like Willie Lampkin, A.J. Epenesa and Andy Dalton, the first time time we’ll see undrafted free agents like Maximus Pulley, Kapena Gushiken and Joshua Weru. Just as importantly, it’s the first time we’ll see Sean Mannion. Mannion, the Eagles’ rookie offensive coordinator, will make his debut as a play caller Saturday when the Eagles open the preseason at 7 p.m. against the Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore.] He won’t have Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith or Dallas Goedert as well as several other starters, but he’ll be under the microscope nonetheless as he calls plays for the first time for his newly installed West Coast Offense. “For ourselves as an offense, I want to see execution, I want to see play style,” Mannion said. “Those are the two things I want to see. We talk about play style a lot, the effort, the physicality, the strain to finish. ”Then offensively, just can we have a clean operation? Can we line up? Can we execute the offense? Those are the major things I’m looking for.” Mannion, the Eagles’ sixth play caller since 2021, modeled his scheme after the concepts made popular by Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay. Mannion coached in Green Bay under Matt LaFLeur, who coached under both Shanahan and McVay. Fantasy football rankings: Matt Bowen’s quarterback tiers for 2026 – ESPN Tier 2: Midtier QB1s. In this second tier, managers can land quality starters with upside potential. Daniels’ second pro season was limited by injuries (he played in only seven games), but he has the pocket presence and rushing ability to finish as a top-three scorer. Daniels scored 20.9 fantasy points per game in 2024, throwing 25 touchdowns and rushing for 891 yards with six touchdowns. … I’m higher on Williams than most because of his playmaking ability in Ben Johnson’s offense. Williams scored 18.1 fantasy points per game last season, and he can produce breakout weeks (eight games with 20 or more points). Another year of development under Johnson could put Williams in the top five. … Hurts gets a new playcaller in Philadelphia with coordinator Sean Mannion. Think of an offense that meshes the West Coast and spread systems, which should create more timing in the pass game. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Hurts will target receiver DeVonta Smith as his No. 1, and the team drafted wideout Makai Lemon. As always, Hurts provides scoring upside as a runner in the low red zone/goal line area of the field (37 rushing touchdowns over his past three seasons). … Prescott won’t give you high-end rushing numbers, but he plays in an explosive Dallas pass game featuring CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and tight end Jake Ferguson. Prescott scored 18.1 fantasy points per game last season, throwing for 4,555 yards (third most) and 30 touchdowns. title: Kirk Herbstreit raves about Steelers rookie after electric preseason debut
summary: Kaden Wetjen did not need long to make an impression in his first NFL game. The Pittsburgh Steelers rookie wide receiver and return specialist turned heads during Thursday night’s 28-9 preseason victory over the Green Bay Packers, catching two passes for 79 yards and a touchdown while displaying the explosive speed that made him one […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Kaden Wetjen #10 of the Pittsburgh Steelers is wrapped up by Nick Niemann #31 of the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kaden Wetjen did not need long to make an impression in his first NFL game. The Pittsburgh Steelers rookie wide receiver and return specialist turned heads during Thursday night’s 28-9 preseason victory over the Green Bay Packers, catching two passes for 79 yards and a touchdown while displaying the explosive speed that made him one of college football’s most dangerous return specialists. His performance was impressive enough to draw praise from ESPN college football analyst Kirk Herbstreit, who appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and offered a strong endorsement of the former Iowa standout. “Kaden Wetjen out of Iowa is a freak,” Herbstreit said. “I’m excited to see what the Steelers are gonna be able to do this year.” "Kaden Wetjen out of Iowa is a freak.. I'm excited to see what the Steelers are gonna be able to do this year" ~ @KirkHerbstreit #PMSLive https://t.co/R4RoR9055v pic.twitter.com/WOZEdyAKCl — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 14, 2026 Wetjen’s biggest play came on a 74-yard catch-and-run from fellow rookie Drew Allar. Wetjen caught the pass in stride, turned on his speed and raced deep into Green Bay territory, immediately demonstrating that his value to Pittsburgh may extend well beyond special teams. Allar and Wetjen connected again later in the game, this time on a five-yard touchdown pass. The performance was particularly notable because Wetjen was selected by the Steelers with the 121st overall pick in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft largely because of his special-teams ability. He was widely viewed as one of the premier return specialists in the draft, but his limited receiving production at Iowa left questions about whether he could become a legitimate offensive contributor. Those questions became considerably more interesting after his preseason debut. Wetjen also handled return duties against Green Bay, recording three kickoff returns for 61 yards and two punt returns for 10 yards. At Iowa, Wetjen established himself as one of the nation’s most dynamic returners. He became the first two-time winner of the Jet Award, earned consensus All-American recognition in 2025 and led the nation in kickoff-return yardage while averaging 26.8 yards per punt return. He also scored touchdowns as a rusher, receiver and on both kickoff and punt returns during his final college season. That background made Wetjen an intriguing fit for a Steelers team looking to improve its return game. But his ability to contribute offensively could ultimately make the fourth-round investment look even more valuable. Let us know what you think in the comments . summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ revamped wide receiver room could remain shorthanded when the team returns to Acrisure Stadium for its second preseason game. Head coach Mike McCarthy said injured wide receivers DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. will be “hard pressed to work this week,” according to Alan Saunders of Steelers Now, without providing a definitive […]
full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ revamped wide receiver room could remain shorthanded when the team returns to Acrisure Stadium for its second preseason game. Head coach Mike McCarthy said injured wide receivers DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. will be “hard pressed to work this week,” according to Alan Saunders of Steelers Now, without providing a definitive timeline for either player’s return. Mike McCarthy said that injured #Steelers WRs DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. will be “hard pressed to work this week,” but did not offer a firm timeline beyond that. — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) August 15, 2026 That creates an important situation for the Steelers with the New York Jets scheduled to visit Pittsburgh on Friday, Aug. 21. Both Metcalf and Pittman were already held out of Pittsburgh’s preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, meaning their availability for the Jets game will depend heavily on how quickly they progress over the coming days. With the preseason serving as an opportunity to establish roles and evaluate the bottom of the roster, additional absences would give players such as Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson and Kaden Wetjen another chance to earn meaningful snaps. Wilson, in particular, was expected to see an increased role with the veteran receivers sidelined but had only one reception for seven yards against Green Bay. There is also a bigger-picture consideration. Pittsburgh does not need Metcalf or Pittman to prove anything in a preseason game if the medical staff believes either player needs additional recovery time. The priority will be having the two veterans healthy for the regular season rather than forcing them onto the field in August. Still, another missed game would mean less time for Rodgers and Pittsburgh’s new receiving corps to develop chemistry in live-game situations. Rodgers did not play in the preseason opener, while rookie Drew Allar and the other quarterbacks handled the workload in Pittsburgh’s 28-9 victory. For now, Metcalf and Pittman should be viewed as uncertain for the Jets game rather than ruled out. Their practice participation throughout the week will likely provide the clearest indication of whether they have a chance to return. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Winners and Losers from the Seahawks’ clunky preseason loss to Cowboys
summary: The Seattle Seahawks were, shall we say, not at their sharpest in their 17-7 preseason opening loss against the Dallas Cowboys. It’s not unexpected when it’s preseason and the starters are absent, but Mike Macdonald definitely was not pleased with the performance on the night. And why would he? A lot of penalties (21 enforced), […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks running back George Holani (36) carries the ball against the Dallas Cowboys during the first half at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Seattle Seahawks were, shall we say, not at their sharpest in their 17-7 preseason opening loss against the Dallas Cowboys. It’s not unexpected when it’s preseason and the starters are absent, but Mike Macdonald definitely was not pleased with the performance on the night. And why would he? A lot of penalties (21 enforced), a lot of ugly mistakes, and some disjointed play that a head coach will not accept even from the bottom end of a 90-man roster. But it wasn’t all bad and boring! Heck, the game ended fairly quickly even with all of the flags. And the bad football should make for great coaching staff audio on the next Hard Knocks episode. Anyway, it’s time for our first Winners and Losers of the 2026 NFL preseason! Seattle Seahawks Winners Tyrice Knight is playing his way back into the defensive rotation Last season, Knight went from starting in Week 1 to splitting snaps with Drake Thomas to special teams duties by about midseason. Knight was sticky in coverage, tackling soundly, and just generally all over the field in a good way. Ernest Jones IV and Drake Thomas are the starting backers, but Knight can be used off-ball and on the edge, so I can see a scenario where he’s in on some sub-packages. Montorie Foster Jr may at least be WR7 Cody White probably has the edge as that last wide receiver on the depth chart, but be on the lookout for Montorie Foster Jr. He caught a touchdown on the opening drive, had a nice block on a George Holani run, and was a step away from a big play to start the second half if not for a Drew Lock overthrow. It’s telling that he was getting early reps over Ricky White III, who’s also had a good training camp. Foster did have a bad drop in the fourth quarter, so that’s one demerit, but he finished with a team-high five catches for 36 yards and the lone TD. The bad news is WR7 probably doesn’t exist on a 53-man roster, but if Foster clears waivers he might be an immediate practice squad re-sign. Alternatively, keep Foster, waive White, he’ll more likely clear waivers, and Cody ends up back on the PS. George Holani a rare bright spot on offense Seattle had no explosive runs from its running backs on Saturday night, but Holani was at least a net positive for his ability to break tackles and showcase that hard-nosed style. Playing behind a second-string offensive line, Holani led the Seahawks with 42 rushing yards on 12 carries. This year will be the first time he won’t have to compete for a roster spot. Noah Igbinoghene has a solid Seahawks debut The journeyman corner had Marquez Valdes-Scantling locked down on a deep shot in the opening quarter, as well as a pressure on a blitz that forced Sam Howell into a bad third-down throw. I think he’s in good position to make the 53 alongside Nehemiah Pritchett. Terrion Arnold’s addition will make things even more interesting in the cornerback room. Rashad Rochelle has a special teams highlight Seattle has no shortage of returner options on special teams. Rashad Rochelle had a 52-yard punt return in the third quarter that got the fans and the Seahawks sideline excited. His path to the roster is nigh on impossible, but practice squad? Maybe. At the very least, he put something on film for the league to notice. Seattle Seahawks Losers The non-Josh Jones swing tackles were a horror show The second- and third-team offensive lines were brutal at times. Logan Brown, Bobby Hart, and Amari Kight all had some rough pass pro reps. Kight committed a hold that negated a fourth-down conversion, Hart was just horrific, and Brown stacked penalty upon penalty. Brown turned a 4th and 3 into a 4th and 8 punt after a false start, which I noticed he had issues with in the one practice I saw. There’s Josh Jones and then there’s the rest. Seattle’s edge rush depth underwhelms I had concerns about this at training camp and nothing happened in this game to dissuade my opinion. Mike Morris playing big edge is very much a preseason-only thing. Connor O’Toole provided next to nothing. Aidan Hubbard and Marvin Jones Jr were not very impactful. Jalan Gaines at least had a couple of nice plays, a near-sack, and a run TFL. The season doesn’t come down to any of those guys getting serious snaps, but it also underscores that with major question marks at the position in 2027, there doesn’t seem to be a gem deep in the depth chart. The third-string interior defensive line wasn’t much better There was not a whole lot to champion watching Bubba Thomas and J.R. Singleton. Deven Eastern had one notable play against the run but otherwise it was the Cowboys’ backup offensive line getting the better of Seattle’s backup d-line in the trenches. Shemar Jean-Charles was on the struggle bus Whenever the Seahawks make the Terrion Arnold signing official, someone has to be let go on the roster. I think Shemar Jean-Charles helped make the decision easier with his performance, which included multiple conversions allowed, an obvious pass interference on third down, and a long touchdown allowed to close out the first half. Drew Lock was not sharp The touchdown pass to Foster aside—really, the opening drive in totality—Lock was not on his game. He was 9/13 for just 40 yards on the night, with some ugly misses to Jake Bobo and Montorie Foster. I’m not all that worried but it was not a convincing display for the veteran quarterback. Jalen Milroe finishes with single digit net passing yards With Lock and Milroe alternating every two series, it was actually a negative for Milroe in the sense that there were enough long drives to shorten his opportunities. The second-year QB finished 5/8 for 36 yards, another 36 on the ground, and 27 sack yards lost. A 9-net yard passing performance isn’t something I will champion. Milroe didn’t play poorly, in my opinion, but he rarely shined. In quick, “get the ball out” situations, he was on time and accurate. I liked the improvised play to Jake Bobo on fourth down, and it’s not his fault Amari Kight got dinged for holding. When it was a longer developing play it felt like nothing was in rhythm, and for every impressive scramble there was a sack. The offensive line did not help matters but some of those pressures and sacks looked like Milroe not being decisive as far as whether to throw or look to run. If you were hoping for tape of Milroe showcasing himself as a franchise player or even just QB2 over Lock, this wasn’t a good start. Preseason is still young and there will be two more games and a joint practice for him to showcase his development. Bryce Cabeldue is firmly on the bubble This has nothing to do with his actual game performance, of which my recollection is hazy. It’s telling that Cabeldue was with the third-team offense deep into the game, which is normally a sign that you’re fighting to make the team. Beau Stephens quickly got some run with the second-team, while Christian Haynes and Mason Richman were other nominal second-team guards. Cabeldue may be the odd man out come roster cuts, especially given Richman has more positional versatility as G/C. Final Notes Rylie Mills had some beastly moments as a pass rusher, but not necessarily as a run defender. There were some times where he got stymied at the line. It’s still good that he had extended playing time when he had limited reps last season. I’d caution that in a normal game, Mills would be lined up alongside Byron Murphy II or Leonard Williams and not Brandon Pili or Jared Ivey. There was a crunching block from Brock Lampe on Justin Jones’ near-touchdown run in the fourth quarter. I will be interested in seeing how he performs over the next couple of weeks and whether he becomes the starting fullback over Brady Russell, whose job should be safe for special teams reasons alone. title: Seahawks vs. Cowboys score: Seattle starts preseason with sloppy loss
summary: The Seattle Seahawks (0-1) got their 2026 preseason off and running at Lumen Field against the Dallas Cowboys (1-0), but unfortunately they couldn’t get off to a winning start. A bright start led by Drew Lock and Montorie Foster steadily fizzled out, as the Cowboys rode two impressive Camden Brown touchdowns into a 17-7 win. […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Tyrice Knight #48 of the Seattle Seahawks hits Michael Trigg #46 of the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter of the NFL preseason game at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks (0-1) got their 2026 preseason off and running at Lumen Field against the Dallas Cowboys (1-0), but unfortunately they couldn’t get off to a winning start. A bright start led by Drew Lock and Montorie Foster steadily fizzled out, as the Cowboys rode two impressive Camden Brown touchdowns into a 17-7 win. Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe alternated every two possessions and collectively failed to clear 100 yards passing. Milroe’s sacks meant Seattle finished the night with just 49 net passing yards. The run game at least had some bright spots without being explosive, as George Holani and Velus Jones Jr had a few quality carries. Seattle’s defense did not generate much pass rush, failed to record a sack on either Joe Milton or Sam Howell, and it was a night to forget for Shemar Jean-Charles, who gave up a touchdown and committed a costly pass interference penalty that resulted in a field goal. The positives included Tyrice Knight and Patrick O’Connell at linebacker, Rylie Mills getting a couple of pressures, and Noah Igbinoghene having a good first half in coverage and as a blitzer. Oh well, at least these games don’t count. The Seahawks started the game off on offense, with Drew Lock leading Seattle on a 13-play, 80-yard drive. There was some help from Cowboys cornerback Caelen Carson, who committed a drive-extending pass interference on the first third-down of the game, followed by a face mask on what was otherwise a Drew Lock scramble for a first down. There wasn’t any penalty help needed on this third-down touchdown. Lock found Montorie Foster Jr on a great throw-and-catch in the back of the end zone. Foster saw the ball late but still pulled it in for the first touchdown of the night. Drew Lock throws a DART for 6️⃣ DALvsSEA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Fo71Mi1DIq — NFL (@NFL) August 16, 2026 Former Seahawks quarterback Sam Howell got the start for the Cowboys, leading a field goal drive on his second possession. Multiple conversions to Jonathan Mingo (plus a pass interference on Shemar Jean-Charles) helped march Dallas down the field. Noah Igbinoghene’s blitz forced Howell into a poor throw on third down, securing a Seahawks red zone stop after 16 plays. Tyrice Knight, Mike Morris, and Patrick O’Connell all had splash plays on the drive. Jalen Milroe’s first series of preseason came at about the 11-minute mark of the second quarter. It was an inauspicious start when he had a botched exchange with Olu Oluwatimi but was able to pounce on the fumble. He erased the mistake with a third-down dart to Jake Bobo to move the sticks. Faced with 3rd and 11, Milroe evaded pressure, tip-toed the sideline and got 12 yards for another conversion. On a 4th and 2 in the red zone, Milroe scrambled out of pressure and improvised a pass to Bobo for another first down, but Amari Kight was dinged for holding. Jason Myers hooked the subsequent 45-yard field goal wide right. In the two-minute drill, Seattle’s pass rush didn’t really affect Howell much, and they paid the price. Camden Brown was on the receiving end of a deep shot from Howell, who exploited Shemar Jean-Charles in coverage for the go-ahead touchdown. 10-7 Cowboys at halftime. . @CamdenBrown7 wrestles for the TD 💪 📺: #DALvsSEA on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx89QL pic.twitter.com/IqkRvShQ6R — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 16, 2026 Joe Milton started the second half for the Cowboys and he led a touchdown drive right away. Seattle’s third-team defense was largely out there and didn’t particularly impress. Camden Brown sure as hell impressed, scoring a one-handed touchdown on rookie Michael Dansby to extend Dallas’ lead to 17-7. CAMDEN BROWN WITH A CRAZY ONE-HANDED TD GRAB 😱 DALvsSEA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sj2vglr6py — NFL (@NFL) August 16, 2026 After the Seahawks stopped Dallas on the next Cowboys offensive possession, Rashad Rochelle made the most of his opportunity on punt return duties. He ran the ball back 52 yards to set the Seahawks up in great field position. Rashad Rochelle just flipped the field ⚡ 52 yards. pic.twitter.com/K3QJVbzwbt — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 16, 2026 Drew Lock and company wasted the field position by turning it over on downs on 4th and 4. Logan Brown got whipped and committed a hold, and Lock threw short of the sticks anyway. Amid a series of penalties on both teams, the Seahawks recorded the first turnover of the game. Cowboys punt returner Traeshon Holden inexplicably decided to return a punt at his own 2-yard line with the whole Seahawks team already in his face. Shockingly, he lost the ball and T.J. Harden recovered. OUR BALL! GET LOUD, @12s pic.twitter.com/2DOSYt4uBP — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 16, 2026 Seattle did not score points off of this, somehow. Harden had three carries, didn’t score, and Milroe got sacked on fourth and goal. Dallas was able to run the final six minutes and 32 seconds off the clock, which is nice when you realize everyone in attendance could go out for dinner with the sun not yet set. 14 yd sack for @IsaiahLand716 ‼️ 📺: #DALvsSEA on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx89QL pic.twitter.com/qiVKoNAdTe — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 16, 2026 Full Box Score Seahawks injury report It looked like Bobby Hart was grabbing his right hand in the second quarter, otherwise there was nothing easily noticeable regarding injuries. Next week’s opponent The Seahawks take on the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Aug. 23 at 5 pm PT. It will be nationally televised on FOX.

After taking more than seven minutes off the clock, wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr. scored the first touchdown of the preseason after some key first downs on the ground by Lock and running back George Holani. title: Why even the young Seahawks will be an important preseason evaluation
summary: Is preseason worth watching? For an outfit that just took the league title, you’d think the backups wouldn’t really matter in the grand scheme of things… but they do! From the collective horse’s (Hawk’s?) mouth itself. Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald on the rookie class: “This has been a great rookie class. They’re different […]
full_text: Is preseason worth watching? For an outfit that just took the league title, you’d think the backups wouldn’t really matter in the grand scheme of things… but they do! From the collective horse’s (Hawk’s?) mouth itself. Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald on the rookie class : “This has been a great rookie class. They’re different than last year; it’s a little bit smaller group, but different personality. Those common threads that we want in our program, like respect, honest work… they’re very talented in their own right. They have all those things.” He goes on to talk about how, “one of the messages to the team right now is: ‘this is a new team. Even though you are a rookie there is a responsibility to add to who we’re gonna become. We don’t know what that’s going to be yet, so we’re trying to create that space for them to be themselves and add to our team so that we become the best version of ourselves.’” Macdonald ended that thought by stating plainly: “We’re going to need them this year, so our vets are doing a great job of fostering as well.” One of those vets is safety, Julian Love. A versatile, cerebral and reliable player on the back-end, Love spoke on the same concept , of having a “new team.” “Those pillars we had last year… it’s like, okay. Do we want to create new ones? Do we want to have that same kind of umbrella, but really think differently about what makes it up, who we are in this current day? … I think we want to shape this thing and learn it and start from ground level and incorporate everybody along.” Love says, “This whole unit—everyone is going to be incorporate in how we build things. It’s a conscious choice. It could be real easy to be like: ‘let’s keep on going with what we did last year!’” It’s not just the rookies (Jadarian Price, Bud Clark and Julian Neal’s pro debuts excite the PNW mind), it would be nice to see some of the new additions get some run and get into the flow of this team. Emmanuel Wilson at running back, Noah Igbinoghene as an inside/outside DB, and Dante Fowler Jr. as a 4th established edge rusher all have shots to be contributors. Fowler Jr. “wanted to be here.” Fowler discussed the idea of adding to the formula : “They’re bringing all the new guys and the young guys along really well,” Fowler said. “But you know like I just fall in line and do what I’m supposed to do. They already had a great defense before we got here, and they won a Super Bowl. It was the best defense in the world last year. So my job is to just fall in line and do whatever I gotta do to make this defense upgrade a little bit more.” Hard Knocks Ep.1 Mike Macdonald is shown addressing his team in the debut of the Seattle Seahawks’ version of Hard Knocks. He talked to his team about how Michael Jordan was always supremely talented, but he didn’t win a title until Phil Jackson became coach and started structuring the team around “team basketball.” Jordan then went on to achieve a 3-peat. Macdonald goes on to state that he believes that “the secret sauce of the NFL is connection.” The directive is clear: to make it back to the mountaintop, and go on a special run, Macdonald believes that they’ll need to commit to team ball. Coach’s money is where his mouth is later in the episode, when a fight broke out. Second year guard, Bryce Cabeldue went after safety Rodney Thomas II after he decked a ball-carrying Velus Jones Jr. Bedlam ensues, when Tyrice Knight, Leonard Williams, and Derick Hall subsequently came to RTII’s defense, going at Cabeldue before Josh Jones finally came in to stand up for B.C. Josh Jobe came in and even swung a helmet. Cameras showed Coach Macdonald addressing the fight at a macro level, then addressing a hurtful comment that was said (Brady Russell to Derick Hall, according to DC, Aden Durde) at the micro level. He was more worried about preserving harmony and team flow than the actual physical fight. The slogan, 12-as-1 is personified in each level of the organization. John Schneider talked, pre-draft, about the search for players that “want to come in and compete at a high level and not be enamored by the guys they just saw playing in the Super Bowl. In a less formal instance (the league’s annual meeting) John Boyle quoted Schneider as saying they want guys who possess the attitude of: ‘I want to take their jobs.’ Are those types of dawgs present among the young and the (current) backups on this roster? Remember how guys like Josh Jobe, Drake Thomas, Ty Okada, Brandon Pili, Jalen Sundell, George Holani, Eric Saubert and even A.J. Barner rose from relative obscurity to help push the Seattle Seahawks towards a Lombardi Trophy ? That shouldn’t stop now, and it feels like Schneider is on a mission to make sure he learns from being in this position before. This time last year, Tyrice Knight (if healthy) over Drake Thomas felt like a given. Mike Macdonald has been quoted as saying, “Players are allowed to get better, our guys are going to get better, they’re going to develop.” You love to hear it. Who will be the ones to make unexpected contributions this year? The Seattle Seahawks are banking on those coming through in multiple spots. The reality of a rough and tumble NFL says that they are a necessity. Some are hungry. Others are starving to make their mark. "Anytime I'm tired now, I just think 'A year ago I would have done anything to get the opportunity to go out and play.'" Rylie Mills describes to @BrockHuard & @TheMikeSalk how missing most of last season has helped shape his perspective and motivation heading into his 2nd… pic.twitter.com/J4yrUcgOG7 — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) August 6, 2026 Seahawks Fan Fest While rookie DB’s Bud Clark (who Mike Macdonald called , “a really smart guy”) and Michael Dansby have gotten early training camp hype (and made plays in the Lumen Field atmosphere as well), two pass catchers caught my eye at Seahawks Fan Fest 2026. I saw 2nd-year TE, Elijah Arroyo catch a red zone TD and a competition period one-on-one pass against Clark, and I saw 6th-Round WR, Emmanuel Henderson Jr. catch a red zone TD and a competition period one-on-one pass against Dansby. Not overreacting to manufactured situations, but Arroyo and Henderson are two players I will keep my eyes on in the passing game. Henderson Jr., in particular enters battle against Cody White, Montorie Foster Jr. and Ricky White III for possibly the last wide receiver spot on the roster. I saw OG’s, Bryce Cabeldue and Christian Haynes early on, working with the 2nd-team offensive line. Can Haynes ever find any of that potential that surrounded him coming out of the 3rd Round in 2024? How do Mason Richman and Beau Stephens figure in? Amari Kight will have to fight with all his might if he wants to ensure a spot, with (at least) veteran OT, Bobby Hart now in the fold. Depth on the O-line is a must, and a battle royale could baptize this unit by fire. After the in-stadium scrimmage/practice, new free agent running back, Emmanuel Wilson was asked about a guy that will most likely be his main competition for snaps come the season opener. J.J. McCarthy went slightly viral for his answer to a similar question in Minnesota, but Wilson struck a different (more effusive) tone: “He’s got great feet. And also, the way he tracks the ball when he’s catching, he’s wonderful. Jadarian, he’s got a lot to him. He’s going to be a great back in this league.” Two players who may have bigger roles on their respective sides of the ball looked good at times as well: CB, Nehemiah Pritchett and WR, Tory Horton. AJ Finley and Rodney Thomas II may be competing for the final safety spot, and they both came up with interceptions! These are just a few of the storylines that I can’t wait to add more data and insight to. This Seahawks team has shown investment in a complete roster in everything they do. There’s a long history of even undrafted guys stepping up and becoming factors. This team doesn’t feel like it is going to lose its edge anytime soon. Hard…

Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3UsROvG1l4 — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Unfortunately, his day would end on a cart after suffering what appeared to be a right knee injury on Jaxson Dart’s touchdown pass to rookie Malachi Fields. Here’s Jamal Adams’ injury (#32 in the slot) Looks like non-contact right knee pic.twitter.com/f2K2z5lXUD — Krauser (@Krauserrific) August 15, 2026 Jamal Adams being carted off the field. pic.twitter.com/a6zafYMxrO — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 15, 2026 The reports from MetLife Stadium do not sound promising for Adams and the severity of his injury. He has already been declared out for the game, which in preseason can be precautionary but may speak to something likely more serious. A cart is coming for S Jamal Adams. Teammates had been checking on him in the medical tent. Josh Metellus and Byron Murphy Jr. looked pretty upset. — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) August 15, 2026 As Seahawks fans know all too well, Adams had a deep injury history in Seattle, including multiple shoulder injuries in his first two seasons with the team, as well as a torn quad tendon in the 2022 Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos. He was shut down for the final few weeks of the 2023 season due to ongoing knee issues, and was subsequently released in the 2024 offseason . Adams has bounced around the league post-Seahawks, barely playing for the Tennessee Titans before a short stint with the Detroit Lions. When Adams reunited with Pete Carroll on the Raiders in 2025, he actually played all 17 games in a reserve linebacker role. Even if the Raiders were a disaster, it was clearly a personal accomplishment for Adams to make it through the full season. Playing in Brian Flores’ comically aggressive, blitz-heavy defense, Adams had a chance to really rejuvenate his career as an off-ball linebacker. Unless the diagnosis comes through with something promising, this could be yet another devastating injury for the 30-year-old.
