title: 5 things to watch in Seahawks’ preseason opener vs. Cowboys
summary: It’s finally here! Seattle Seahawks football is back, albeit in preseason mode, but would you rather watch preseason Seahawks football or no Seahawks football at all? I thought so. And we get another year of Michael Bennett and Michael Robinson on the mic. While the key starters will be out for the opener against the […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JULY 25: Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks throws the ball during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on July 25, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s finally here! Seattle Seahawks football is back, albeit in preseason mode, but would you rather watch preseason Seahawks football or no Seahawks football at all? I thought so. And we get another year of Michael Bennett and Michael Robinson on the mic. While the key starters will be out for the opener against the Dallas Cowboys, there’s still plenty to monitor throughout preseason. The Seahawks maintained much of their Super Bowl roster from last season, but it’s the bottom-end depth chart battles that will be super fascinating to see play out. Here’s what I’ll be watching closely throughout tonight’s game at Lumen Field. How much Jalen Milroe plays and who he plays with Mike Macdonald already indicated on Friday that Sam Darnold won’t play and Drew Lock will start, but a change from last year is a planned rotation of Lock and Milroe throughout the game. In other words, Milroe won’t just be coming in with the third-team unit at some stage in the third quarter. While Milroe won’t be playing with “established starters” in preseason, we could see him handing the ball off to George Holani, or throwing the ball to Elijah Arroyo, and that would be a step up from throwing almost exclusively to guys who did not crack last year’s 53-man roster. Having seen him plenty at training camp, Milroe looks improved in a controlled intrasquad environment. Can he take that next step in his development against actual opposition? The biggest task for Milroe is to show enough development as a passer to justify being an active game day quarterback. There can’t be a Milroe package if he’s no threat to throw the ball. This is the opportunity to add a new wrinkle to the offense. Will anyone stake their claim for the sixth wide receiver spot? If we assume Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, Cooper Kupp, Tory Horton, and Jake Bobo are the main five receivers, who’s going to be that sixth guy? Will there even be a sixth receiver? Let’s assume there is or else I’ve wasted a paragraph. Cody White is the mainstay who has oscillated between practice squad and active roster for a couple of years. Ricky White III and Montorie Foster have both been very impressive in training camp. All three of these players also are special teams factors. Emmanuel Henderson Jr. is the sixth-round rookie with deep kick return experience, albeit with not the best training camp in terms of wide receiver work. The only complicating factor for WR6 is if the Seahawks opt to roster an extra tight end or running back or even another defensive back, in which case we’d probably see a lot of practice squad elevations for multiple receivers. Otherwise, WR6 is up for grabs. Is the Rylie Mills hype real or should we be sued for false advertising? Throughout our week at training camp and just reading reports from Seahawks beat writers, it’s clear that Rylie Mills has stood out for his performances on the practice field. Mills wowed everyone with his Super Bowl sack, but the big picture with the former Notre Dame standout is this is his first normal camp and healthy offseason. The ACL tear is behind him and he looks stupidly strong against Seattle’s first-team OL. Rylie Mills is going to get preseason reps and frankly, he should. Mills played a grand total of 34 defensive snaps last season (including the Super Bowl), so he shouldn’t get “established starter” protections. There’s plenty of room for development for Mills and there’s obviously going to be demand to see him prove it on a more consistent basis, even if versus preseason opposition. If Mills is, bare minimum, another viable interior pass rushing threat, that’s a bonus for the Seahawks defense given they don’t have (at least I don’t think) a generational superstar edge rusher on the team. It also can justify more rotation on the d-line if there’s another playable body who can function as a 3- or 5-tech. Can Velus Jones Jr make a shock push for a roster spot? Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: The Seattle Seahawks running back room is a bit banged up. We’re not even into the first preseason game yet and there are some players on the mend. Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson, Jacardia Wright, and Zach Charbonnet are all hurt. Charbonnet won’t be around until October at the earliest, whereas none of Price, Wilson, or Wright is due to play on Saturday. Assuming George Holani has a limited role as someone whose roster spot is not under threat, who’s going to be running the ball for the Seahawks in their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys? Enter Velus Jones Jr. Justifiably cast off by the Chicago Bears after doing very little as a receiver and returner, struggling with fumbles and drops, Jones has seemingly reinvented himself as a “Joker” type of RB/WR hybrid who can also return kicks. Velus is by no means suddenly an every-down back, but his prior WR experience combined with his speed could make him a sneaky change-of-pace option for a handful of snaps. If there is any avenue for Velus to crack the 53 (at least while Charbonnet is out), it’s while the other backs ahead of him are either unavailable or will have minimal preseason carries. The crowded Seahawks secondary This room is so crowded even without Terrion Arnold in the mix. Now that he is part of the team, that complicates matters a bit for some roster bubble players at cornerback. In the meantime, it looks like replacing Riq Woolen might not be as simple as it may seem. Arnold is part of the equation, as are Nehemiah Pritchett, Noah Igbinoghene, Michael Dansby, Andre Fuller, and even Shamar Jean-Charles. Jordan Washington is also on the roster but he’s the definition of a camp body. At safety, it looks like Ty Okada has the starting job alongside Julian Love on lock. Bud Clark will presumably get some reps here and there, while Nick Emmanwori will eventually be back from his ankle injury. If Seattle keeps five safeties, then there’s one spot for D’Anthony Bell, Maxen Hook, A.J. Finley, and Rodney Thomas II. Those will be some tough decisions for Mike Macdonald and staff to make. Who will you be most interested in watching in Seahawks vs. Cowboys? Tell us below in the comments! Join the conversation! title: Seahawks sign Devon Witherspoon to record-setting $132 million contract extension
summary: A foundational piece of Mike Macdonald’s Seattle Seahawks is here to stay. The Seahawks and cornerback Devon Witherspoon agreed to a four-year, $132 million contract extension with more than $101 million in guarantees, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Saturday. The deal will make Witherspoon the highest-paid cornerback in league history, topping the two-year, $62.2 million […]
full_text: A foundational piece of Mike Macdonald’s Seattle Seahawks is here to stay. The Seahawks and cornerback Devon Witherspoon agreed to a four-year, $132 million contract extension with more than $101 million in guarantees, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Saturday . The deal will make Witherspoon the highest-paid cornerback in league history, topping the two-year, $62.2 million deal signed by the Cleveland Browns’ Denzel Ward earlier this offseason. Witherspoon’s extension comes after a breakthrough of sorts, with NFL Network and ESPN’s Ian Rapoport saying on Inside Training Camp on Saturday, Aug. 8, that a deal wasn’t close. With the All-Pro corner entering the fourth season of his rookie deal, there was certainly motivation on both the player and team’s side to get it done ahead of the regular season or, worse, before a contract year during his fifth-year option. All eyes for cornerback contracts now turn to Christian Gonzalez of the New England Patriots, who has the same agent as Witherspoon and is seeking his own big deal. Since Seattle selected Witherspoon with the fifth overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, he has emerged as one of the league’s best cornerbacks and a crucial weapon in Macdonald’s defense. The three-time Pro Bowler and 2025 second-team All-Pro has notched two picks and 32 pass breakups across three seasons, with his versatility highlighted by 4.5 career sacks and a pair of forced fumbles, to boot. With linebacker Ernest Jones locked in for another two seasons, Derick Hall newly extended , and Nick Emmanwori still on his rookie deal, the Seahawks have key young pieces in place for the foreseeable future. Now, after Witherspoon’s extension, they have potentially the most important player on their Super Bowl-winning defense tied down too.

title: Seahawks Reacts Results: Seattle’s defense backed to lead NFC West in sacks
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The latest SB Nation Reacts results offer an interesting vote of confidence in the Seattle Seahawks’ […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 8: Byron Murphy II #91 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates with Leonard Williams #99 during the fourth quarter of the NFL Super Bowl LX football game against the New England Patriots at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The latest SB Nation Reacts results offer an interesting vote of confidence in the Seattle Seahawks’ defensive philosophy. When asked which NFC West team will finish the regular season with the most sacks, 56% of respondents picked Seattle , comfortably ahead of the Los Angeles Rams at 41%. The Arizona Cardinals received 3%, while the San Francisco 49ers finished with just 1%. At first glance, Seattle’s position at the top is somewhat surprising considering the arms race taking place within the division. The Rams made one of the biggest moves of the offseason by acquiring Myles Garrett , the reigning Defensive Player of the Year who set an NFL single-season record with 23 sacks in 2025. Los Angeles also remains in the middle of the increasingly serious possibility of Aaron Donald returning from retirement. And yet, even with that collection of star power, the Rams trail Seattle by 15 percentage points. That speaks to something important about how the Seahawks generate pressure. Seattle doesn’t necessarily need one player to dominate the sack leaderboard for its defensive front to be one of the NFL’s most productive units. In fact, that’s almost the point. Mike Macdonald’s defense is built around creating problems for offensive protections rather than simply asking one elite pass rusher to win his matchup every down. The Seahawks can use overload fronts, simulated pressures, stunts, rotations and creative pressure packages to manipulate where the offense believes the pressure is coming from. That versatility allows Seattle to generate pressure with different players and from different locations on the defense. Macdonald’s system has repeatedly emphasized making every defender a potential rusher while maintaining the ability to drop players into coverage. That’s why the idea of Seattle leading the NFC West in sacks is much more plausible than the idea of one Seahawks defender winning the individual sack title. That could once again be the identity of this unit in 2026. Seattle may not have the obvious individual advantage that comes with having a Myles Garrett, or potentially an Aaron Donald, on the defensive line. But Macdonald’s scheme gives the Seahawks another way to create pressure: make the quarterback and the offensive line wrong before the snap. The most surprising result may actually be San Francisco finishing with only 1% of the vote. The 49ers have traditionally been associated with an aggressive and talented defensive front, making such a low number stand out. But injuries could have influenced the perception of their pass rush, particularly the latest setback involving Nick Bosa . Bosa is currently considered week-to-week with tendinitis in his right knee as he continues his recovery from the ACL injury that ended his 2025 season. He has already missed multiple practices, and San Francisco’s pass rush struggled when he was unavailable last season. That context makes the 1% figure easier to understand. It may not represent a lack of respect for the 49ers’ defensive talent as much as uncertainty surrounding the health and availability of their most important pass rusher. Arizona, meanwhile, received just 3%, leaving Seattle and Los Angeles responsible for 97% of the total vote . Ultimately, this poll feels particularly fitting for Seattle because of the way Macdonald wants his defense to operate. The Seahawks aren’t necessarily built around having the player who finishes the season with 15 or 20 sacks; they’re built around creating pressure as a unit. One week it might be a defensive lineman winning an isolated matchup. The next, it could be a linebacker attacking a protection adjustment. On another snap, a defensive back can become the unexpected rusher. That unpredictability is part of Macdonald’s defensive identity. So while Seattle probably won’t have the NFC West’s most obvious candidate to lead the league in individual sacks, finishing with the most sacks as a team is entirely realistic . The results suggest voters see it the same way. And perhaps that’s the most interesting part: even after the Rams made a blockbuster move for Myles Garrett and opened the door for one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history to potentially return, Seattle remains the team most people expect to finish on top. title: Robbie Ouzts neck injury not believed to be career-threatening
summary: Seattle Seahawks fullback Robbie Ouzts saw his Super Bowl-winning rookie season end during the playoffs due to a neck injury, and he will miss all of 2026 after he was placed on injured reserve due to that ongoing neck problem. It’s natural to speculate the worst case scenario of a neck injury potentially ending someone’s […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - DECEMBER 28: Seattle Seahawks running back Robbie Ouzts (40) during an NFL football game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Carolina Panthers on December 28, 2025 at Bank of America stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Seattle Seahawks fullback Robbie Ouzts saw his Super Bowl-winning rookie season end during the playoffs due to a neck injury, and he will miss all of 2026 after he was placed on injured reserve due to that ongoing neck problem . It’s natural to speculate the worst case scenario of a neck injury potentially ending someone’s career, as was the case for Seahawks from yesteryear like Cliff Avril, Kam Chancellor, and Mack Strong. If there is any sign of optimism that this isn’t the end of the road for Ouzts after such a short professional stint, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald provided a glimmer of hope at Friday’s press conference. “It’s an unfortunate situation,” Macdonald said of Ouzts’ injury. “It’s just someone you are really rooting for. To our knowledge, there is a recovery process, and this should help his career long-term. That’s why we are doing it.” For what it’s worth, Emerald City Spectrum’s Corbin Smith was told earlier in the week that , “The organization remains optimistic that this won’t be a career-threatening issue and that he will be able to return healthy in 2027.” The Seahawks currently have Brady Russell as the lead fullback, albeit a bit undersized for the position, hence he’s more of a fullback/tight end hybrid. Brock Lampe, a former Northern Illinois fullback who was coached by current Seahawks running backs coach Thomas Hammock, was added to the roster last week .

(Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling? “The team has long shied away from plugging any of its young wideouts into one position, instead asking them to learn all three spots (F, X or Z) before deciding where to put them. That workload can faze some players, but coaches and teammates have said Stribling isn’t bothered. The strong impression he left on the team was a result of the routine Stribling developed after the offseason program. Along with the studying film each day, he would say every playcall out loud or have someone recite it to him. Then, he would write it down or draw the play out so he could visualize it. Stribling would go through the playbook repeatedly, occasionally asking his mother or his girlfriend to quiz him or call out plays. He even joined fellow wideout Jordan Watkins for throwing sessions with Purdy and Jones in Nashville prior to training camp.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 12 of 49ers Camp: The Purdy-Evans Connection Needs Work “Give Samuel credit — he’s in the best shape possible and he shows every day, as opposed to lots of other veterans on the team. He’s one of the iron mans of camp so far, which is incredible….[Jack Jones] injured his hand early on Thursday night against the Titans, but practiced today and recovered a fumble. He takes the ball away from the offense seemingly every other practice, but his coverage isn’t exactly sticky. He’s an enigma. Mike Evans returns to 49ers practice as left guard competition heats up “Wide receiver Jacob Cowing, out since Aug. 5 with a hip flexor injury, returned to practice. He took a handoff on a running play, then dropped a pass from Jones. Later, he made a very nice grab of a Jones pass along the right sideline.” 49ers DC Raheem Morris evaluates young players after preseason opener “San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris spoke with reporters after Saturday’s training camp practice. Here’s everything he had to say.” 49ers’ Gracen Halton making an impression with both burst and outburst at camp (paywall) “ After Halton’s first win in one-on-one drills earlier this month, 49ers tackle Trent Williams strolled over to the defensive line’s section to offer a handshake and encouragement. Both are Oklahoma products who met three years ago when Williams was on the sideline for a Sooners game, though Halton doubts the veteran tackle remembers the encounter. “I was one of the guys that said what’s up to him,” Halton said. “I was dang starstruck.” …Halton feels he’s making up for lost time. He hyperextended his knee on the first day of training camp and missed the initial week of practice. He didn’t exactly ease his way back into the mix when he returned, making plays in both one-on-one and 11-on-11 situations and letting everyone know about it. “That’s what I like to do,” he said. “I imagine myself as a lion going out to get the gazelle. So when I do those one-on-ones, my mindset is, I’m going off to hunt.” 49ers change up their left guard rotation; Mike Evans and Jacob Cowing return “After Thursday’s game, Kyle Shanahan said this about Jones: “We felt he fit into our scheme and was a guy that we were able to get that we think can compete for that starting job, and if not, he can have some good depth for us.” That almost sounds like they want Willis or Colby to be the guy for the job. In the same breath, this shouldn’t be viewed as a demotion for Jones, who played in his first live game since 2024 fewer than 48 hours ago. The team has to manage Jones’ inevitable soreness. After practice, Trent Williams said it’s a three-man race and “may the best man win.” He believes Willis has a “high ceiling and a lot of potential.”

title: 49ers change up their left guard rotation; Mike Evans and Jacob Cowing return
summary: The San Francisco 49ers brought in tight end Khalil Dinkins for a tryout, per the transaction wire. This comes 48 hours after three tight ends, Brayden Willis, Josiah Deguara, and Hayden Rucci, played 33 to 37 snaps in the preseason opener. George Kittle remains on the active/PUP, while the team still has Luke Farrell and […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Carver Willis #74 of the San Francisco 49ers holds a pad during a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers brought in tight end Khalil Dinkins for a tryout, per the transaction wire. This comes 48 hours after three tight ends, Brayden Willis, Josiah Deguara, and Hayden Rucci, played 33 to 37 snaps in the preseason opener. George Kittle remains on the active/PUP, while the team still has Luke Farrell and Jake Tonges. Dinkins, an undrafted free agent from this past draft, was released by the 49ers after dealing with injuries. The team might want to see if he’s healthier now and if he can bring more to the table than the trio that played on Thursday A couple of wide receivers return to practice Wide receivers Mike Evans (quad) and Jacob Cowing (hip flexor) returned to practice and participated in 11-on-11s. I wonder if we’ll see Evans participate in joint practices this upcoming week, or if the plan is to keep him on ice until the games mean something. It’s a big couple of weeks for Cowing. His return is a good sign, but he needs to prove he can stay healthy for the rest of the preseason. The team waiving Junior Bergen should have hinted that Cowing was close to returning, given that he’s a returner. A changing of the guard? There was a change of the guard with the starters, according to the reporters on hand. Connor Colby and Carver Willis rotated at left guard with the starters. Robert Jones was at right guard with the second team, while Austen Pleasants remained at left guard with the third team. Apparently, Willis took the most reps with the starters at left guard during the move-the-ball drills. That should read like Willis is higher on the depth chart than Colby. This was likely the plan all along — or at least based on the past week and a half of practice. Jones gets the first crack at it with the starters in the first preseason game, while Willis and Colby are up next. After Thursday’s game, Kyle Shanahan said this about Jones: “We felt he fit into our scheme and was a guy that we were able to get that we think can compete for that starting job, and if not, he can have some good depth for us.” That almost sounds like they want Willis or Colby to be the guy for the job. In the same breath, this shouldn’t be viewed as a demotion for Jones, who played in his first live game since 2024 fewer than 48 hours ago. The team has to manage Jones’ inevitable soreness. After practice, Trent Williams said it’s a three-man race and “may the best man win.” He believes Willis has a “high ceiling and a lot of potential.” One rookie who impressed Trent Williams Williams was asked who impressed him on Thursday night, and he mentioned the 49ers rookie, with obvious bias involved: “Boomer sooner. You know it. G-baby, man. Obviously, Oklahoma guy. I’m always gonna be a little biased. I think the world is going to see what he has to offer. Very explosive. Short-area quickness. Really powerful. Put you in the mind of D.J. Jones a little bit, what he had when he was here. He definitely impressed.” Williams highlighted how Halton loves football, saying he appreciates Halton’s enthusiasm in the locker room or whenever he wins a rep in practice. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said he was pleased with how Halton executed, specifically on the sack that was negated.

title: De’Zhaun Stribling is in rare company with his preseason debut against the Titans
summary: Well, the 49ers’ first pick of the 2026 draft, wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, just keeps looking better and better. On Thursday, against the Tennessee Titans, Stribling hauled in seven catches for 63 yards. In the first half. Sure, we can make all the jokes we want about it being preseason, but that doesn’t happen very […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: De'zhaun Stribling #15 of the San Francisco 49ers catches a deep pass over Cor'dale Flott #18 of the Tennessee Titans in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the 49ers’ first pick of the 2026 draft, wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, just keeps looking better and better. On Thursday, against the Tennessee Titans, Stribling hauled in seven catches for 63 yards. In the first half. Sure, we can make all the jokes we want about it being preseason, but that doesn’t happen very often. In fact, it’s only happened once in the last decade. Stribling is the second receiver in the past decade to catch seven passes in the first 20 minutes. Look, I know useless stats can be exhausting sometimes. Especially when, during a game, it seems like new stats are invented every five seconds—but I will gladly take this one. Now that’s not to say Stribling wasn’t perfect. He missed a block early and dropped a pass (his one target that didn’t turn into a reception). He also has some work to do on his route-running. All three of these things can be coached up. “Thought he struggled a little bit on the first drive,” Kyle Shanahan said following the game. “But I think he got three drives after that. It seemed as if he executed on all the stuff that went to him.” The 49ers’ other pass catcher, Mike Evans, was on the sideline for the first preseason game of the season. Maybe you forgot about him. That’s ok, Stribling looked that good. Now toss him in with Deebo Samuel and Evans and that seems like a decent trio. One that lost Jauan Jennings to free agency. While Stribling missed a block, it doesn’t seem like he’ll lack the physicality or shy away from it. “I liked how his hands looked out there and played physical,” Shanahan said. Shanahan said that they are switching things up for Stribling and he won’t be primarily in the slot. If he has that versatility, he’ll be even more of a steal than the second round where the 49ers got him. And maybe polarizing reaction will be negated . Now Stribling just needs to stay on the field. He was kept out of practice for a few days and has been back for about a week. The 49ers haven’t had much luck lately with their early-pick rookies getting a full season of reps. Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall (selected in 2024) was in and out of the lineup in 2024, and defensive lineman Mykel Williams (selected in 2025) suffered a torn ACL in Week 9 last year. If he can stay on the field, Shanahan is optimistic: “Hopefully he can string together two more of these weeks, because he’s going about it the right way and as long as he gets those reps and continues to do what he’s been doing, he should be ready for the season.”

title: 49ers News: We’re on to the Los Angeles Chargers
summary: After broken neck, 49ers’ Robert Jones ready to fight for a job: ‘I do have to hit again’ (paywall)“Jones used a bone-stimulation machine to promote healing for four months, took regular hospital trips for two-hour stints in a hyperbaric chamber and wasn’t permitted to run until he was medically cleared in March….“When we got to […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 23: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers and head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers shake hands after the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Los Angeles Chargers and San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on August 23, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images After broken neck, 49ers’ Robert Jones ready to fight for a job: ‘I do have to hit again’ (paywall) “Jones used a bone-stimulation machine to promote healing for four months, took regular hospital trips for two-hour stints in a hyperbaric chamber and wasn’t permitted to run until he was medically cleared in March….“When we got to training camp and it was the first padded practice, it was in my head: ‘I do have to hit again,’” Jones said. “I was a little cautious, but once I got going, I felt good. After I got that first hit in, it helped my confidence. I knew I was good, I was healthy and I was able to do this.” The fact that Jones is doing this in the NFL is wildly unlikely given his background. Jones didn’t play organized football until his junior year at Rockford (Ill.) East High School, didn’t play offensive line until his freshman year at Highland (Kan.) Community College, and wasn’t drafted after his two seasons at Middle Tennessee State. “The NFL was never really on my radar,” Jones said. “I was really using football as a vehicle to get my degree. I tried to lock in on that while I was still learning the sport.” Jones grew up in Chicago dreaming of becoming a basketball star. But that ended when he didn’t make his high school team. The message: He was too big. But the 280-pounder was soon approached by a football assistant coach, David Hampton, a former NFL running back. “He told me, ‘Man, you’ve got to play football. You’re a walking meal ticket,’ Jones said. That wasn’t immediately obvious. As a junior, Jones was a backup defensive lineman who quit the team after about five games because, he said, his mom was “terrified” about her only son playing such a violent sport. After Jones returned to earn a starting role as a senior, he was moved to the offensive line when he arrived at Highland. It didn’t click overnight: He didn’t start until his sophomore year. “After that,” Jones said, “the rest is history.” That history includes last year’s painful chapter. Jones suffered his broken neck early in practice, but he was able to finish: He thought he’d suffered a shoulder stinger. Jones even did some post-practice work with a teammate before he finally went to the trainers, who sent him for a CT scan. “That’s when they told me: ‘You broke your C5,’” Jones said.” 6 Winners and 4 losers from the 49ers’ preseason opener “Eason had a play where he sniffed out a screen and forced an incompletion. Kris Kocurek will appreciate that, as defensive line coaches are always saying something along the lines of, “If you’re getting after the quarterback for the first time all game, it’s probably because they want you to.” Eason stood his ground against double teams, pushed the pocket against rookie Jackson Slater, and looked like he belonged in his debut.” 49ers receiver Jordan Watkins produces in another promising NFL preseason opener “I think my diet has been a big part of me being able to stay healthy, especially getting through this camp,” he said. “I’m a really big sweet tea drinker, and I’m trying to stay away from sweet tea and sweet coffee.” Watkins, a fourth-round pick from Ole Miss in the 2025 NFL Draft, spent last season around 195 pounds. This year, he said his weight fluctuates from 202 to 205, and he has dropped body fat, too. He said he eats a lot of protein and has cut out carbohydrates — except for breakfast — from his diet. Watkins’s diet consists of primarily steak, chicken and vegetables, he said. This summer has signified a new start for Watkins, who is competing to become the team’s primary punt returner, too. He handled two punts on Thursday night with a fair catch and a 4-yard return. “It’s been a fun journey, and I feel like I’m getting better,” said Watkins, who ran a time of 4.37 seconds in the 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. “Knowing that everybody in the stadium is looking at you, and everyone on the sideline is expecting you to catch the ball. It’s just you and the ball.” 49ers vs. Titans PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Defensive tackle Gracen Halton was the 49ers’ highest-graded run defender (75.0), recording a game-high four stops. Cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. came in second with a 74.1 run-defense grade.” 49ers QB Kurtis Rourke released from hospital after rib injury in preseason opener “The San Francisco 49ers announced that quarterback Kurtis Rourke was released from the hospital on Thursday night.”

title: Three Takeaways: Buccaneers vs Jets Preseason Week 1
summary: The Buccaneers first preseason game is in the books, defeating the New York Jets 24-16. There were certainly highs and lows in this one as we got our first look at preseason action from Tampa Bay. Lets take a look at some of the main takeaways from this first contest. Jalon Daniels is the front […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 14: Elijah Roberts #95 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts with DeMonte Capehart #90 after a sack in the second quarter against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on August 14, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buccaneers first preseason game is in the books, defeating the New York Jets 24-16. There were certainly highs and lows in this one as we got our first look at preseason action from Tampa Bay. Lets take a look at some of the main takeaways from this first contest. Jalon Daniels is the front runner for QB3 Undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels made the most of his opportunity Friday night. He went 10/15 with 111 passing yards as well as three carries for nine yards and a rushing touchdown. Daniels displayed his athleticism countless times throughout the game and also showcased a little bit of his pinpoint accuracy. On the other hand, Connor Bazelak and the offense struggled in the first half. Bazelak went 12/20 for 72 passing yards and the offense had a tough time consistently moving the football in that first half. Bazelak has the experience edge and Jake Browning is still going to be this team’s QB2 but for the question of who that third signal caller will be, it might be Daniels’ job to lose after a strong performance on Friday. Bucs may have some serious pass rush depth For years Tampa Bay’s defense has struggled to consistently rush the passer, and they tried to address that this offseason, but they may have found some depth in unexpected places. Of the Bucs four sacks against the Jets, three of them were by pass rushers in Elijiah Roberts and undrafted free agent rookie Jack Pyburn, who had two. Pyburn specifically flashed and you wonder if he keeps this up the tough decisions the Bucs may be faced with. Having too many productive players who can get the quarterback is a good problem to have and one the team hasn’t had in a few years. Roberts’ ability to rush from the interior will be very valuable and Pyburn along with second year player David Walker, could end being very productive depth for a defense that could certainly use it. Good chance Ayden Garnes has already made the roster Speaking of depth, cornerback may be the one position on the team that on the surface does not appear to have a lot of depth, but an unlikely source could change that. Undrafted free agent rookie out of Arizona Ayden Garnes has impressed in training camp and there has been a lot of buzz already about Garnes before the game even started. Well, he certainly helped his case in this one as he had a big tackle for loss, but the big moment was when he picked off Bailey Zappe and took it to the house for a pick six. Those types of splash plays are exactly the things that can help keep a player like Garnes around. With Benjamin Morrison just returning from injury and having some injury troubles last year, plus Zyon McCollum being banged up at times last year depth at corner in this league is a must and Garnes can provide a role on this team if he continues to impress. At this point barring injury, I’d expect Garnes to make the final roster as one of the final corners. It will be well earned. The theme? All of these takeaways involved undrafted free agents and late round picks in some capacity. It just goes to show the job Jason Licht and his team have done in finding these players and the coaching staff continuing to develop them. There are still two preseason games left, but this was a good start by a lot of guys trying to make the roster.
author: Evan Wanish

title: Titans roster 2026: Tony Pollard, John Franklin-Myers and Fernando Carmona Jr. are underrated
summary: Nobody reading this site on a regular basis needs to be told that the Tennessee Titans’ two straight 3-14 seasons are not good enough. That falls into the “Well, DUH” category for any NFL team. So, instead of reliving the mistakes of years past, let’s focus on how the Titans can rise out of the […]
full_text: Nobody reading this site on a regular basis needs to be told that the Tennessee Titans’ two straight 3-14 seasons are not good enough. That falls into the “Well, DUH” category for any NFL team. So, instead of reliving the mistakes of years past, let’s focus on how the Titans can rise out of the muck and become competitive again. One reason for optimism is the development that rookie quarterback Cam Ward showed as the 2025 season went along. From Weeks 1-9, Ward completed 170 of 295 passes for 1,760 yards, five touchdowns, six interceptions, and a passer rating of 72.1. But starting in Week 10 through Week 18, Ward turned it around, completing 153 of 245 passes for 1,409 yards, 10 touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 90.0. That was entirely legit. And new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll is excited about helping Ward take the next steps. “He is a young professional,” Daboll said of Ward in early May. “He wants to be great. He is instinctive. When we are just watching the tape, he is able to communicate the things that he sees, and why he did certain things, when we watch the tape from last year. When we are installing the new system to him, concepts and things like that, he is able to pick things up very quickly. It has been awesome to work with him.” New head coach Robert Saleh, one of the NFL’s best defensive minds, does carry a 20-36 record as a head coach as baggage. But as that happened over four seasons with the New York Jets from 2021-2024, we’ll give him a pass. We are not sure who could succeed with the Jets at this point. And this Titans team is loaded with talent. Ward is ascending. First-round receiver Carnell Tate has the skills to be an alpha X-iso receiver, no matter what some may say. Carnell Tate as your new alpha iso receiver. No need to overthink it. pic.twitter.com/mBnvr9ul2L — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) March 19, 2026 There could be at least five new starters on defense, if not more, and Saleh has to be excited about that — as we will detail, Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi have done a nice job of acquiring players who fit the new head coach’s schematic preferences. Can the 2026 Titans be like the 2025 New England Patriots, and jump from obscurity to the Super Bowl? That’s a tall order, but stranger things have happened in the National Football League. For that to happen, of course, everybody on the roster will have to step up to unimaginable heights. The stars, yes, but also the guys whose names don’t make a dent in a national sense. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Titans — one underrated veteran, one underrated free-agent signing, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: RB Tony Pollard When it comes to running backs, explosive plays are great, but consistency is just as crucial to ultimate success. The back who can upend defenses year after year without blips in performance will find himself respected as a franchise pillar. So, let’s note here that two NFL running backs have at least 1,000 rushing yards in each of the last four seasons: Derrick Henry and Tony Pollard. Henry won’t surprise you; El Tractorcito is on his way to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. But Pollard? The 2019 fourth-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys who signed a three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Titans in 2024, and doesn’t make much noise on the national radar? Well, yes. Consistency may be important, but it often avoids headlines. Especially on teams with stacked 3-14 records. Regardless of how the nation views him (or doesn’t), everybody in Tennessee should be pretty happy about Pollard. Last season, he ran the ball 242 times for 1,082 yards, five touchdowns, 39 forced missed tackles, and 10 runs of 15 or more yards. The Titans’ new head coach didn’t take long to realize the value there. “He’s an unbelievable pro,” Saleh said of Pollard over the summer. “Does everything the right way, brings a lot of juice and energy, he’s a positive individual. I feel like he’s in here all the time, working on his body, doing the things he needs to do to get himself ready, and then his practice habits are second to none and how deliberate he is. And I’m not just talking about live reps, but if you guys get a chance to watch a walkthrough today, I mean every single step he takes is deliberate in terms of the pad level, the hand placement, the eyes to make sure that he’s executing at a high level and those are the reasons why he’s so successful.” Tony Pollard of the @Titans is one of two NFL backs with at least 1,000 rushing yards in each of the last four seasons. Derrick Henry is the other. We all know how Henry does it. Here's how Pollard does it. pic.twitter.com/Om1p8hmx2D — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 11, 2026 The Titans also have veteran Tyjae Spears and rookie Nicholas Singleton on the depth chart, but there should be no doubt as to who’s the leader in Brian Daboll’s backfield. Underrated free agent: DL John Franklin-Myers One reason the Titans traded DI T’Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for edge-rusher Jermaine Johnson II was Saleh’s particular requirements for defensive linemen. Generally speaking, Saleh runs four-on-the-floor fronts without too much blitzing or stunting; it’s on the guys on the line to get home. And it helps when Saleh has familiarity with the guys he’s coaching as he does with Johnson, who was drafted by the Jets in 2022 when Saleh was head coach. This is also why the Titans also signed defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers to a three-year, $63 million contract with $42 million guaranteed this offseason. Franklin-Myers also overlapped with Saleh, as he was part of the Jets’ defense from 2020-2023, so Saleh knew exactly how good this particular Hidden Gem can be. Last season with the Denver Broncos, Franklin-Myers collected eight sacks, 43 pressures, 11 solo tackles, 18 stops, and six tackles for loss. He was a stalwart presence on one of the NFL’s best defensive lines, and he contributed as much as he benefited. Which is why I tagged him as one of the NFL’s Secret Superstars of free agency . “Our relationship, we have one of the best relationships in football, I would say,” Franklin-Myers said of Saleh after the contract was official. “We kept in contact. When I’m down, he is going to shoot me a text, and he is going to pick me up. Relationships in football, they’re so important. And I appreciate coach Saleh because I can always count on him. Whenever free agency started, it was like: ‘If the opportunity ever came about and he was willing, and we set the financials straight, I would be more than willing.’ “And I am so happy to be back in this defense with him, for real.” Every great defensive line has at least one "glue guy" who holds it together under the radar. The @Broncos have John Franklin-Myers. pic.twitter.com/2oTBK7XwXK — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) October 28, 2025 Given Franklin-Myers’ ability to disrupt anywhere on the line, and what that can do for those around him (including Jeffery “ Hi, I’m the best defensive tackle in football ” Simmons), the Titans should be just as happy. Underrated draft pick: OL Fernando Carmona Jr. So, the defensive line is pretty set. The offensive line, however… The Titans raised a lot of eyebrows when they signed former Pittsburgh Steelers tackle Dan Moore Jr. to a four-year, $82 million contract with $50 million guaranteed after Moore allowed 12 sacks in 2024. I guess you could say that the eight sacks Moore allowed in 2025 technically constitutes “improvement,” but still. Right tackle JC Latham, who also allowed eight sacks last season, is still figuring things out as he comes into his third NFL season. Outside of left guard Peter Skoronski, there are no sure things on this line, and that includes center Austin Schlottmann and right guard Cordell Volson. Based on 2025 performance, one guy who could provide clarity is Arkansas guard Fernando Carmona Jr, selected with the 142nd overall pick in the fifth round.…
author: Doug Farrar

title: Commanders vs. Dolphins preseason: Mark Tyler’s Studs and Duds
summary: The Commanders 2026 preseason opener against the Dolphins went pretty much as planned. Washington gave up an opening drive score, mainly with the second-team defense against Miami’s starters. They locked in after that and didn’t allow any more points for the rest of the game in a 20-7 victory at Northwest Stadium. What really caught […]
full_text: The Commanders 2026 preseason opener against the Dolphins went pretty much as planned. Washington gave up an opening drive score, mainly with the second-team defense against Miami’s starters. They locked in after that and didn’t allow any more points for the rest of the game in a 20-7 victory at Northwest Stadium . What really caught my attention was the lack of sloppy play — which is usually prevalent in the preseason opener. Although new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones kept things pretty vanilla, the execution was good and I didn’t see a lot of bad mistakes. To me, this was the biggest win of the evening. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs Fatman Allen/Robert Henry Jr. The rookie running back duo turned out to be the highlight of the evening for Washington. Robert Henry Jr. showed vision and burst while Fatman Allen showed patience and wiggle. Both men found the end zone in the opener. FatMan has some WIGGLE! pic.twitter.com/EzlOyTsKGO — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Fat-Man with the burst. GREAT block by Yankoff!!! pic.twitter.com/PC6Mgdwovw — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Henry with a BEAUTIFUL 22yd TD run around right edge. pic.twitter.com/8MOC9cOKfH — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Quan Martin Martin, playing safety with the second-team defense, and looked the part of a starter against Miami. He had a beautiful tackle on Dolphins running back De’Von Achane on the first drive and got an interception on the sideline early in the second quarter. He was around the football quite a bit early in the game. Quan coming downhill like a 🦇 out of HELL to make the big hit!!! pic.twitter.com/OKEHRODgA0 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Shy Tuttle/Rickey Barber Shy Tuttle and Rickey Barber showed well throughout the evening. The duo combined for eight total tackles, a sack and a tackle for a loss to go along with multiple pressures. 3rd and 9 – Barber and Jean-Baptiste great pressure. pic.twitter.com/9ORCC2zTGH — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Ricky Barber (who is playing some ZERO tech here) plays this run very well! pic.twitter.com/cGemTMjP1M — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Great stack, shed and tackle here by Tuttle pic.twitter.com/hfrjefF5No — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Matt Gulbin Rookie sixth-r0under Matt Gulbin played a really nice game at center, albeit against the Dolphins second- and third-string defensive line. He did a nice job working to the second level to pick off Miami defenders and his anchor in pass protection looked really good. Watch rookie Matt Gulbin work to the second level and get the block on the LB that helps Henry rip off this chunk play 💪🏻💥 pic.twitter.com/bbtSIQohrn — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Nice block by Gulbin here at center and Henry creases the defense 💪🏻 pic.twitter.com/j8yr5OSxsY — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Duds Sam Hartman Quarterback Sam Hartman doesn’t look like he belongs on an NFL field. He lacks accuracy and zip on his passes, and his pocket-presence is below-average. However, he does have a potential career as a hair model. This sack is on Hartman. Need to get rid of the ball here. pic.twitter.com/QhGcPuuP3D — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 14, 2026 Great protection here. Dyami is open on the DIG. Hartman sails the pass and it’s intercepted pic.twitter.com/toPGbGlgOT — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Johnny Newton Playing with the starters, Newton looked anything but one! He was blown off the ball by Miami’s starting offensive line and looked slow and out of place. Julian (Not-so-)Good Jones Washington’s starting center (by default), looked overwhelmed against the Dolphins defense. He showed a poor anchor in pass-pro and didn’t do a good job moving bodies or getting to the second level. Good-Jones gets completely BLOWN UP by a Dolphins LB on a blitz pic.twitter.com/nMh3sQWrbO — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Yankoff with a poor block on the edge and Good-Jones whiffs at his target at the second level. pic.twitter.com/kp4ciwoT6s — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Commanders Notes Athan Kaliakmanis easily outplayed Hartman in this first preseason contest. He looked more in control of the offense, had better pocket presence and threw the ball with better accuracy and a LOT more zip. He did get sacked twice, but he’ll clean that up and get rid of the ball quicker as he matures. Damn 🎯 by AK to Jones who can’t hang on pic.twitter.com/M7aPX6ANWn — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Sonny Syles had a lackluster debut. The first-round pick had a couple tackles he got in on, but there were also some times where he looked like he was jogging out there. I can’t wait to see how he looks with the entire first-team defense. You can call this nitpicking a bit, but to me, it looks like Styles (lined up on-the-ball at right EDGE) is just kinda jogging here instead of hauling ass down the line. pic.twitter.com/8SpQjNgfHV — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Receiver Jaylin Lane made three catches (which led the team) for 31 yards. A good game for a young wide receiver who needs to show his hands are not an issue. Linebacker Leo Chenal had a quiet evening in limited playing time. He recorded one stop and whiffed on another. Chenal should have had this run stopped for a short gain. Instead, he slightly over-runs it and whiffs pic.twitter.com/SDNgsZ7iIg — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Defensive tackle Byron Cowart had a few nice splash plays during the game working with the backups. Cowart get the pressure and Malik Spencer gets the INT pic.twitter.com/yAUU5hrW2C — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Rookie receiver Antonio Williams had a nice catch on the sidelines and made some good blocks in the run game. Antonio Williams in the left HIP with the nice block! pic.twitter.com/vRbSROjY4L — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Defensive back Antonio Hamilton Sr. was a special-teams demon and was flying all over the field in coverage. Kicker Jake Moody is going to DOINK his way out of the league. Jake Moody’s DOINK that somehow slipped through pic.twitter.com/Ru3216VQzY — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Linebacker Ale Kaho played a good game. He had a nice interception and played well against the run. Ale Kaho with the INT! Nice drop by Ale, but the pressure up front caused this. pic.twitter.com/hEeikyD29A — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Linebacker Jordan Magee flashed some of his speed and had a really nice play where he slipped under a block and got in on the tackle. LOVE this play by Jordan Magee at right ILB!!!!! Slips UNDER the block, re-directs his momentum, and gets in on the tackle!!! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WxNS25kmP6 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Tanoa Togiai , playing right guard, showed nicely in his Commanders debut. I saw No. 62 on a few occasions opening up holes and sealing off defenders. Defensive back Tyler Owens was lined up all over the field. He was part of a two-deep look, was in the box as a money-backer and even came off the edge on a blitz. Tight end Colson Yankoff had a few nice blocks (also whiffed badly on one) and snagged two receptions for 24 yards. Defensive back Malik Spencer had his first NFL interception. I’d like to see him get some more time with the second-team defense. The potential is there.
author: Mark Tyler

title: Kaytron Allen, Robert Henry Jr. ramp up competition among Commanders RBs
summary: The Commanders didn’t have many running backs available during Friday night’s preseason game against Miami.   Bill Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White weren’t active, along with 24 others, to avoid unnecessary injury risk. Jeremy McNichols is dealing with a reported quadriceps issue.   Jerome Ford was up but the Commanders chose to limit his exposure during […]
full_text: The Commanders didn’t have many running backs available during Friday night’s preseason game against Miami. Bill Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White weren’t active, along with 24 others , to avoid unnecessary injury risk. Jeremy McNichols is dealing with a reported quadriceps issue . Jerome Ford was up but the Commanders chose to limit his exposure during the game. That left rookies Robert Henry Jr. and Kaytron Allen to do some dirty work. They seemed to enjoy it, rushing for a combined 160 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 35 carries in the 20-7 win . Most production came against Miami’s lower defensive tiers, but that shouldn’t discount what was done in the run game by two relatively unheralded prospects. Allen’s a sixth-round pick. Henry’s an undrafted free agent. Both guys shined using different styles. Henry’s a patient runner who will slash through space. Allen’s plan is to run at you and then through you, with some elusiveness when required. Both guys looked worthy of the carries they got, and impressed head coach Dan Quinn with the quality work done over the course of the game. “He and Kaytron had a nice night,” head coach Dan Quinn said in his postgame press conference . “Also Jerome Ford went out. We had three backs for the game, and when Jerome was out there was no flinch with these guys, playing on (special teams) and returning. I felt the outside stuff with Rob.” “It was great to see both of these guys go. Kaytron finished the game with a first down and had the touchdown towards the end. Those are the physical-style runs we expect from him.” Henry jump started the offense with an 11-yard run to start Washington’s second series, which ended in a field goal He kept that good vibe going on the next Commanders draft, with a 15-yard gain around the right end. That set up this beauty, a 22-yard touchdown run that put Washington ahead for good. Robert Henry Jr. takes it 22 yards for his first NFL TD! pic.twitter.com/xbeWJqwLgR — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 15, 2026 Henry was super efficient, averaging 6.3 yards per carry in this one. He was also inspirational to Allen. Kaytron Allen said when he saw Robert Henry having success it “got me going.” Said after Henry scored he knew he had to as well. Said Henry is his “dog.” — John Keim (@john_keim) August 15, 2026 Allen had more carries and less efficiency, but made his mark with violence. That was clear on his touchdown run eight seconds from halftime, when he crossed the goal line and then kicked the door down. Kaytron "Fatman" Allen TD! (approved nickname) Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Qr6XNV28yk — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Per Sharp Football Analysis , Allen’s the only running back in the last decade to have 20-plus carries in the preseason without a run for negative yards. It was good to see Allen in a live tackling situation, too, so Washington could get a better grasp of how he can break or elude tackles. “He’s a bigger back so, in practice you wonder, ‘Would he have gotten stopped there? Could it have been more?’” Quinn said. “There was a similar situation with (quarterback Jayden Daniels), where you wonder if he would’ve been sacked or not, and he would not have been. There’s a little bit of that with Kaytron. Would he be able to get yards after the hit? We were anxious to see what that looked like after the contact.” The Commanders have a competitive running back room, with Croskey-Merritt and White earmarked for a high carry count. More games like this from Allen and Henry could make for a deep room and tough roster choices, especially with McNichols and Ford also in the mix. There’s plenty of work remaining over the course of this preseason, but Allen and Henry have given Commanders coaches plenty to think about as they decide how to work out the running back room. “I like the backs,” Quinn said. “They’re in shape. They’re focused. They’re ready. When they came out and were a little short-handed, there was no flinch. That was a good sign to me.”
author: Scott Bair

title: Commanders News: Stock up for RB Robert Henry; sudden question at QB
summary: The Daily Slop – 15 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Washington […]
full_text: The Daily Slop – 15 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Washington Awaits Marcus Mariota Update After Preseason Win With 26 players held out of the game, including starting QB Jayden Daniels , Mariota got the start but only lasted four plays before going down with an apparent leg injury. Mariota had just completed a 22-yard pass to Dyami Brown before going down on the following handoff to Kaytron Allen and eventually leaving for further evaluation. Mariota got hit pretty hard on the play to Brown, but stayed in the game until the handoff on the next play, when he appeared to grab at his knee. He was able to walk off the field on his own. Mariota enters the season as Washington’s established No. 2 quarterback behind Daniels, with two developmental prospects behind him who are far from NFL-ready; he is the last line of defense if something happens to Daniels. His health matters far more than the outcome of an August game. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn had no update on Mariota when asked after the game: “I don’t. I know we’re connecting on Sunday, so I’ll give an update on Marcus and some of the other guys that we’ve talked about who couldn’t be back.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Standouts from Washington’s preseason opener against Miami QB Athan Kaliakmanis Rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis also made his case for the Commanders’ QB3 job. The 2026 seventh-round pick started fast, connecting with rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams for 16 yards before finding tight end Colson Yankoff for 17 yards. He finished the night with 87 passing yards and no touchdowns. Sam Hartman had a disappointing preseason debut, throwing for just 80 passing yards and one interception. Kaliakmanis’ performance could give him the edge in the QB3 competition. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable The backup QB competition on display against Miami The first half was for Hartman to impress, which was met with more lows than highs. The first drive replacing Mariota ended in a punt by Matt Haack, then his next drive ended after just six plays after a potential scoring drive ended into an easy Dolphins interception following a clear-cut overthrow by Hartman. Full drive number two was highlighted by the run game and a 14 yard catch by Van Jefferson as the offense drew a fresh set of downs at the six yard line. But an incompletion on second down followed by a sack on third down squandered the chance to tie the game, instead forcing Jake Moody to rattle in a 29-yard field goal to cut into the deficit. Hartman was more efficient over his last two drives, finding Jaylin Lane on a pair of throws along with Ben Sinnott for an 11 yard pickup before Robert Henry Jr. punched in his first NFL touchdown on a 22 yard run. The final drive of the half was highlighted by Hartman’s 17 yard completion to Jaylin Lane before Kaytron Allen’s first NFL touchdown gave Washington a ten point halftime lead. Hartman took the field for one final drive in the second half, ending his day 8-of-15 with 80 yards and an interception, before seventh-round pick Athan Kaliakmanis took the field for the rest of the game. The rookie finished 6-of-10 with 87 yards, including 33 yards on his first two throws to rookie Antonio Williams then Colson Yankoff, followed by a completion over 20 yards to Jacoby Jones then short gain to Jaden Bradley. While the big plays may not have always been there, the rookie’s arm strength was evident in his unofficial debut. The question now is, with Mariota exiting the game with a possible non-contact leg injury, can Kaliakmanis potentially stabilize the backup quarterback spot? To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) Robert Henry Jr. bursts onto the scene The slithery runner from UTSA [Robert Henry] turned into a video game back in the first half. The UDFA’s first carry went for 11 yards inside. After modest gains on the next three carries, Henry gave the home crowd a reason to get out of their seats besides making a nacho run. The 5-foot-9, 196-pound rookie zoomed around the right end for a 15-yard gain. Following a Ben Sinnott 11-yard catch, Henry took the handoff with the apparent intention of cutting upfield between the tackles. Instead, he quickly moved to his right as if he had entered the Matrix, and then zoomed down the right side for a 22-yard touchdown. We see electric runners and receivers each preseason who look like Week 1 starters only to fade quietly out of the league. Henry, who had 75 yards on 12 attempts (6.3 ypc), should get a chance to hang around on Washington’s practice squad, allowing everyone involved to see if this RB has staying power. There’s unlikely to be a true competition between the first-year players. Allen’s draft status gives him a head start that Henry likely cannot close. Regardless, the fun UDFA will make his run at it. For more from Ben Standig, click here From Commanders Wire: Henry showed excellent vision, cut-back ability and the potential to break off a long run. Allen banged in between the tackles, didn’t lose yardage and kept the chains moving. The Commanders will likely keep four backs, with many assuming Croskey-Merritt, White, McNichols, and Allen will win those four spots. Henry is now firmly in the mix. Each of these running backs offers a different skill set. There is excellent depth. This spot became more intriguing over the final two preseason games and one joint practice. To read more of this Commanders Wire article, CLICK HERE From ESPN: A few rookies had strong games. Undrafted free agent running back Robert Henry Jr. showed juice on his runs and scored from 22 yards out. He finished with 75 yards on 12 runs. Henry hit the holes fast and used good vision to knife through narrow openings. Center Matt Gulbin showed some power inside in the second quarter. Third-round receiver Antonio Williams caught one pass for 16 yards and didn’t play until the third quarter. Running back Kaytron Allen doesn’t have Henry’s burst but managed 85 yards on 23 carries and a 1-yard touchdown. — John Keim Next game: at Detroit Lions (Aug. 22, noon ET) Commanders.com 5 takeaways from Washington’s 20-7 win over the Dolphins Quan Martin and Ale Kaho helped flip the field. The Commanders have stressed the importance of creating more turnovers in practice, and while no one will likely remember an interception in the preseason, it is hopefully a sign of things to come. Quan Martin, who is in a battle with the rest of the safeties, was the player who secured the ball from Ewers, who either expected his receiver to be in a different spot or simply misfired his pass. Either way, Martin was there to make the play, giving the Commanders the ball at the Dolphins’ 35-yard line. It led to the Commanders getting a 29-yard field goal from Jake Moody, who doinked the kick off the right upright to make the score 7-3. The next came from 2024 undrafted free agent Ale Kaho, who read Miller’s eyes on the play and made the easy grab that set the offense up at the Dolphins’ 33-yard line. That also led to a field goal — a 44-yarder by Drew Stevens. And then there was a third. Malik Spencer intercepted a pass from Miller with less than six minutes in the fourth quarter, essentially ending the Dolphins’ chances at a comeback. It was the kind of complimentary football that was missing from the Commanders’ roster in 2025. Hopefully, the current roster can keep that up and create shorter fields for the offense going forward. title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 1: Game takeaways, analysis
summary: The NFL preseason is underway! How did rookies and players in new places perform in their debuts?
full_text:
The first week of the  2026 NFL preseason kicked off Thursday, giving us our first look at rookies and players making debuts with new teams. It continued with three games Friday, with seven games being played Saturday.

 How did players in new uniforms perform? Who stood out? Which first-year players showed promise?

 Our NFL Nation reporters picked out what you need to know about top debuts and more as the NFL returns.

 
 Quick links: 
 Full schedule | Where to watch 
 Depth charts  | Sign up to play fantasy 

 
 

 Saturday's games 

 Cowboys 17, Seahawks 7 
 

 Cowboys:  The Cowboys will likely give both of Dak Prescott 's backups, Sam Howell and Joe Milton III , at least one start this preseason, but Howell, who signed a one-year deal worth $2.5 million as a free agent, got the call vs. Seattle and put together a solid first half. He completed 8 of 12 passes for 94 yards, including a 39-yard touchdown to undrafted rookie Camden Brown . Howell also ran twice for 15 yards, and he managed the game and kept the offense out of trouble, despite some inexperience around him.

 First-rounders Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence saw spot duty, although Downs' first appearance didn't even last through the opening drive of the game. Lawrence saw action at both edge positions and got caught inside on one pass rush, giving Jalen Milroe the chance to scramble for a decent gain.

 There are always some undrafted receivers who shine in camp practices but don't do the same in preseason games. Brown, from Georgia Southern, carried over his practice performance to Saturday's game. On his first touchdown, he pulled the ball away from Seahawks corner Shemar Jean-Charles . Brown's second touchdown was even prettier, a left-handed snare of a Milton pass on the opening drive of the third quarter.  -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: at  Arizona Cardinals  (Aug. 22, 10 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Seahawks:  Safeties Bud Clark (three tackles) and Rodney Thomas II (five tackles) were the only newcomers who stood out, but not necessarily for plays they did or didn't make. That both were still playing well into the second half looks like further indication of where each stands on the depth chart. Clark, Seattle's second-round pick, does not appear close to wrestling away the starting job from Ty Okada , who got the night off along with virtually every other starter. The one-year deal Seattle gave Thomas, which included only $187,500 guaranteed, suggested the former Colts starter would likely be fighting for a roster spot. That still appears to be the case.

 Running back Jadarian Price did not play as Seattle's first-round pick continues to work his way back from what coach Mike Macdonald has described as lower-body soreness that should not keep him out long.  -- Brady Henderson 

 Next game: at  Tennessee Titans  (Aug. 23, 8 p.m. ET, Fox)

 

 Ravens 24, Eagles 7 
 

 Ravens:  There was a familiar sight in the preseason opener: wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane in the end zone. With great effort after the catch, the rookie third-round pick dived across the goal line to score on a 16-yard touchdown in the second quarter. Lane finished with 38 yards on three catches, with the star of the Ravens' training camp shining brightly in the preseason.

 Tight end Matthew Hibner (fourth round) stretched the field on his first reception, catching a 29-yard pass on a wheel route. Hibner, who is looking to become the No. 3 tight end, led Baltimore with 61 yards receiving on five catches. Wide receiver Elijah Sarratt (fourth round), who has had struggles in training camp, fumbled in the third quarter. Running back Adam Randall (fifth round) scored on a 4-yard run in the fourth quarter but didn't run decisively. He finished with 46 yards on 12 carries (a 3.8-yard average).  -- Jamison Hensley 

 Next game: at  Minnesota Vikings  (Aug. 22, 1 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 

 Eagles:  The best rookie on the field for the Eagles was tackle Markel Bell , as has been the case all summer. The 6-foot-9, 346-pound third-round pick out of Miami got the start at right tackle and showed the power and poise (he drove a defensive lineman back 6 yards on one run play) that have fueled the organization's increasing confidence in him. With Lane Johnson coming off an injury-riddled season and likely entering his last NFL campaign, Bell's emergence appears right on time.

 Quarterback Cole Payton , the fifth-round pick out of North Dakota State, got the offense rolling late, using his legs to get into striking distance before throwing a TD pass to Erik Ezukanma .

 Philadelphia will need more patience when it comes to edge rusher Joshua Weru and defensive tackle Uar Bernard , who are products of the NFL's International Player Program. Both made their pro debuts and held their own, all things considered. Weru even registered a QB pressure and a tackle.  -- Tim McManus 

 Next game: at  New England Patriots  (Aug. 22, 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Jaguars 24, Saints 20 
 

 Jaguars:  Rookie running back J'Mari Taylor got rolling in the second half. After 20 yards on seven carries in the first half, the undrafted player out of Virginia gained 58 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the final two quarters. The top three backs are set and the Jags are unlikely to keep four on the active roster, but Taylor made a solid push for a practice squad spot.

 Two rookie third-round draft picks -- defensive tackle Albert Regis and safety Jalen Huskey  -- showed up the most on defense. Regis plugged up the middle and recorded a sack for a 14-yard loss. Huskey had a pass breakup and three solo tackles. He also had one of those hustle plays that coaches love: He chased down Saints kick returner Ty Chandler inside the 10-yard line after an 86-yard return on the opening kickoff, saving a touchdown. The Saints scored on the next play, but it's something that will stand out on film.

 Rookie receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron combined for three catches for 45 yards. Cameron also added a 25-yard kickoff return.  -- Michael DiRocco 

 Next game: vs.  Carolina Panthers  (Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Saints:  Several drafted rookies didn't play in this game, including receivers  Jordyn Tyson and Bryce Lance , and defensive tackle  Christen Miller left at halftime with an unspecified injury. Rookie wideout Barion Brown continued to be a camp standout and had a highlight-reel 28-yard catch down the sideline from Zach Wilson . Tight end Oscar Delp caught a 1-yard touchdown pass, and  Jeremiah Wright saw significant time as the starting right guard with Cesar Ruiz and the rest of the starters sitting out the game. Undrafted rookie edge rusher Michael Heldman also put together a nice game after having several key moments in practices.  -- Katherine Terrell 

 Next game: at  Los Angeles Rams  (Aug. 22, 4 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Rams 20, Chiefs 12 

 

 Rams:  All eyes were on rookie quarterback Ty Simpson , the Rams' first-round pick, as he faced a live pass rush for the first time in his NFL career. Heading into the game, Los Angeles coach Sean McVay said he wanted to see Simpson "consistently making good decisions" and "playing within the timing and rhythm" of the plays called. Simpson certainly checked those boxes Saturday, completing 21 of 25 passes for 190 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions.  -- Sarah Barshop 

 Next game: vs.  New Orleans Saints  (Aug. 22, 4 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 

 Chiefs:  Several Chiefs rookies had quality moments Saturday. Edge rusher R Mason Thomas displayed his burst off the edge, finishing with a pressure that led to a third-down stop inside the red zone, two tackles, a quarterback hit and a pass deflection. On offense, running back Emmett Johnson and receiver Cyrus Allen produced multiple highlights. Johnson ran around and through many tackles to lead the Chiefs with 59 rushing yards. He also reached the end zone, but his 4-yard touchdown was nullified by a holding penalty.…

title: Could Ryan Flournoy give Cowboys a third 1,000-yard receiver?
summary: Ryan Flournoy's "confidence is up" after securing the No. 3 role behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- Preseason games like Saturday's against the Seattle Seahawks  ( 8 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) meant everything to Ryan Flournoy in his first two seasons with the Dallas Cowboys .

 A sixth-round pick in 2024, Flournoy was guaranteed only an opportunity, not a job. He did enough to tease his talent -- like the two touchdown catches he had in his rookie preseason -- to stay around.

 

 While he could slip into the training camp fields in anonymity those years, things have changed for Flournoy. On the Cowboys' wide receiver hierarchy there was CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Jalen Tolbert , KaVontae Turpin and maybe Jonathan Mingo ahead of him on whatever depth chart may have been available.

 This summer, he has a guaranteed spot and role. He likely will not even be asked to play against the Seahawks.

 He secured the No. 3 role behind Lamb and Pickens last season, finishing with 40 catches for 475 yards and four touchdowns. In Week 5 last season, he caught six passes for 114 yards against the New York Jets with Lamb on the sideline with a high ankle sprain. He had his second 100-yard game later against the Detroit Lions (nine catches for 115 yards and a touchdown).

 "I'm in a different spot," Flournoy said. "I want to say last year I was wide receiver six or something like that. Now coming in as wide receiver three, my confidence is up. I know what to expect. I know what to do. Definitely just having fun, playing comfortable."

 

 In a way, the Cowboys got lucky with Flournoy when they waived the wide receiver last August, as they worked their final moves on the 53-man roster. Even though coach Brian Schottenheimer told him they wanted him back on the practice squad if he cleared waivers, Flournoy did not know what his future held.

 There was a chance he could go anywhere.

 "That was the only scary part, [like] the Eagles or something," he said, shaking his head like a child asked to eat vegetables.

 As he awaited his fate, Flournoy went to a local football field and ran routes. He guessed at what might be coming for that week's practice for the Cowboys because he didn't want to be behind if he went unclaimed.

 "It's a gamble with all these decisions that we make and all the roster gamesmanship that we all play," Schottenheimer said, "but I certainly like the outcome."

 

 This August, Flournoy is an integral part of the Cowboys' offense and fans now yell out his name from the stands in Oxnard, California. Quarterback  Dak Prescott looks his way with full trust and confidence.

 The Cowboys know what type of productivity they will get from Lamb, who has five straight 1,000-yard seasons, and Pickens, who had career highs in catches (93), yards (1,429) and touchdowns (nine) last season.

 The ascension of Flournoy makes a dangerous offense more dangerous.

 "He is a guy," Lamb said. "And the way he's developed in his last, I want to say seven, eight months, if you will, or really just later on in the season, you can see him really emerge and start filling himself. Again, confidence is the main thing about this league, especially at the receiver position, because you never know when your [opportunity] is going to come. But when it does, you want to cherish it and take advantage. So I feel like he did a great job then."

 Said Pickens, "Detail guy. That's what I mean by detail can put you at a high standard. When you come from the position he came from and you have high detail, you end up being where he is."

 Prescott's belief in Flournoy goes deeper than just what happened at The Star or in training camp. Whenever the quarterback sent out the text message that he wanted to have a throwing session, Flournoy was there.

 "Always asking questions, always just doing the right thing," Prescott said. "He's a guy that you want on your team. He's a guy that you want on your team no matter what game you're playing. His belief in himself, I think that's where it starts. And the moment he's gotten his opportunity, he's never looked back. And not only never looked back, he's looking to get more opportunities, to get more responsibility, to do more for the team."

 Flournoy has eyes on 1,000 yards. Five teams have had three 1,000-yard receivers in a season, the 2008 Arizona Cardinals being the most recent ( Larry Fitzgerald , Anquan Boldin , Steve Breaston ).

 

 In 2020, Lamb's rookie season, there was talk of possibly having three 1,000-yard receivers with Amari Cooper , Michael Gallup and Lamb, a first-round pick, but it never happened.

 "I wanted 1,000 yards last year," Flournoy said. "But definitely, honestly, 1,000 yards for everybody on the offense. I feel like me, GP, CeeDee, even [tight end Jake Ferguson ] can do it."

 That might be a tad much, even for an offense that wants to be GOTI -- " Greatest Offense There Is " -- but from where Flournoy came from, why not?

 Flournoy's rise is not as rapid as that of  Miles Austin , an undrafted free agent in 2006 who, in 2009, set a franchise record by catching 10 passes for 250 yards and two scores in an overtime win against the Kansas City Chiefs , which led to back-to-back Pro Bowl appearances. But they're in the same neighborhood with their matching No. 19s.

 "That was kind of the reason I picked 19," Flournoy said. "I was 80 my rookie year. Obviously Miles Austin was in 19. Amari Cooper was in 19. They got the 88 tradition , I wanted to do the 19 tradition for sure."
