title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Patriots' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 

 

 Who has been the Patriots' top performer at camp so far? 

 CB Christian Gonzalez . The question entering training camp was if he might be a hold-in due to ongoing talks on a contract extension. Instead, he was a full participant the first 13 practices and played a significant role in elevating the competition level for the entire team with his back-and-forth, fire-breathing 1-on-1 matchup with WR A.J. Brown -- which was arguably the top storyline of camp.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 How much is the rookie class ready to contribute? First-round pick Caleb Lomu ideally projects as the swing offensive tackle, second-round pick Gabe Jacas as a top backup OLB who creates havoc as a pass-rusher, and third-round pick Eli Raridon as the No. 2 tight end behind Hunter Henry . Their performance in games can solidify those roles, along with other rookie-based questions, such as whether seventh-round pick Behren Morton earns a roster spot as the No. 3 quarterback.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 15 
 Two days after Andy Borregales was 2-of-5 on field goal attempts in the preseason opener, he was put in a pressure-filled spot by coach Mike Vrabel in practice Saturday.

 Borregales had to kick through skinny goalposts that are about half the width of regulation goalposts. He aced the test, going 6-of-6 from a distance between 32 and 47 yards.

 "Obviously, the skinny posts are posed as a challenge after the game," Borregales said after the practice attended by season-ticket holders. "At the end of the day, whatever two poles are in front of me, that's my target and that's my job that I have to do.

 "I felt like I bounced back today, going back to the basics."

 After Thursday's 13-13 tie with the Colts, in which Borregales was wide left from 56, 55 and 49 yards, the second-year kicker said he planned to watch the tape and make improvements. The miss from 49 came at the end of regulation.

 What did he learn?

 "Just some technical stuff. I came out here today and fixed those little issues," he said. "I think today was a great day to build off."

 One change that also might have helped was the return of incumbent snapper Julian Ashby , who missed the last week with an ankle injury.

 More observations: 

 
 Top backup center/guard Ben Brown , who was knocked out of the preseason opener with an undisclosed lower-body injury, will miss multiple weeks throughout the preseason, according to Vrabel. 
 Another top backup center/guard, Andrew Rupcich , also didn't finish the preseason opener after appearing get rolled up on. He didn't practice Saturday. The injuries to Brown and Rupcich led the team to sign free agent interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt (Alabama) and Joe Michalski (Oklahoma State). 
 WR Romeo Doubs delivered multiple highlight-reel touchdown catches, including one in the end zone over CB Charles Woods to cap off a red zone drill. Doubs threw the football high in the air to celebrate in a rare show of emotion. 
 Starting CB Carlton Davis III returned as a full participant for the first time since leaving practice July 28 with what he said was a hamstring injury. He acknowledged after practice that he was knocking off some rust. 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez remained out of practice after appearing to injure his ankle Monday while defending Doubs in the end zone. 
 Starting OLB Dre'Mont Jones didn't finish practice for unknown reasons, so second-round pick Gabe Jacas elevated into the starting lineup opposite Elijah Ponder . 
 Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla was a guest of the team at practice. He spent time talking with WR A.J. Brown at one point. 
 

 

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Patriots' had an official ribbon-cutting ceremony for their new 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center on Wednesday, with owner Robert Kraft and coach Mike Vrabel among those sharing remarks before VP of football operations and strategy John Streicher led a behind-the-scenes tour.

 "There's not a better place to teach and prepare our players," Vrabel said.

 The facility includes a 15,000-square-foot weight room; 11,000 square feet of dining and kitchen space; a 10,500-square-foot virtual reality room; 3,700 square feet dedicated to hydrotherapy; and a state of the art draft room.

 The 160,000 square feet is more than double the amount the team previously occupied at Gillette Stadium.

 On one notable part of the tour, Streicher stopped at QB Drake Maye 's locker and explained the thought that went in to selecting the details of each locker -- which includes two separate areas to dry shoulder pads/helmets and cleats.

 Maye's locker is directly next to WR A.J. Brown 's, and across from CB Christian Gonzalez 's, with whom he has regularly engaged in back-and-forth locker room banter in recent years.

 

 More: 

 
 The Patriots waived undrafted rookie RB Myles Montgomery with an injury designation Wednesday and signed RB Hassan Haskins , a 2022 fourth-round draft pick of the Titans. The Patriots host the Colts in the preseason opener Thursday, and with top-of-the-depth-chart RBs Rhamondre Stevenson , TreVeyon Henderson and Terrell Jennings not expected to play, Haskins could get carries right away after Lan Larison and rookie Jam Miller . 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Drake Maye isn't expected to play in Thursday's preseason opener against the Colts, coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday.

 "That's where my mindset is right now, standing here today," Vrabel said before Tuesday's joint practice with the Colts in Foxborough. "That can always change, but I wouldn't anticipate that happening right now."

 Vrabel noted that Tuesday's practice essentially takes the place of the game for Maye & Co.

 "That's really the only reason that we do these joint practices. It will be a lot of the front-line players and whoever's available [in the practice]. Some of the guys that maybe will not get as much work will get extensive work in the game on Thursday," he said.

 The plan for practice was to have the offense take 24 full-team reps, which Vrabel pointed out was more than Maye & Co. would likely see in a preseason game.

 Maye's final rep in practice wasn't to his liking, as he threw an end zone interception to Colts safety Cam Bynum on a second-down play in the two-minute drill. Otherwise, he was pleased with the Patriots' effort, energy and execution.

 "We challenged our guys to be consistent throughout the day, and I think they responded to that," Maye said.

 More observations: 

 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez missed his first practice of training camp. It might have been related to his final play of Monday's practice, when he landed hard in the end zone while defending WR Romeo Doubs . Gonzalez has also been in negotiations with the team on a contract extension. 
 With…

title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Steelers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the TEAM's top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 Steelers' Benton agrees to 4-year, $72M extension 
 Rookies Drew Allar, Will Howard 'very poised' in Steelers' preseason win 
 Steelers bring back veteran LB Roberts on one-year deal 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 
 

 Who has been the Steelers' top performer so far at camp? 
 DB  Asante Samuel Jr . He immensely benefitted from Joey Porter Jr .'s stint on the PUP list with back soreness in the midst of extension negotiations. With his increased playing time, Samuel made play after play in Latrobe, including several PBUs in two-minute drills and against wide receiver DK Metcalf .

 Samuel, whom coach Mike McCarthy said was one of his "favorite" players since arriving in Pittsburgh, was a late add last season coming off of neck surgery, and he signed a one-year, $4 million deal to stay with the Steelers in free agency. If his camp performance is any indication, Samuel's value will be significantly higher than his cost.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does this new-look defense operate under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham? While there's plenty of questions about how Aaron Rodgers and the offense will look with McCarthy, perhaps more important to the team's success this season is Graham's ability to bring a fresh perspective and scheme to the NFL's highest-paid defense. Of course Graham won't show all of his tricks in the preseason, but these games will give an early preview of the defensive communication and the quality of depth across the board.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 15 

 Keeanu Benton knew good news must be coming when his agent told him to give him a call at 10 p.m. on Friday. And that's just what the Steelers' defensive lineman got as his agent informed him that the team was giving the 2023 second-round pick a four-year, $72 million extension .

 "I was in my bed actually," Benton said Saturday afternoon after officially signing his contract. "Then my agent told me to call him and I assumed, because you're not about to tell me to call you for no reason when I'm about to go to bed."

 Benton's agent also added outside linebacker Nick Herbig to the call to share the good news. Not only do the two share the same agent, but they've been best friends since playing together at Wisconsin.

 "Me and Nick stayed up for a little bit just talking and reflecting on how far we came," Benton said, adding that he didn't sleep much after getting the news. "That seven years done went by kind of fast, but we made a lot of progress within it."

 Earlier this offseason, Benton stood in the back of the room during a news conference following Herbig's $100 million extension . Saturday, Herbig, whom the Steelers drafted in the fourth round the same year, returned the favor.

 "We've been best friends since the day we met in college," Herbig said. "That's my brother. Everything we've been through together -- and seeing him, all the trials and hardships, grinding, going through the mud together, and getting drafted together -- this journey we've been on. I can't even put it into words, man, how it feels."

 More observations: 

 
 The Steelers had a light walkthrough on Saturday with practice lasting less than an hour. 
 DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . didn't participate after sustaining undisclosed injuries earlier in training camp. McCarthy said the two would be "hard pressed" to work this week, suggesting that it's unlikely either will play against the New York Jets on Friday. If that's the case, it's also unlikely Aaron Rodgers will play because McCarthy has stressed the importance of playing certain combinations together, including WR1-WR2-QB1. 
 Chief of staff Steve Scarnecchia suffered a "medical situation" prior to Thursday's preseason game, and McCarthy said he would be out for a couple of days. 
 McCarthy said he's likely going to retain the job of throwing the challenge flag, but if he was going to designate someone else to do it, allowed for the first time this year, it would be Scarnecchia. 
 Inside linebacker Elandon Roberts was at practice Saturday wearing No. 50 after signing a one-year deal to return to the organization Wednesday. Roberts initially took No. 57 because Jamin Davis had No. 50. But after a conversation, the two switched. 
 Though Roberts is two years older than the last time he played in Pittsburgh, he said Saturday that he's still just as physical a player. "Probably the only thing that's changed, man, I got a little smarter from a football standpoint," he said. "The more years I'm in it, I'm able to get around a lot of good coaches, good defenses to be able to learn different systems and seeing different things. So that's the only thing. But from a physicality standpoint, I'm going to always be me." 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Entering his 22nd year in the NFL, quarterback Aaron Rodgers  doesn't see a real advantage to playing in preseason games.

 "It's preseason," he said after Tuesday's practice. "It's not real football. So if I do, great. If not, great.

 "... Preseason's a lot different. Teams don't run anything anymore. They just really don't. ... I think preseason football is good to see guys with the pads on, under the lights, how they react to the nerves, but it's not real regular-season football."

 Instead, Rodgers said he's anxious to see how younger quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar react to being in game-like environments for the first time.

 Coach Mike McCarthy said he'll make a decision about the quarterback rotation for Thursday in meetings on Tuesday night, but he envisions using three groups on offense. The first will play one or two series, McCarthy said, while the second will finish out the first half and the third will play the second half.

 Rodgers said if he doesn't play, he views his role as providing comic relief from the sideline.

 "I like to be on the headset and calm everybody down," Rodgers said. "Usually the first game, it's a little hectic on the headset. So I like to be the voice of reason, occasional dad joke or one-liner. Just keep everybody settled in a little bit."

 It wasn't always that way, though.

 "It was my Super Bowl, for sure," Rodgers said of playing in the preseason 20 years ago.

 "I was so locked in and dialed in, and then you get out there and you run on a field and the nerves start flooding you and you start trying to slow your breathing down just to remember what the play was that you just heard in your helmet and not have to ask him again on the sideline and say it with conviction in the huddle, and then break the huddle and try and remember what the hell's going on to play and who's got what.

 "It's a great experience the first time just to be out there and to be live."

 More observations:

title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling? 
 49ers' Ricky Pearsall has knee surgery, targets 9-month recovery 
 How the 49ers' defense looks different under Raheem Morris 
 Kyle Shanahan nears full strength, plans to coach preseason opener 
 What's next for 49ers receivers Aiyuk, Deebo and Pearsall? 
 
 

 

 Who is the 49ers' top performer so far at camp? 
 QB Brock Purdy . There are others deserving of mention here, but this has been Purdy's best and most consistent training camp despite working with a constantly changing supporting cast. No matter who has been at running back or receiver, Purdy has found ways to move the offense in nearly every practice. He has been particularly sharp when pushing the ball downfield for big plays. If healthy, he looks poised for a big year.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where's the pass rush coming from? The Niners were last in the NFL in sacks (20) and 31st in pressures (157) in 2025. In the offseason, they traded for defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa ; they used draft picks on edge Romello Height and defensive tackle Gracen Halton . All three should help, but with defensive ends Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams not yet back from ACL surgeries, the exhibition slate will be the time for others to step forward and carve out roles.

 
 Saturday, Aug. 15 
 For the 49ers offense, there aren't many obviously available spots in the starting lineup. The exception comes at left guard where the competition is growing larger rather than narrowing as the season approaches.

 In Saturday's practice, the Niners added rookie Carver Willis to the mix after Connor Colby and Robert Jones have spent the first few weeks of camp rotating with the starting unit. Colby went first but in the next set of snaps, it was Willis working next to left tackle Trent Williams . Nobody has separated there so far and it was tough sledding blocking DT Osa Odighizuwa in this session, which means any formal decision is going to take some time.

 "Those guys are competing," Williams said. "It's a three-man race, so may the best man win, but they're all playing their butts off. Carver is the youngest and he got a little more to learn, but he has a high ceiling, a lot of potential. So just can't wait to see how he develops."

 More observations: 

 
 WR Jacob Cowing returned from his hip flexor injury and made a deep catch down the sideline in team drills. 
 CB Jack Jones was back at practice after injuring his hand early in Thursday's preseason opener. Jones recovered a fumble early in practice. 
 Still no RB Christian McCaffrey or DE Nick Bosa as they recover from some soreness and tendinitis, respectively. 
 Injured RBs Kaelon Black (adductor) and Jordan James (ribs) did some work on the side during the practice, the first time James has been seen since the injury early in camp. 
 QB Kurtis Rourke , who went to the hospital at halftime of Thursday's game because of a hit to the ribs and subsequent breathing problems, did not practice but was on the sideline watching and seemingly in good spirits. 
 With Dre Greenlaw only doing individual drills Saturday, rookie Jaden Dugger continued to get work with the starters at weak side linebacker. Dugger has made a strong impression on defensive coordinator Raheem Morris in the first few weeks and seems to have a good shot at a role in the defense early on. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 More than two weeks into camp, the 49ers offense was looking forward to seeing how it would fare against another team Tuesday. The answer? Quite well.

 After a slow start for the unit, QB Brock Purdy continued his strong camp by carving through the Titans secondary for much of the joint practice session, particularly in the latter half of the session. I had Purdy at 21-of-27 on the day, including multiple touchdown passes and no interceptions.

 

 His best throws came in a move in which he dropped a perfect ball between three defenders to rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling that would have gone for a long touchdown. And then, he had another layered throw over linebacker Cody Barton for a big gain to TE Jake Tonges .

 Even Purdy's toughest critic had to give it up for him after the practice.

 "Brock's a really good player, so I expect him to have good plays," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "I notice all the bad plays ... I didn't notice many bad plays today so I think he had a hell of a day."

 More observations: 

 
 There were a handful of fights early in the practice that looked like they might have ended the day early. San Francisco's defense seemed to be doing most of the early agitating. But both sides settled in and got some good work. 
 Stribling showed that his early flashes aren't limited to producing against his teammates. Regardless of which unit he was working against, he repeatedly made big plays. 
 Veteran WR Demarcus Robinson also had another big day, catching a couple of touchdowns from Purdy and continuing to make the case to be a valuable backup at multiple spots. 
 Speaking of receivers, Mike Evans was back from his quad injury, though he didn't do much beyond individual drills. 
 DE Nick Bosa is still not practicing with soreness and what Shanahan described as tendinitis. Shanahan said the tendinitis is normal for a player coming off a torn ACL; he has no concern about Bosa's long-term status. The hope is to have him at full strength for Week 1. 
 RB Christian McCaffrey watched the practice in street clothes and, like Bosa, Shanahan indicated there's no worry about the tightness McCaffrey is battling. Shanahan said he'd be more concerned if McCaffrey tried to play through it and risked making it worse. 
 Shanahan is out of the cast on his left hand and has traded it in for a black brace. He was out there for the whole session. 
 Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. was at practice and spent some time chatting with Niners GM John Lynch before the session. 
 Didn't catch who it was, but one of the officials was on the wrong end of a collision and had to be helped off the field. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 The Niners had only one new addition to their "did not practice" report Monday, but it was a big one: running back Christian McCaffrey .

 McCaffrey did not practice because of what the team called "tightness" after participating in every other practice during this training camp. After the session, offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak indicated McCaffrey isn't dealing with anything serious and the team is trying to be smart with him.

 "[He's] a little sore, but he's doing fine," Kubiak said. "Just kind of managing him as we go."

 Kubiak said the team will continue to keep an eye on McCaffrey's workload as it tries to get him to full speed against the Rams in Australia.

 "In terms of his rep load, we're right on track where we want to be," Kubiak said. "And he's a veteran player, so you got to monitor him and get him ready for the first week."

title: Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling?
summary: Stribling had a strong preseason debut after an exciting training camp. How does he transform the 49ers' depleted WR room?
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Late in Tuesday's joint practice against the Tennessee Titans , San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy dropped back, turned his eyes to the middle of the field and let it rip.

 At first blush, the ball flew directly toward a trio of Titans defenders ready to intercept it. Suddenly, Niners rookie receiver  De'Zhaun Stribling  burst through the congestion, snatched the pass in stride, and raced downfield for what would have been a long touchdown.

 While the 49ers expect Purdy to connect on such throws, the fact that he was willing to cut it loose for Stribling spoke volumes about how far the rookie has come in 11 training camp practices.

 "He's a really smart dude," Purdy said. "He gets the game of football. Sometimes guys come in, they're talented and stuff, but to understand the speed of the NFL and how defenses operate in the NFL, it can be hard for guys to sort of get with it quick. Eventually, they get there, but Strib has been a guy that has come in and has shown he understands it ... It is preseason and everything, so we'll see once we get to the season, but right now I have a lot of trust in him."

 That understanding has transformed Stribling from an intriguing Day 2 draft pick into a necessity. A brief, three-day bout with hamstring tightness aside, he has provided a lifeline to a depleted receivers room that lost  Ricky Pearsall  to a season-ending knee surgery . And in San Francisco's preseason opener against Tennessee, he led the team with seven receptions for 62 yards. He's the first rookie in the past decade with seven or more receptions in the first half of his team's first preseason game, per ESPN Research.

 "It seemed good," said coach Kyle Shanahan about Stribling's debut. "I thought he struggled a little bit on the first drive, but I think he got three drives after that. It seemed like he executed all the stuff that went to him, and I liked how his hands looked out there and played physical."

 

 Stribling's arrival in Santa Clara raised eyebrows among NFL draft pundits when he was taken at No. 33 with the 49ers' first selection of the draft after trading down twice to get out of Round 1. He ranked No. 15 at WR in ESPN's prospect rankings  but was the sixth one off the board.

 The 49ers' brass felt that Stribling's physical blueprint was something the team lacked: boundary size blended with legitimate vertical speed. At 6-foot-2 and 207 pounds, he is big enough to block defenders of all sizes in the run game and make plays over the middle of the field. His 4.36-second 40-yard dash (eighth fastest out of all receivers at the NFL combine) also allows him to take the top off the defense.

 Backup quarterback Mac Jones  borrowed a nickname from longtime MLB outfielder Shane Victorino to describe that speed.

 "I call him the 'Flyin' Hawaiian' because he's so fast," Jones said. "He has like a second gear when the ball's in the air. Some guys are really fast, but when the ball goes up and your eyes go up, you slow down, but he doesn't do that, so it's pretty impressive."

 Since Shanahan and general manager John Lynch took over in 2017, the 49ers have drafted 14 wide receivers. Of those, only Jalen Hurd and Jauan Jennings stood taller. Only Hurd, Jennings, and  Deebo Samuel Sr . weighed more than Stribling. And only  Danny Gray (4.33 seconds) ran a faster 40-yard dash in the predraft process.

 Although every team wants the biggest and fastest receivers possible, the Niners made it a point of emphasis to get one this year amid another makeover of the receivers room.

 "That's the thing when you look at receivers, usually you're going to get a guy who's maybe big and physical, but he doesn't have the speed," receivers coach Leonard Hankerson said. "... It's rare to get a guy like Strib that has everything. Big, strong, physical, and he can run."

 But physical abilities alone don't get receivers on the field early in Shanahan's system. The team has long shied away from plugging any of its young wideouts into one position, instead asking them to learn all three spots (F, X or Z) before deciding where to put them. That workload can faze some players, but coaches and teammates have said Stribling isn't bothered.

 The strong impression he left on the team was a result of the routine Stribling developed after the offseason program. Along with the studying film each day, he would say every playcall out loud or have someone recite it to him. Then, he would write it down or draw the play out so he could visualize it.

 Stribling would go through the playbook repeatedly, occasionally asking his mother or his girlfriend to quiz him or call out plays. He even joined fellow wideout Jordan Watkins for throwing sessions with Purdy and Jones in Nashville prior to training camp.

 

 Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said Stribling's football acumen was "one of the reasons why we really love him," adding that Stribling "absorbs football naturally." Although learning all three positions for that many plays could be confusing, Stribling viewed it as an advantage.

 "Playing a bunch of the spots allows me to see the full picture of the play, not just focusing on one spot," Stribling said. "If I know the whole concept, I kind of know what I have to do at either F, X or Z. I feel like I'm very confident wherever I'm at."

 The question now is where, exactly, Stribling will fit in.

 In stops at Washington State, Oklahoma State and Ole Miss, Stribling did a little bit of everything. He ran most of his 1,744 routes across three collegiate seasons from the outside (1,358), followed by 372 routes from the slot. He even ran 10 routes as an in-line tight end and four more out of the backfield.

 As it stands with the 49ers, free agent signing   Mike Evans will be the "X" receiver -- a spot Stribling might one day inherit. Pearsall was supposed to be the "Z," but his injury leaves that spot open. Hankerson indicated that, for now, Stribling projects more to the "F" -- or slot -- position that Jennings previously filled.

 Hankerson added there "may come a time and point" that Stribling could play the "Z." Of his 15 routes Thursday night, Stribling ran 10 from the slot and five from the outside.

 Regardless of where Stribling lines up, he is on track to be one of San Francisco's top receivers right away so long as he continues to pile up productive practices and performances in the last two preseason games.

 "We need to get him ready to play an NFL game, and it takes awhile for rookies to do that," Shanahan said. "That's why a lot aren't ready for Week 1 ... I think each day he's got better and better. Hopefully he doesn't have any injuries, so he can continue getting those days in for Week 1, and if he does, feel real confident about him."

title: Mets troll Jayden Daniels over LSU NIL dispute
summary: The team is the latest to poke fun at Daniels over his jersey number dispute with his alma mater, LSU.
full_text:
Jayden Daniels is getting trolled ... by the New York Mets , of all teams.

 The Washington Commanders quarterback has been embroiled in an unusual dispute with his alma mater, LSU . Daniels' spokesperson told ESPN that the quarterback took issue with the Tigers allowing cornerback DJ Pickett to wear the No. 5 jersey that Daniels donned during his Heisman-winning season in 2023. Daniels' attorney has informed LSU that it can no longer use his name, image and likeness, according to an Aug. 5 letter sent to Tigers athletic director Verge Ausberry, a copy of which was obtained by ESPN on Wednesday.

 The dispute has become fodder for internet trolling. StubHub announced it would "no longer offer tickets in groups of 5." NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series team TRICON Garage said it would not be running No. 5 at a race Friday. The account for Minor League Baseball made a joke about a postponed game resuming at 5:05 p.m. in the fifth inning. But perhaps the most notable troll came Friday night after the Mets' 4-1 win over the Washington Nationals .

 After the win, which came against the Commanders' neighbor in MLB, the Mets posted a graphic saying they "Stopped at 4 out of respect for Jayden Daniels."

 

 As of Saturday, the post had over 8,700 retweets and 108,000 likes. The Mets rank 22nd in MLB with 514 runs scored.
